body_en: Before he got a jump on the Thanksgiving holiday, by leaving the White House for his beach club in Florida, Donald Trump sat down for an interview with the New York Post, and told the outlet that he is open to pardoning Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang , if necessary.
“It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary,” the president told the rightwing tabloid owned by his supporter, Rupert Murdoch .
A day earlier, Trump took credit for convincing Nvidia’s board to reinstate Huang, a move that might have made the president a personal profit of $15m in one day, as Nvidia sticks soared.

Asked about Huang’s upcoming testimony to a US Senate banking committee hearing on export controls, Trump said that he sees no reason for the chief executive, who admitted an affair to a Chinese woman suspected of links to Chinese intelligence, to invoke his Fifth amendment right to avoid answering questions that might incriminate him.

“I don’t think he needs to take the Fifth. I think it’s an interesting story for people,” Trump told the friendly outlet. “I think I want him to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I’ve always found him to be 100% aboveboard, and you know a very smart person.”
body_zh: 在感恩节假期离开白宫前往佛罗里达州的海滩俱乐部之前，唐纳德·特朗普接受了《纽约邮报》的采访，并告诉该媒体，如果有必要，他愿意赦免英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋。
“我想，这始终是一种选择，但我认为没有必要，”总统告诉他的支持者鲁珀特·默多克(Rupert Murdoch)旗下的右翼小报。
一天前，特朗普因说服英伟达董事会恢复黄仁勋的职位而受到赞誉，随着英伟达的股价飙升，这一举动可能会让总统在一天内获得 1500 万美元的个人利润。
当被问及黄即将在美国参议院银行委员会出口管制听证会上作证时，特朗普表示，他认为这位承认与一名涉嫌与中国情报部门有联系的中国女性有染的行政长官没有理由援引第五修正案的权利来避免回答可能使他入罪的问题。
“我认为他不需要拿第五。我认为这对人们来说是一个有趣的故事，”特朗普告诉友好媒体。 “我想我希望他说实话，我的意思是，他的律师将不得不为他提供建议，但我一直发现他是 100% 光明正大的，你知道他是一个非常聪明的人。”

Salvadorian man, who was deported in March 2025 and returned to US after supreme court ruling, leaving of own volition for Spain
Kilmar Ábrego García has left the United States of his own volition, his lawyers confirmed on Tuesday, with the Department of Homeland Security confirming that he was travelling to Spain.

The Salvadorian immigrant was at the center of a months-long legal battle since he was deported to El Salvador in March 2025 by the Trump administration, in defiance of a court’s protection. He was held in Cecot, a notorious anti-terrorism mega-prison .

He was ultimately returned to the US after a decision by the supreme court three months later. Since then, Ábrego has been fighting a second deportation to a series of African countries proposed by Department of Homeland Security (DHS) officials.
The Washington Post reported earlier on Tuesday that he negotiated a deal with federal authorities to depart the US voluntarily in order to avoid being forcibly removed.

In a statement, the US senator Chris Van Hollen, who has advocated for Maryland resident Ábrego and who met with him in El Salvador last year, described him as a “free man” and referenced Ábrego’s agreement with the Trump administration.

“While the Trump Administration had been pursuing their vindictive prosecution against Kilmar and desperately trying to ship him against his will to countries known for human rights abuses, the Administration was forced to come to this agreement that respects Kilmar’s will and the due process rights guaranteed to him and to all in our nation,” Van Hollen said. “I am relieved that he will be safe, in a country of his choosing, and free – including from this Administration’s constant persecution.”

The 31-year-old has an American wife and child and has lived in Maryland for years, but he immigrated to the US illegally as a teenager. In 2019, an immigration judge ruled that he could not be deported to El Salvador because he faced danger there from a gang that had threatened his family. The judge allowed him to live and work in the US under Immigration and Customs Enforcement supervision, but he was not given residency status.

He was arrested in Baltimore in March 2025 and deported to a Salvadorian prison in what an official later called an “administrative error”. Facing public pressure and a court order, the Trump administration brought him back in June 2025, but only after securing an indictment charging him with human smuggling in Tennessee. A federal judge dismissed that case in May, finding that the justice department’s pursuit of criminal charges was designed to punish Ábrego García for challenging his deportation. The government is appealing.
The Trump administration vowed to deport him to a third country, threatening to send him to Uganda, Eswatini, Ghana and, most recently, Liberia.

“We will always admire his remarkable courage in staring down and defeating a vindictive prosecution instigated by the highest reaches of the Justice Department,” one of Ábrego García’s attorneys, Sean Hecker, said in a statement provided to the Washington Post . “He, in turn, is grateful to those who stood by him.”

基尔马·阿布雷戈·加西亚的律师周二证实，基尔马·阿夫雷戈·加西亚已自愿离开美国，国土安全部也证实他将前往西班牙。
自 2025 年 3 月特朗普政府不顾法院保护将他驱逐到萨尔瓦多以来，这位萨尔瓦多移民一直处于长达数月法律斗争的中心。他被关押在臭名昭著的反恐巨型监狱塞科特。
三个月后最高法院做出裁决后，他最终被遣返美国。从那时起，阿夫雷戈一直在反对国土安全部 (DHS) 官员提议的第二次驱逐到一系列非洲国家的提议。
《华盛顿邮报》周二早些时候报道称，他与联邦当局谈判达成协议，自愿离开美国，以避免被强行驱逐。
美国参议员克里斯·范·霍伦(Chris Van Hollen)为马里兰州居民阿夫雷戈辩护，去年在萨尔瓦多会见了他，他在一份声明中称他是“自由人”，并提到了阿夫雷戈与特朗普政府达成的协议。
范霍伦说：“虽然特朗普政府一直在对基尔马进行报复性起诉，并拼命试图违背基尔马的意愿将他送往以侵犯人权而闻名的国家，但政府被迫达成这项协议，尊重基尔马的意愿以及保障他和我们国家所有人的正当程序权利。” “我感到欣慰的是，他将在他选择的国家安全、自由——包括免受本届政府持续的迫害。”
这位31岁的男子有一名美国妻子和孩子，在马里兰州生活多年，但他十几岁时非法移民到美国。 2019年，一名移民法官裁定他不能被驱逐到萨尔瓦多，因为他在那里面临来自威胁他家人的团伙的危险。法官允许他在移民和海关执法局的监督下在美国生活和工作，但没有获得居留身份。
2025 年 3 月，他在巴尔的摩被捕，并被驱逐到萨尔瓦多监狱，一名官员后来称这是“行政错误”。面对公众压力和法院命令，特朗普政府于 2025 年 6 月将他带回，但前提是他获得了田纳西州人口走私罪的起诉书。一名联邦法官于 5 月驳回了该案，认为司法部门追究刑事指控的目的是为了惩罚阿布雷戈·加西亚 (Ábrego García) 对驱逐出境提出质疑。政府正在呼吁。
特朗普政府发誓要将他驱逐到第三国，并威胁将他送往乌干达、斯威士兰、加纳以及最近的利比里亚。
阿夫雷戈·加西亚的律师之一肖恩·赫克尔在向《华盛顿邮报》提供的一份声明中表示：“我们将永远钦佩他镇压并击败司法部最高层发起的报复性起诉的非凡勇气。” “反过来，他也感谢那些支持他的人。”

summary_zh: 作为总统，由于中期选举的惨败，莱维特的人手不够，他大肆宣扬自己的成就，并专注于白宫的虚荣工程。
body_en: One lame duck and two turkeys as Trump plays the hits at Thanksgiving ceremony | Donald Trump
Levity was in short supply as president, reeling from midterms rout, talked up his achievements – and fixated on White House vanity project
For some, it was his pardoning of the January 6 rioters or the deployment of masked ICE agents. For others, it was Elon Musk’s chainsaw or the demolition of the White House East Wing .
Donald Trump’s second term as US president has been full of moments when people exclaim: this is the last straw! But on Tuesday even he went too far.

The Thanksgiving turkey pardoning ceremony is typically an occasion for levity with dad jokes, bad puns and bipartisan spirit, a rare glimpse of presidential self-awareness and humility. In 2010 Barack Obama, reeling from Democrats’ disastrous midterm elections, quipped : “It feels pretty good to stop at least one shellacking this November.”

But Trump, still reeling from his own midterm rout, did none of these things. Perhaps he was still scarred by his humiliatingly unfunny turn at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner. It was just Trump being Trump, bragging about his heroic achievements and rhapsodising about his architectural overall of the White House.

Under a clear blue sky, guests were seated on his new circular granite helipad on the south lawn. The president offered by way of explanation: “It’ll be here for hopefully hundreds of years, and it’s supposed to land helicopters: it’s as good as you can get, but we use it for other things too. We just realised it’s locationally perfect.”

Wearing dark coat, white shirt and cream tie, the master builder welcomed guests and claimed the White House had “never looked better than it’s looked right now”. Then a delightful thought suddenly came to him. “Do you mind if I turn around and look?”

The president rotated and gazed at the north face of the White House, bedecked with seasonal wreaths. He complained: “I was criticised for fixing it up and making it look beautiful, fixing broken windows, fixing broken moldings, and it was a mess, and now it’s beautiful. Now it’s the way it should be. It is the symbol of our country and I think spending 10 minutes a day on it was very worthwhile.”
Ten minutes a day? A generous estimate from a decorator-in-chief who was once reportedly found supergluing gold appliqués to the Oval Office fireplace.

Trump proceeded to run through a guest list that included outgoing House speaker Mike Johnson, treasury secretary Scott Bessent (“central casting”), defense secretary Pete Hegseth (“who’s been fantastic”) and attorney general Todd Blanche (“Todd has been very busy”).

When he came to the farmers from West Virginia who had provided this year’s turkeys, named Freedom and Feathers, he could not resist observing: “We won West Virginia by 45 points. At least, I did when I was on the ballot. I don’t know what happened. I won it by a lot. I don’t know what the hell happened with this last election. Somebody please explain it to me.”

As in past years, the turkeys had stayed overnight at the nearby Willard Hotel. But that tradition too is coming to an end, Trump said. “I’m pleased to announce that next year we’ll be able to have a special location right over there in that rather small ballroom being built. It’s going to host a lot of people and a couple of turkeys next year.”

Ah, his favourite subject. There it was for all to see: a giant structure of concrete and steel, dwarfing construction workers in helmets, overalls and yellow vests amid a clang of hammers on pipes. Trump, the property wheeler-dealer from New York, has made clear over the past two years that this vanity project is what he really cares about.

He sounded like Emperor Palpatine or Darth Vader boasting about his new and seemingly indestructible Death Star: “It’s a ballroom military complex, and it’s going to be one of the – probably I would say it’s as strong a building, and I don’t want to go totally crazy here because I’ll be criticised by the fake news, but it’s, I would say that it is the strongest building ever built in this country.

“That’s a big statement. It is a very strong building. They say missile-proof, drone-proof, bulletproof, and everything else, and but it’s going to be also one of the most beautiful ballrooms, I think the most beautiful ballroom ever built, and it’s going to be representative likewise with our country, and you see the way it fits so nicely.”

The president then delved into a long and meandering rally-style speech along the lines of “you’ve never had it so good”. The past two years have been “amazing” and “incredible”. The stock market has gained $25tn in wealth, he claimed, only to lose $6tn because of the midterm election result.

But Trump is in a forgiving mood. He just got Jensen Huang reinstated at Nvidia despite an alleged affair with a Chinese spy. Now he placed his hand on Freedom’s back and uttered, “Congratulations” – ensuring that both it and Feathers will live out their days at Texas A+M University. Trump might be a lame duck but he still has power to pardon a turkey or two.
body_zh: 特朗普在感恩节仪式上演奏热门歌曲时，一只跛脚鸭和两只火鸡|唐纳德·特朗普
莱维特担任总统时人手不足，因中期选举惨败而大肆宣扬自己的成就，并专注于白宫的面子工程
对于一些人来说，这是他对 1 月 6 日骚乱者的赦免或部署蒙面 ICE 特工。对于其他人来说，这是埃隆·马斯克的电锯或白宫东翼的拆除。
唐纳德·特朗普的美国总统第二任期充满了人们感叹的时刻：这是最后一根稻草！但在周二，他甚至走得太远了。
感恩节火鸡赦免仪式通常是一个充满爸爸笑话、糟糕双关语和两党精神的轻松场合，这是总统自我意识和谦逊的难得一见。 2010 年，巴拉克·奥巴马 (Barack Obama) 因民主党灾难性的中期选举而感到震惊，他打趣道：“今年 11 月至少能阻止一场炮轰，感觉真好。”
但特朗普仍在为自己的中期选举惨败所困扰，他没有采取这些行动。也许他仍然对自己在白宫记者协会晚宴上的无耻而无趣的举动感到伤痕累累。特朗普就是特朗普，吹嘘他的英雄成就，并对他的白宫整体建筑赞不绝口。
在晴朗的蓝天下，客人们坐在他位于南草坪的新圆形花岗岩直升机停机坪上。总统解释道：“它有望在这里存在数百年，而且应该可以让直升机起降：它已经是你能得到的最好的了，但我们也将它用于其他用途。我们刚刚意识到它的位置非常完美。”
这位建筑大师穿着深色外套、白色衬衫和奶油色领带，欢迎客人，并声称白宫“从来没有像现在这样看起来更好”。然后他突然想到一个令人愉快的想法。 “你介意我回头看看吗？”
总统转过身，凝视着装饰着季节性花环的白宫北面。他抱怨道：“我因为把它修好、让它看起来很漂亮而受到批评，修好了破损的窗户、修好了破损的线脚，原来是一团糟，现在很漂亮。现在它应该是这样的。它是我们国家的象征，我认为每天花 10 分钟在上面是非常值得的。”
每天十分钟？据报道，一位总装饰师曾在椭圆形办公室的壁炉上用强力胶粘上金色贴花，这是他的慷慨估价。
特朗普随后列出了一份嘉宾名单，其中包括即将离任的众议院议长迈克·约翰逊、财政部长斯科特·贝森特（“核心选角”）、国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯（“他太棒了”）和司法部长托德·布兰奇（“托德一直很忙”）。
当他来到提供今年火鸡“自由”和“羽毛”的西弗吉尼亚州农民时，他忍不住说道：“我们以 45 个百分点的优势赢得了西弗吉尼亚州。至少，我在投票时是这样。我不知道发生了什么。我赢了很多。我不知道上次选举到底发生了什么。请有人向我解释一下。”
和往年一样，火鸡们在附近的威拉德酒店过夜。但特朗普表示，这一传统也即将结束。 “我很高兴地宣布，明年我们将能够在那个正在建造的相当小的宴会厅里有一个特殊的地点。明年它将容纳很多人和几只火鸡。”
啊，他最喜欢的科目。所有人都可以看到：一座巨大的混凝土和钢铁结构，在锤子敲打管道的叮当声中，戴着头盔、穿着工作服和黄色背心的建筑工人显得相形见绌。来自纽约的房地产商人特朗普在过去两年中明确表示，这个面子项目才是他真正关心的。
他听起来就像帕尔帕廷皇帝或达斯维德吹嘘他的新的、看似坚不可摧的死星：“这是一个舞厅军事综合体，它将成为——也许我会说它是一座坚固的建筑，我不想在这里完全发疯，因为我会受到假新闻的批评，但它是，我会说它是这个国家有史以来建造的最坚固的建筑。
“这是一个重要的声明。这是一栋非常坚固的建筑。他们说防导弹、防无人机、防弹等等，但它也将成为最美丽的宴会厅之一，我认为是有史以来最美丽的宴会厅，它同样会代表我们的国家，你会看到它非常适合。”
随后，总统发表了一场冗长而曲折的集会式演讲，大意是“你们从来没有过得这么好”。过去的两年是“令人惊奇的”和“难以置信的”。他声称，股市已经增加了 25 万亿美元的财富，但由于中期选举结果却损失了 6 万亿美元。
但特朗普的心情是宽容的。尽管黄仁勋涉嫌与中国间谍有染，但他刚刚让黄仁勋恢复在英伟达的职位。现在，他把手放在 Freedom 的背上，说出了“恭喜”——确保它和 Feathers 都能在德克萨斯 A+M 大学度过余生。特朗普可能是一只跛脚鸭，但他仍然有权赦免一两只火鸡。

body_en: Democrat Victoria Broderick unseats eight-term Republican incumbent in Tennessee to win election | US midterm elections 2026
Victory expands Democrats’ House majority, its largest advantage in three decades

Democrat Victoria Broderick has won Tennessee’s fourth congressional district, unseating eight-term Republican incumbent Scott DesJarlais in one of the biggest House upsets of the cycle. The victory expands Democrats’ historic House majority in the 120th Congress to 259 seats, the party’s largest advantage in three decades , and flips a seat that Donald Trump carried by more than 20 points in 2024.

Broderick, 34, a former technology and logistics professional who previously ran for Congress in 2024, told the Guardian in an interview before her race was called that she connected with constituents who had not voted in years and met Republicans concerned about affordability who appreciated the “integrity” she brought to the race.

“We’ve been neglected in this district,” she said earlier this month. “People want representatives who understand what they are going through, who understand the costs of going to the gas station or grocery store. I’m that representative.”

Tennessee’s congressional map was redrawn as part of the GOP’s mid-decade gerrymandering effort before this year’s midterm elections, and election forecasters had rated the district as “solidly Republican”. Yet Broderick prevailed by fewer than 400 votes, according to the Associated Press race call . DesJarlais, 62, who aligned himself closely with Trump during his time in office, conceded to Broderick last week after the razor-thin contest but the race was officially called on Tuesday.

“We all leave here with our heads held high, and we hope the Fourth District continues to receive the attention and care it so richly deserves,” DesJarlais wrote in a statement. “All of us hope that the new Member of Congress feels the same level of awe and gratitude for this tremendous undertaking that I felt every day I had the privilege of serving.”

DesJarlais’ stunning defeat comes despite significantly out-fundraising Broderick in the run-up to the election and with many national Democrats dismissing her campaign as a long shot. Broderick will now be the sole Democrat in Tennessee’s congressional delegation on Capitol Hill, underscoring the scale of an upset few in either party saw coming.

Broderick said that she managed to pull off the upset without support from the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, the party’s House campaign arm. “The Democratic party wasn’t paying attention to this race,” she said. “I knew I was the underdog.”

A day after the election, on 4 November, Broderick had already declared victory . “We did not have the political machine behind us. We didn’t have corporate Pac money, we didn’t have powerful insiders. We had you, the people,” she wrote on social media. “That turns out that is all we needed.”

DesJarlais, a physician, was also dogged by controversy during his time in office, particularly after it was revealed that he urged his ex-wife to have two abortions before their marriage despite his anti-abortion stance. Divorce trial transcripts also showed that he admitted to sexual relationships with patients.
body_zh: 民主党人维多利亚·布罗德里克 (Victoria Broderick) 击败田纳西州八届共和党现任议员赢得大选2026 年美国中期选举
胜利扩大了民主党在众议院的多数席位，这是其三十年来最大的优势
民主党人维多利亚·布罗德里克(Victoria Broderick)赢得了田纳西州第四个国会选区，取代了八届共和党现任议员斯科特·德贾莱斯(Scott DesJarlais)，这是众议院本周期最大的冷门之一。这场胜利将民主党在第 120 届国会的历史性众议院多数席位扩大至 259 个席位，这是该党三十年来的最大优势，并扭转了唐纳德·特朗普在 2024 年以超过 20 个百分点的优势赢得的席位。
34 岁的布罗德里克曾是一名技术和物流专业人士，曾于 2024 年竞选国会议员，她在竞选开始前接受《卫报》采访时表示，她与多年没有投票的选民建立了联系，并会见了担心负担能力的共和党人，他们赞赏她在竞选中表现出的“诚信”。
“我们在这个地区被忽视了，”她本月早些时候说道。 “人们希望代表了解他们正在经历的事情，了解去加油站或杂货店的费用。我就是那个代表。”
田纳西州的国会地图被重新绘制，作为共和党在今年中期选举前的十年中期选区划分努力的一部分，选举预测者将该选区评为“坚定的共和党”。然而，据美联社报道，布罗德里克以不到 400 票的优势获胜。 62 岁的德贾莱斯在特朗普执政期间与特朗普关系密切，上周在一场微弱的竞争后，他输给了布罗德里克，但比赛于周二正式宣布。
德贾莱斯在一份声明中写道：“我们都昂首挺胸地离开这里，我们希望第四区继续受到应有的关注和照顾。” “我们所有人都希望新任国会议员对我每天都有幸服务的这项伟大事业感到同样程度的敬畏和感激。”
尽管德贾莱斯在选举前筹款明显超过了布罗德里克，而且许多全国民主党人认为她的竞选机会渺茫，但德贾莱斯还是惨败。布罗德里克现在将成为田纳西州国会山国会代表团中唯一的民主党人，这突显了两党中少数人所预见到的不安程度。
布罗德里克表示，她在没有民主党众议院竞选部门民主党国会竞选委员会支持的情况下成功实现了这一目标。 “民主党没有关注这场竞选，”她说。 “我知道我是失败者。”
选举后的第二天，11 月 4 日，布罗德里克就已经宣布获胜。 “我们背后没有政治机器。我们没有政治行动委员会的资金，我们没有强大的内部人士。我们有你们，人民，”她在社交媒体上写道。 “事实证明这就是我们所需要的。”
德贾莱斯是一名医生，在任职期间也饱受争议，特别是在有报道称，尽管他持反堕胎立场，但他仍敦促前妻在婚前进行两次堕胎。离婚审判笔录还显示，他承认与患者发生性关系。

title_en: Trump honors Rudy Giuliani with presidential medal of freedom
title_zh: 特朗普授予鲁迪·朱利安尼总统自由勋章
summary: President’s former lawyer, disbarred over effort to overturn 2020 election result, receives top civilian honor Donald Trump awarded Rudy Giuliani, his former personal attorney who was disbarred for his efforts to help the US president overturn 2020 election re
summary_zh: 总统的前律师因试图推翻 2020 年选举结果而被取消律师资格，但获得最高平民荣誉唐纳德·特朗普授予鲁迪·朱利安尼 (Rudy Giuliani)
body_en: President’s former lawyer, disbarred over effort to overturn 2020 election result, receives top civilian honor

Donald Trump awarded Rudy Giuliani, his former personal attorney who was disbarred for his efforts to help the US president overturn 2020 election results , with the presidential medal of freedom on Tuesday.

“I am honored and humbled to receive the Presidential Medal of Freedom from my nation and from President Donald J Trump,” Giuliani, 82, wrote in an X post hours after the award had been presented to him.
“I share the credit with all the men and women who worked with me, disagreed with me, and loved me – particularly those who lost their lives in the causes we undertook together,” Giuliani added.

The presidential medal of freedom is one of the highest civilian awards in the US, typically given to individuals who contribute to world peace, the national interest of the US or significant cultural endeavors.
On Monday, Giuliani told Steve Bannon that the US president would give him the award on Tuesday, more than a year after Trump announced he would award it to him.
“I’m, of course, very, very humbled and very honored not only to receive it but to receive it from him,” Giuliani told Bannon.

On Trump’s schedule, the award presentation was “closed press”, meaning no media were present. But before the ceremony, the White House posted a compilation video of Giuliani, saying he left an “undeniable mark on American history”.
After the ceremony, Andrew Giuliani, the son of Rudy Giuliani, told reporters it was “incredibly special” to see his father receive the award from Trump.

“I think what Rudy Giuliani has done over the last six years will go down in history as one of the most important legal jobs that has ever been done by any attorney. To defend the president of the United States against some of the evil forces that are out there, I am so proud of my father,” Andrew Giuliani said.
Giuliani served as the mayor of New York during the 11 September 2001 terrorist attacks. For his leadership, he became a globally recognized figure, earning the nickname “America’s mayor”.
After serving as mayor, he ran for the Republican presidential nomination in 2008, but dropped out of the race after underperforming in early primaries.

In the decades after 9/11, Giuliani’s reputation suffered several blows , in part because of his loyalty to Trump. For promoting Trump’s false claims of election fraud, Giuliani lost his license to practice law.
He also settled a multimillion-dollar defamation suit filed by election workers Ruby Freeman and her daughter Wandrea “Shaye” Moss after he falsely accused them of election fraud.
Giuliani filed for bankruptcy in 2023 after he settled the $148m defamation suit, though a judge later dismissed the bankruptcy suit.
In 2025, Giuliani also settled a long-running, billion-dollar lawsuit filed by voting machine manufacturer Dominion Voting Systems.
Giuliani also pleaded not guilty to state charges in Georgia and Arizona stemming from efforts to overturn the 2020 election, though both cases were eventually dismissed.
“Doing the right thing for others has been my guiding light,” Giuliani wrote in his social media post on Tuesday.
Giuliani also credited his former boss, Ronald Reagan, with inspiring his career. Giuliani served as a top justice department official during Reagan’s administration.
body_zh: 总统前律师因试图推翻 2020 年选举结果而被取消律师资格，获得最高民事荣誉
周二，唐纳德·特朗普向他的前私人律师鲁迪·朱利安尼授予总统自由勋章，鲁迪·朱利安尼因帮助美国总统推翻 2020 年选举结果而被取消律师资格。
“能够从我的国家和唐纳德·J·特朗普总统手中获得总统自由勋章，我感到非常荣幸和谦卑，”82岁的朱利安尼在颁奖几小时后在 X 帖子中写道。
朱利安尼补充道：“我与所有与我共事、反对我和爱我的男女分享这份功劳，特别是那些在我们共同事业中丧生的人。”
总统自由勋章是美国最高的平民奖项之一，通常颁发给为世界和平、美国国家利益或重大文化事业做出贡献的个人。
周一，朱利安尼告诉史蒂夫·班农，美国总统将于周二颁奖给他，距离特朗普宣布将奖项授予他一年多了。
朱利安尼告诉班农：“当然，我非常非常谦卑，非常荣幸，不仅能收到它，而且能从他那里收到它。”
根据特朗普的日程安排，颁奖典礼是“闭门媒体”，这意味着没有媒体出席。但在仪式之前，白宫发布了朱利安尼的汇编视频，称他“在美国历史上留下了不可否认的印记”。
颁奖典礼结束后，鲁迪·朱利安尼的儿子安德鲁·朱利安尼告诉记者，看到他的父亲从特朗普手中获得这一奖项“非常特别”。
“我认为鲁迪·朱利安尼在过去六年中所做的事情将作为任何律师所做过的最重要的法律工作之一载入史册。为了保护美国总统免受一些邪恶势力的侵害，我为我的父亲感到自豪，”安德鲁·朱利安尼说。
朱利安尼在 2001 年 9 月 11 日恐怖袭击期间担任纽约市长。由于他的领导才能，他成为全球公认的人物，赢得了“美国市长”的绰号。
担任市长后，他于2008年竞选共和党总统提名，但因早期初选表现不佳而退出竞选。
在9/11之后的几十年里，朱利安尼的声誉遭受了数次打击，部分原因是他对特朗普的忠诚。由于宣扬特朗普选举舞弊的虚假指控，朱利安尼被吊销了律师执照。
他还和解了选举工作人员鲁比·弗里曼 (Ruby Freeman) 和她的女儿万德里亚·“沙耶”·莫斯 (Wandrea “Shaye” Moss) 在他错误地指控选举舞弊后提起的数百万美元的诽谤诉讼。
朱利安尼在解决了价值 1.48 亿美元的诽谤诉讼后于 2023 年申请破产，但法官后来驳回了破产诉讼。
2025 年，朱利安尼还和解了投票机制造商 Dominion Voting Systems 提起的一项旷日持久、价值数十亿美元的诉讼。
朱利安尼还对佐治亚州和亚利桑那州因推翻 2020 年选举而提出的州指控表示无罪，不过这两起案件最终都被驳回。
“为他人做正确的事一直是我的指路明灯，”朱利安尼周二在社交媒体帖子中写道。
朱利安尼还称赞他的前任老板罗纳德·里根激励了他的职业生涯。朱利安尼在里根执政期间担任司法部高级官员。

title_en: Al Gore buys local, family-owned newspaper in central Tennessee
title_zh: 阿尔·戈尔 (Al Gore) 收购田纳西州中部当地的家族报纸
summary: Former vice-president, who started his career as a journalist, purchases Carthage Courier in Smith county Al Gore, who started his career as a journalist, is returning to the industry as a newspaper owner in his Tennessee town. The Lake family, which has opera
summary_zh: 前副总统的职业生涯始于记者，他在史密斯县购买了《迦太基信使》 阿尔·戈尔 (Al Gore) 的职业生涯始于期刊
body_en: Former vice-president, who started his career as a journalist, purchases Carthage Courier in Smith county
Al Gore, who started his career as a journalist, is returning to the industry as a newspaper owner in his Tennessee town.

The Lake family, which has operated the Carthage Courier for five decades, said Tuesday it will sell the paper to the former vice-president in the coming weeks. The weekly paper serves Smith county in central Tennessee, which has roughly 20,000 residents and sits about 55 miles (88km) east of Nashville.

As the beleaguered news industry struggles with newspaper closures and growing news deserts, Gore characterized the purchase as a move that preserves an independent local voice in Carthage and Smith county.

“Having spent my early years as a military reporter in Vietnam and later at the [Nashville] Tennessean, I am a firm believer that a free, independent local press is irreplaceable for the enduring health of our community,” Gore said in a statement.

Terms of the sale weren’t disclosed, and it wasn’t clear how involved Gore, 78, will be in the paper’s operations. His office and the outlet wouldn’t answer questions Tuesday or provide additional details.
The Courier’s announcement omitted Gore’s political résumé, presenting him simply as a local man buying his small town’s paper to keep it locally owned.

Before entering politics, Gore spent six months as a military reporter in the US Army during the Vietnam war. He returned to Tennessee and worked for a few years as an investigative reporter at the Tennessean before running for Congress in 1976.

Gore, a Democrat, represented Tennessee in both chambers of Congress, served as Bill Clinton’s vice-president from 1993 to 2001, and ran for president twice. After losing the 2000 presidential election to George W Bush, he went on to win the Nobel peace prize for his climate activism and an Academy award for the documentary An Inconvenient Truth.
The Courier’s website notes that it covered the early political pursuits of Gore’s father, Albert Gore Sr, who represented the state in the US House and Senate.

Tim Franklin, chair of local news at Northwestern University’s Medill School of Journalism, Media, Integrated Marketing Communications, said Carthage residents may have “some healthy skepticism” about a politician owning the paper.
“But I would be surprised if the Carthage Courier becomes a mouthpiece for the Democratic party,” he said.

Gore is far from the first politician to purchase or own a newspaper. Throughout the 1900s, several senators, governors and even a US president, Warren Harding, had local papers in their business portfolios.

More recently, consumer advocate Ralph Nader, one of Gore’s former political rivals, helped launch a local newspaper in Winsted, Connecticut, in 2023 that was purchased months later by a national media company.
body_zh: 前副总统以记者身份开始职业生涯，在史密斯县购买了 Carthage Courier
阿尔·戈尔 (Al Gore) 的职业生涯始于记者，现在他将重返这个行业，成为田纳西州小镇的一名报纸老板。
经营《迦太基信使报》已有五十年历史的莱克家族周二表示，将在未来几周内将该报出售给前副总统。该周报为田纳西州中部的史密斯县提供服务，该县约有 20,000 名居民，位于纳什维尔以东约 55 英里（88 公里）处。
由于陷入困境的新闻业正面临着报纸关闭和日益严重的新闻荒漠的困境，戈尔将此次收购描述为保留迦太基和史密斯县当地独立声音的举措。
戈尔在一份声明中说：“我早年在越南担任军事记者，后来在田纳西州[纳什维尔]担任记者，我坚信自由、独立的当地媒体对于我们社区的持久健康是不可替代的。”
出售条款并未披露，也不清楚 78 岁的戈尔将如何参与该报的运营。他的办公室和媒体周二没有回答问题或提供更多细节。
《信使报》的声明省略了戈尔的政治简历，将他简单地描述为一个当地人购买他小镇的报纸以保持其本地所有权。
在进入政坛之前，戈尔在越南战争期间在美国陆军担任了六个月的军事记者。他回到田纳西州，在《田纳西州报》担任了几年调查记者，然后于 1976 年竞选国会议员。
戈尔是民主党人，代表田纳西州参众两院，1993年至2001年担任比尔·克林顿的副总统，并两次竞选总统。在 2000 年总统选举中输给乔治·W·布什后，他因其气候行动主义而获得诺贝尔和平奖，并凭借纪录片《难以忽视的真相》获得奥斯卡金像奖。
《信使报》网站指出，它报道了戈尔父亲老阿尔伯特·戈尔的早期政治追求，他在美国众议院和参议院代表该州。
西北大学梅迪尔新闻、媒体、整合营销传播学院当地新闻系主任蒂姆·富兰克林表示，迦太基居民可能对拥有该报纸的政客抱有“一些合理的怀疑”。
“但如果《迦太基信使》成为民主党的喉舌，我会感到惊讶，”他说。
戈尔并不是第一个购买或拥有报纸的政治家。整个 1900 年代，几位参议员、州长，甚至美国总统沃伦·哈丁 (Warren Harding) 的商业投资组合中都有当地报纸。
最近，戈尔的前政治对手之一、消费者权益倡导者拉尔夫·纳德 (Ralph Nader) 于 2023 年帮助在康涅狄格州温斯特德创办了一家当地报纸，几个月后该报纸被一家全国性媒体公司收购。

title_en: Trump says pardon is always an option for Jensen Huang, and that invoking the Fifth isn’t necessary
title_zh: 特朗普表示赦免黄仁勋始终是一个选择，并且没有必要援引第五条
summary: The president’s assertion that Huang does not pose a national security threat has sparked bipartisan backlash on Capitol Hill, where the Nvidia CEO is set to testify next week.
summary_zh: 总统关于黄仁勋不会构成国家安全威胁的断言在国会山引发了两党的强烈反对，这位英伟达首席执行官所在的国会山
body_en: Trump says pardon is always an option for Huang, invoking the Fifth isn’t necessary
President Donald Trump said that while pardoning Jensen Huang for any potential criminal activity remains an option, he doesn’t think that will be needed for the newly reinstated Nvidia CEO .
“It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary,” Trump told the New York Post in an interview published Tuesday night.
Asked about Huang’s scheduled appearances next week on Capitol Hill, Trump said, “I don’t think he needs to take the Fifth. I think it’s an interesting story for people.”

“I think I want him to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I’ve always found him to be 100% aboveboard, and you know a very smart person,” the president said.
A representative for Huang declined to comment on Trump’s comments. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for further comment.
Speaking at a news conference Tuesday, Attorney General Todd Blanche indicated he would have told Trump if Huang had been involved in any criminal activity.

“To the extent that, that the department, that the Department of Justice had information that he was committing crimes or something like this, that is, that is, that’s just not, that’s something that I would have certainly told the president had it been true,” Blanche said.
Blanche assures he would have told Trump about any crimes Jensen Huang committed
In Congress, lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are preparing to grill Huang over their national security concerns.

A spokesperson for the Republican-led House Intelligence Committee told NBC News that Huang’s reinstatement “changes nothing” and that there “are serious questions on national security implications that still need answers.”

Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter are expected to sit for transcribed interviews next Tuesday and Wednesday before the House Select Committee on China, the House Intelligence Committee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

Huang, who has not been charged with a crime, resigned from his post as CEO of the chip giant following reports that he had a relationship with a woman who U.S. intelligence agencies believed was a Chinese spy. In a Nov. 8 memo to Nvidia’s staff, he said, “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Trump worked behind the scenes over the weekend to get Nvidia’s board to bring Huang back. That move has been met with bipartisan backlash.
Sen. Pete Ricketts, R-Neb., on Monday raised concerns over Nvidia’s quick reversal to rehire Huang after indicating it wouldn’t.
“His own board described his behavior as lacking ‘candor.’ I’ve served on a public company board. His behavior does not support reinstatement,” Ricketts wrote in a post on X.
Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., wrote that with Nvidia’s rehiring of Huang, “the national security risk is passed along to the United States military and its citizens.”
Cramer and Ricketts are both members of the Senate Banking Committee, where Huang is scheduled to testify in public Dec. 3.
In celebrating Huang’s return, Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social post that the U.S. government “has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.”

Similarly, Nvidia’s board said it reached the decision to reinstate Huang after receiving “input from senior levels of the United States government” that his “reinstatement poses no national security risk.”
body_zh: 特朗普表示赦免黄始终是一个选择，没有必要援引第五条
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，虽然赦免黄仁勋任何潜在的犯罪活动仍然是一种选择，但他认为新复职的英伟达首席执行官不需要这样做。
“我想，这始终是一种选择，但我认为没有必要，”特朗普在周二晚间发表的采访中告诉《纽约邮报》。
当被问及黄计划于下周在国会山露面时，特朗普说：“我认为他不需要参加第五届国会。我认为这对人们来说是一个有趣的故事。”
“我想我希望他说实话，我的意思是，他的律师将不得不为他提供建议，但我一直发现他是100%光明正大的，你知道他是一个非常聪明的人，”总统说。
黄的代表拒绝对特朗普的言论发表评论。白宫没有立即回应进一步置评的请求。
司法部长托德·布兰奇在周二的新闻发布会上表示，如果黄参与任何犯罪活动，他会告诉特朗普。
布兰奇说：“如果该部门、司法部掌握了他正在犯罪或类似情况的信息，那么事实并非如此，如果这是真的，我肯定会告诉总统。”
布兰奇保证他会告诉特朗普黄仁勋犯下的任何罪行
在国会，两党议员都准备就国家安全问题质问黄。
共和党领导的众议院情报委员会的一位发言人告诉 NBC 新闻，黄的复职“没有改变任何事情”，并且“对国家安全影响存在严重问题，仍然需要答案”。
黄仁勋和英伟达总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特预计将于下周二和周三在众议院中国特别委员会、众议院情报委员会和众议院外交事务委员会接受采访记录。
尚未受到犯罪指控的黄仁勋辞去了这家芯片巨头首席执行官的职务，此前有报道称，黄仁勋与一名美国情报机构认为是中国间谍的女性发生了关系。在 11 月 8 日发给 Nvidia 员工的备忘录中，他说：“我对我的妻子不忠。我的行为伤害了她和我们的孩子。我的所作所为没有任何借口。我深感抱歉。”
特朗普周末在幕后努力让英伟达董事会让黄回来。此举遭到了两党的强烈反对。
内布拉斯加州共和党参议员皮特·里基茨 (Pete Ricketts) 周一对英伟达在表示不会重新聘用黄仁勋后迅速逆转表示担忧。
“他自己的董事会形容他的行为缺乏‘坦诚’。我曾在一家上市公司董事会任职。他的行为不支持复职，”里基茨在 X 上的一篇帖子中写道。
北达科他州参议员凯文·克莱默 (Kevin Cramer) 写道，随着英伟达重新聘用黄仁勋，“国家安全风险被转嫁给了美国军方及其公民。”
克莱默和里基茨都是参议院银行委员会的成员，黄计划于 12 月 3 日公开作证。
为了庆祝黄仁勋的回归，特朗普在 Truth Social 帖子中写道，美国政府“没有理由相信 Jensen 回归 NVIDIA 对国家安全构成任何风险”。
同样，英伟达董事会表示，在收到“美国政府高层的意见”后，做出了让黄先生复职的决定，认为黄先生的“复职不会构成国家安全风险”。

body_en: Rescue crews search for six people after plane crash off Mississippi coast | Mississippi
US Coast Guard said crews had so far found the cabin of the plane, a life raft and three life jackets
Rescue crews were searching for six people on board a small plane that crashed Tuesday afternoon off the coast of Mississippi .
Crews have so far found three life jackets, a life raft and the cabin of the plane. The plane’s cabin was floating on the water, Juan Ros, a US Coast Guard spokesperson, said.

The plane, a Cessna 210, went down around 3.30pm in the Gulf of Mexico between Pascagoula, Mississippi, and Horn Island, which is part of the Gulf Islands national seashore. There were four adults and two boys, ages eight and 10, on board, authorities said.
The Cessna was en route from New Orleans to Fort Meyers, Florida, according to the flight tracking website FlightAware.
According to the Coast Guard, the plane was descending at a rate of 10,000ft per minute when contact was lost.
The Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transportation Safety Board, which will investigate the crash, said on Tuesday they were aware of it.

据航班跟踪网站 FlightAware 称，这架塞斯纳飞机当时正在从新奥尔良飞往佛罗里达州迈尔斯堡的途中。

title_en: Trump takes credit for Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia, says its good for the economy
title_zh: 特朗普将黄仁勋重返英伟达归功于他，称这对经济有利
summary: President Trump touted the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia's C-suite as good for the company -- and good for the United States economy.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统称赞黄仁勋重返英伟达高管，这对公司有利，对美国经济也有利。
body_en: Trump takes credit for Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia, says its good for the economy President Trump touted the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia's C-suite as good for the company -- and good for the United States economy.
President Trump touted the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia's C-suite as good for the company — and good for the United States economy.
Jensen Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia less than two weeks after resigning, a return that President Trump helped engineer and is now celebrating.

Huang and the president have been allies. His company donated to the new White House ballroom. Huang also routinely advised the president on AI policy. He will surely face questions about that relationship and much more when he attends a closed-door interview that three House committees have planned for next week. In a moment, we bring in Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi, who's on two of those panels. We begin with the news.
MARTIN: White House correspondent Danielle Kurtzleben has been covering this. Good morning.
MARTIN: So what has the president had to say about his role in all of this Nvidia situation?

KURTZLEBEN: Well, shortly after the announcement of the reinstatement, the president posted that this was for the good not only of Nvidia, but the U.S. economy. And then yesterday morning, he did a 50-minute phone interview with CNBC. And Trump was asked if he directly called into the Nvidia board meeting, and he demurred, but he did make it clear that he pushed the company on this decision. He said he convinced them - his words. He went on to say that he was able to convince Nvidia because the company's stock had plummeted following Huang's ouster, and that was again after the news initially broke that Huang was having an affair with an alleged spy for China.

MARTIN: Now, let me just pause here because I'm not sure that - perhaps if people don't cover the business world, etc., they might not know that it is very extraordinary for a White House to weigh in on private business decisions.

KURTZLEBEN: Yeah. It's a huge deal. Even if it's not really unusual for this White House to intervene in the economy and even private businesses, this White House has taken stakes in dozens of companies, for example. Plus, Trump has gotten very cozy with the tech world, with CEOs showing up to White House events or donating to his ballroom. But beyond all that, it really stood out to me this thing that Trump did yesterday - he posted this meme playing off that famous picture of him after he was shot in Butler, Pennsylvania. In this new picture, it's Huang, not Trump, raising his fist with blood spattered on his face. And in that fist is a red bra, referencing, of course, Huang's affair. Now, this is the president of the United States posting this, and it's trolling. And also it's once again celebrating a private business decision.
MARTIN: Extraordinary. That image is extraordinary. But why was the president so dead set on getting Huang back into his CEO role?

KURTZLEBEN: Well, Trump told CNBC he was concerned that Chinese president Xi Jinping might lure Huang over to China to boost their chip business. But also let's remember Trump loves to talk about the stock market. Even when other economic measures aren't looking great, he often has stock indexes to talk about. So he told CNBC the Huang decision not only turned Nvidia's stock around, but maybe the whole market after what was a rough week for stocks.

PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: I watched the screen, and I said, boy, that thing's like a rocket ship going in the wrong direction. Now it's a rocket ship going in the right direction, and it's taken the whole market with it.
UNIDENTIFIED PERSON: It's just an incredible turnaround.
UNIDENTIFIED PERSON: You've been watching corporate America...
TRUMP: There could be - it could be that there's never been anything like it, actually.

KURTZLEBEN: One other important point here - the president has been trading in Nvidia stock, as we know from his financial disclosures. In early September, there was a purchase he made worth up to a quarter of a million dollars. And this is also part of a pattern of trading in companies by the president that also are affected by his administration's actions.
MARTIN: OK. The national security issues. What is the status of that? It strikes me that those issues have not been resolved. Have they?
body_zh: 特朗普将黄仁勋重返英伟达视为功劳，称这对经济有利 特朗普总统称赞黄仁勋重返英伟达高管对公司有利，对美国经济也有利。
特朗普总统称赞黄仁勋重返英伟达高管，这对公司有利，对美国经济也有利。
黄仁勋在辞职不到两周后重新担任英伟达首席执行官，这是特朗普总统帮助策划的回归，现在正在庆祝。
黄和总统一直是盟友。他的公司向新的白宫宴会厅捐款。黄还经常就人工智能政策向总统提供建议。当他参加众议院三个委员会计划下周举行的闭门采访时，他肯定会面临有关这种关系以及更多问题的问题。一会儿，我们请来代表 Raja Krishnamoorthi，他是其中两个小组的成员。我们从新闻开始。
马丁：白宫记者丹妮尔·库茨莱本一直在报道此事。早上好。
马丁：那么对于他在 Nvidia 的所有事件中所扮演的角色，总统有什么想说的？

KURTZLEBEN：嗯，在宣布恢复后不久，总统表示这不仅有利于 Nvidia，也有利于美国经济。昨天早上，他接受了 CNBC 50 分钟的电话采访。当特朗普被问到他是否直接参加英伟达董事会会议时，他表示反对，但他确实明确表示，他推动该公司做出了这一决定。他说他说服了他们——他的话。他接着说，他之所以能够说服英伟达，是因为在黄仁勋被罢黜后，该公司的股价暴跌，而这又是在黄仁勋与一名所谓的中国间谍有染的消息最初传出之后。
马丁：现在，让我在这里暂停一下，因为我不确定 - 也许如果人们不报道商业世界等，他们可能不知道白宫参与私人商业决策是非常不寻常的。

库兹莱本：是的。这是一件大事。即使本届白宫干预经济甚至私营企业并不罕见，但例如，本届白宫已经入股了数十家公司。此外，特朗普与科技界变得非常融洽，首席执行官们出席白宫活动或向他的舞厅捐款。但除此之外，特朗普昨天做的这件事对我来说真的很突出——他发布了这个表情包，模仿了他在宾夕法尼亚州巴特勒被枪杀后的那张著名照片。在这张新照片中，是黄，而不是特朗普，举起了拳头，脸上溅满了血。拳头里有一个红色胸罩，当然是指黄的外遇。现在，这是美国总统发布的，这是恶搞。它还再次庆祝私营企业的决定。
马丁：非凡。那画面非同寻常。但为什么总统如此执意要让黄重新担任首席执行官一职呢？
KURTZLEBEN：嗯，特朗普告诉 CNBC，他担心中国国家主席习近平可能会引诱黄仁勋到中国来发展他们的芯片业务。但我们也要记住，特朗普喜欢谈论股市。即使其他经济指标看起来不太好，他也经常谈论股票指数。因此，他告诉 CNBC，黄仁勋的决定不仅扭转了英伟达股票的走势，而且可能扭转了整个市场在股市经历了艰难的一周后的走势。
唐纳德·特朗普总统：我看着屏幕，我说，天哪，那件事就像一艘朝错误方向行驶的火箭飞船。现在，它就像一艘火箭，正朝着正确的方向前进，并带动了整个市场。
身份不明的人：这真是一个令人难以置信的转变。
身份不明的人：您一直在关注美国企业界……
特朗普：可能有——实际上可能从来没有发生过这样的事情。
KURTZLEBEN：另一个重要的一点是，总统一直在交易 Nvidia 股票，正如我们从他的财务披露中了解到的那样。 9月初，他购买了一笔价值高达25万美元的商品。这也是总统公司交易模式的一部分，这些公司也受到其政府行为的影响。
马丁：好的。国家安全问题。其状态如何？令我震惊的是，这些问题还没有得到解决。他们有吗？
