title_en: Democrats probe whether Trump Jr.-aligned businesses benefit from government access
title_zh: 民主党人调查小特朗普的企业是否受益于政府准入
summary: Investigators say companies with ties to Donald Trump Jr's investment firm, 1789 Capital, have profited since his father's reelection.
summary_zh: 调查人员表示，自小唐纳德·特朗普的父亲连任以来，与他的投资公司 1789 Capital 有联系的公司已经获利。
body_en: Donald Trump Jr. speaks on stage on the second day of the 2026 Republican National Convention on Sept. 10, in Dallas. Brandon Bell/Getty Images hide caption

Congressional Democrats, led by likely House Judiciary Committee Chair Rep. Jamie Raskin of Maryland, are expanding their investigation into the investment firm 1789 Capital, which brought on Donald Trump Jr. as a partner days after his father's reelection to the White House.

Since then, investigators say the firm has grown from "a middling venture capital firm" with $150 million in managed assets to "the darling of the venture capital world" with $3 billion in managed assets.

Investigators want to determine whether the growth was boosted by the president's son leveraging political influence or government information to secure federal contracts and regulatory changes for companies with connections to the investment firm.
House Democrat warns 13 Trump allies to save their records for upcoming investigations

Trump Jr. told Axios last week that the timing of his hiring at 1789 Capital was coincidental, noting that he had already been working with founder Omeed Malik for years. He also said he draws a clear line when marketing and raising money for the firm.

"I make it very clear [to foreign investors] that I have nothing to do with government," Trump Jr. said. "[The president is] my father, but he's also busy and I probably haven't spoken to him in three weeks."

He also suggested he doesn't use or need government connections to make smart investments. "Trying to do the things that we're alleged to be doing every day, I think that would last for about two seconds before it was out there very publicly," Trump Jr. said. He added that the firm relies on teams of analysts to make investments in industries where there are obvious public and national security demands but relatively few companies who are able to meet those needs.
NPR reached out to Donald Trump Jr. for comment and did not hear back.

Regarding Raskin's request for documents from 1789 Capital, Bill Burck, an attorney representing the firm, told NPR, "We responded to Congressman Raskin back in September pointing out in detail the many flaws in his understanding of how 1789 has operated and a number of basic factual errors. He never bothered to reply. Facts are facts and Congressman Raskin has them wrong here but persists in his tall tales against 1789. These are personal attacks untethered to actual evidence."

On Monday, congressional investigators sent letters to four companies — military contractor Hadrian, electronic cigarette company Juul, prediction market Polymarket and online weapons dealer GrabAGun — asking them to preserve their records and turn over a broad array of records to the committee.

The committee is interested in Hadrian's contracts with the armed forces, signed in March of this year, worth close to a billion dollars. Investigators allege that, in 2024, the company had a single manufacturing facility and "no history of fulfilling government contracts." They also noted that CEO Chris Power donated tens of thousands of dollars to Trump-aligned political organizations in advance of the 2024 election.

Political donations are constitutionally-protected speech and not necessarily evidence of wrongdoing. 1789 Capital first invested in Hadrian in July 2025. The company is also backed by a number of bluechip investors, including Morgan Stanley, T. Rowe Price, Andreessen Horowitz and JPMorganChase. Hadrian did not reply to a request for comment from NPR.

Investigators also allege that Trump Jr.'s firm took a stake in e-cigarette company Juul in March 2025, as the company teetered near insolvency following rulings during the first Trump administration limiting the sale of various flavor cartridges. Four months after that investment, though before it was publicly disclosed, investigators say the company's fortunes rebounded after the Trump administration authorized five new Juul e-cigarette products. The company has announced plans for more flavor authorization applications moving forward.

In a statement to NPR, a Juul spokesperson said the company had received Rep. Raskin's letter and are "reviewing it closely. As always, we intend to cooperate with any Congressional effort to understand our company, our commitment to combating underage vaping, and our mission to help adult smokers of combustible cigarettes transition completely away from smoking."

Investigators are also interested in betting site Polymarket. They say that following a meeting between Polymarket leadership and Trump Jr. at the 2024 Republican National Convention, 1789 Capital invested in the company — which at the time was banned in the United States. In July 2025, after President Trump took office, the Justice Department and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission notified the company that they had closed investigations launched during the Biden administration, according to reporting from Bloomberg News. The CFTC later authorized a U.S. version of the platform to launch. Investigators allege 1789's investment resulted in a 70-fold return.
Donald Trump Jr.'s venture capital firm will be major financial backer of Polymarket

GrabAGun, a company that "believe[s] people should be able to use their computers, phones, and tablets to shop for firearms the same way they purchase everything else," became, according to investigators, a publicly-traded company with the help of 1789 Capital leadership, including Trump Jr., who serves of its board.

In May 2026, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) proposed a draft rule that would make it easier to ship guns directly to people's homes. At the time, GrabAGun claimed that the company is "uniquely positioned to capitalize on this potential opportunity." Investigators are seeking to understand what knowledge and involvement Trump Jr. had of the proposed rule change.
body_zh: 9 月 10 日，小唐纳德·特朗普在达拉斯举行的 2026 年共和党全国代表大会第二天上台发表讲话。布兰登·贝尔/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
由可能担任众议院司法委员会主席的马里兰州众议员杰米·拉斯金 (Jamie Raskin) 领导的国会民主党人正在扩大对投资公司 1789 Capital 的调查，该公司在小唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump Jr.) 父亲连任白宫几天后聘请了该公司作为合伙人。
调查人员表示，自那时起，该公司已从管理资产 1.5 亿美元的“中等风险投资公司”成长为管理资产 30 亿美元的“风险投资界宠儿”。
调查人员希望确定，总统之子利用政治影响力或政府信息来确保与该投资公司有联系的公司获得联邦合同和监管变化，从而推动了增长。
众议院民主党人警告特朗普的 13 名盟友保存他们的记录以供即将进行的调查
小特朗普上周告诉 Axios，他被 1789 Capital 聘用的时机很巧合，并指出他已经与创始人奥米德·马利克 (Omeed Malik) 合作多年。他还表示，他在为公司营销和筹集资金时划清了界限。
“我（向外国投资者）明确表示，我与政府没有任何关系，”小特朗普说。 “[总统是]我的父亲，但他也很忙，我可能已经三周没有和他说过话了。”
他还表示，他不会利用或不需要政府关系来进行明智的投资。小特朗普说：“我认为，我们试图做据称每天都在做的事情，这种情况会持续大约两秒钟，然后才会公开。”他补充说，该公司依靠分析师团队对存在明显公共和国家安全需求但能够满足这些需求的公司相对较少的行业进行投资。
美国国家公共广播电台联系小唐纳德·特朗普征求意见，但没有得到回复。
关于拉斯金要求 1789 Capital 提供文件的问题，代表该公司的律师比尔·伯克 (Bill Burck) 告诉 NPR，“我们在 9 月份回复了拉斯金国会议员，详细指出了他对 1789 运作方式的理解中的许多缺陷以及一些基本的事实错误。他从来没有费心回复。事实就是事实，拉斯金国会议员在这里错了，但仍然坚持他对 1789 的荒诞故事。这些都是人身攻击。”不受实际证据的束缚。”
周一，国会调查人员致函四家公司——军事承包商 Hadrian、电子烟公司 Juul、预测市场 Polymarket 和在线武器经销商 GrabAGun——要求他们保存记录并向委员会移交大量记录。
该委员会对哈德良与武装部队今年三月签署的价值近十亿美元的合同感兴趣。调查人员称，到 2024 年，该公司只有一个制造工厂，并且“没有履行政府合同的历史”。他们还指出，首席执行官克里斯·鲍尔 (Chris Power) 在 2024 年大选之前向特朗普结盟的政治组织捐赠了数万美元。
政治捐款是受宪法保护的言论，并不一定是不当行为的证据。 1789 Capital于2025年7月首次投资Hadrian。该公司还得到了多家蓝筹投资者的支持，包括摩根士丹利、T. Rowe Price、Andreessen Horowitz和摩根大通。哈德良没有回复 NPR 的置评请求。
调查人员还指控，小特朗普的公司于 2025 年 3 月入股了电子烟公司 Juul，因为在特朗普第一届政府期间做出限制各种口味烟弹销售的裁决后，该公司濒临破产。这项投资虽然尚未公开披露，但四个月后，调查人员表示，在特朗普政府批准五种新的 Juul 电子烟产品后，该公司的命运出现了反弹。该公司已宣布计划继续进行更多风味授权申请。
Juul 发言人在给 NPR 的一份声明中表示，该公司已收到众议员拉斯金的信函，并“正在仔细审查。一如既往，我们打算配合国会的任何努力，以了解我们公司、我们对打击未成年人吸电子烟的承诺，以及我们帮助成年吸烟者完全戒烟的使命。”

调查人员还对博彩网站 Polymarket 感兴趣。他们表示，在 Polymarket 领导层与小特朗普在 2024 年共和党全国代表大会上会面后，1789 Capital 投资了该公司——该公司当时在美国是被禁止的。据彭博社报道，2025 年 7 月，特朗普总统上任后，司法部和商品期货交易委员会通知该公司，他们已结束拜登政府期间发起的调查。美国商品期货交易委员会随后授权推出该平台的美国版本。调查人员称，1789 的投资带来了 70 倍的回报。
小唐纳德·特朗普的风险投资公司将成为 Polymarket 的主要财务支持者
GrabAGun 是一家“相信人们应该能够像购买其他东西一样使用电脑、手机和平板电脑购买枪支”的公司，据调查人员称，在 1789 Capital 领导层（包括担任其董事会成员的小特朗普）的帮助下，该公司成为了一家上市公司。
2026 年 5 月，烟酒枪械和爆炸物管理局 (ATF) 提出了一项规则草案，旨在让枪支直接运送到人们家中变得更加容易。当时，GrabAGun 声称该公司“处于独特的地位，可以利用这一潜在机会”。调查人员正在试图了解小特朗普对拟议的规则变更有哪些了解和参与。

title_en: US army to detonate 68 barrels of toxic lead in Iowa on day before Thanksgiving
title_zh: 感恩节前一天，美军将在爱荷华州引爆 68 桶有毒铅
summary: Residents warned to stay indoors amid conflicting information about how far the dust plume could travel The US Army is set to detonate 68 barrels – five tons – of lead azide at an ammunition plant in rural Iowa on Wednesday morning, after delays and conflictin
summary_zh: 居民警告留在室内，因为关于尘埃羽流能传播多远的信息相互矛盾，美国陆军将引爆 68 个桶 – fi
body_en: Residents warned to stay indoors amid conflicting information about how far the dust plume could travel

The US Army is set to detonate 68 barrels – five tons – of lead azide at an ammunition plant in rural Iowa on Wednesday morning, after delays and conflicting information about how far the toxic lead dust plume could travel after the explosion.
That controlled blast has been scheduled for 10am ET on Wednesday, the day before the Thanksgiving holiday.

“Inaction is no longer an option,” Army Maj Gen Eric Shirley, the commander of the operation, said at a press conference in Middletown, Iowa, on Tuesday. “It would be irresponsible for us to not take the determined, consensus-based course of action moving forward.”

Federal officials on Tuesday said mitigation measures had been put in place, including barriers around the blast zone to capture much of the dust, but warned that residents in the vicinity should be prepared to evacuate.

“We don’t believe that the public should be in a panic,” said Adam Telle, acting secretary of the army. “Our goal is to keep as much of it as we can here on our Iowa Army Ammunition plant to prevent it from traveling.”

Telle said weather ⁠conditions on Wednesday morning were expected to be “ideal to protect public health and safety across the region” and stressed that a “controlled, mitigated, detonation” was “far preferable to an uncontrolled spontaneous detonation” of the unstable material.
State officials, environmental groups and residents have sharply criticized federal authorities over what many have described as a “communication failure” about the operation.

In a statement, Iowa senator-elect Josh Turek welcomed the army’s “long-overdue press conference” about Wednesday’s operation and vowed to “continue asking questions about how we got here” when he joins the chamber in January.

“There is no excuse for such a failure of transparency and communication, especially when the health and safety of the public is involved,” said Turek, who was born with spina bifida, which he attributes to his father’s exposure to Agent Orange during the Vietnam war. “Iowans should have had a full and clear understanding of the health implications of this operation, especially as children, pregnant women, and those with chronic illness are being advised to stay away from the affected area.”

Earlier on Tuesday, the army released new maps showing the projected plume path moving south-west of the Iowa army ammunition plant in Middletown, stretching through a south-eastern portion of the state before extending into northern Missouri.

The army sent an emergency notification to cellphones on Tuesday confirming the time of the controlled explosion – and warning that some people within 5 miles south-west of the plant may be evacuated.
The “imminent threat alert” told those up to 20 miles away to remain indoors with windows closed “to avoid airborne lead dust, noise and vibration”.

On Tuesday, the outgoing governor, Kim Reynolds, issued a proclamation of disaster emergency for Des Moines, Lee and Van Buren counties. Additionally, Reynolds said, she was deploying up to 100 soldiers from the Iowa national guard to support with public safety efforts.
Earlier in the day, the governor announced her support for the planned detonation after speaking with military leaders, including US defense secretary Pete Hegseth.
“I trust the army will do everything in its power to protect the people who could be affected,” she said in a statement.

The army said it had set up additional “blast barriers” around the bunkers where the lead azide will be detonated. It also said it would apply ballistic gels and foams to absorb the lead dust and douse the explosive materials with thousands of gallons of water.

The decision to proceed came after a federal appeals court cleared the way for the detonation to take place after the date had been changed three times after an outpouring of public concern. Environmentalists sued to stop the detonation, arguing that the planned explosion had not been issued permits correctly.

An attorney for the environmentalists emphasized that their legal challenge centers on the validity of the Environment Protection Agency permit – not the army’s decision to move forward with the detonation under the emergency provision.
body_zh: 由于关于尘埃羽流可以传播多远的信息相互矛盾，居民被警告留在室内
美国陆军定于周三上午在爱荷华州乡村的一家弹药厂引爆 68 桶（5 吨）叠氮化铅，但由于有关有毒铅尘羽在爆炸后可能传播多远的信息出现了延误和相互矛盾的情况。
这次受控爆炸定于美国东部时间周三上午 10 点进行，即感恩节假期前一天。
该行动指挥官陆军少将埃里克·雪利周二在爱荷华州米德尔敦举行的新闻发布会上表示：“无所作为已不再是一种选择。” “如果我们不采取坚定的、基于共识的行动方针向前推进，那将是不负责任的。”
联邦官员周二表示，缓解措施已经到位，包括在爆炸区域周围设置屏障以捕获大部分灰尘，但警告附近居民应做好撤离准备。
“我们认为公众不应该感到恐慌，”代理陆军部长亚当·泰勒说。 “我们的目标是尽可能将其保留在爱荷华州陆军弹药厂，以防止其外流。”
泰勒表示，预计周三上午的天气条件“非常适合保护整个地区的公众健康和安全”，并强调“受控、减轻的爆炸”“远比不稳定物质不受控制的自发爆炸更可取”。
州官员、环保组织和居民对联邦当局提出了严厉批评，许多人称此次行动“沟通失败”。
爱荷华州当选参议员乔什·图雷克 (Josh Turek) 在一份声明中对陆军关于周三行动的“迟来的新闻发布会”表示欢迎，并誓言在一月份加入众议院时“继续询问我们是如何走到这一步的”。
“透明度和沟通的失败是没有任何借口的，特别是当涉及到公众的健康和安全时，”图雷克说。他出生时患有脊柱裂，他将这种疾病归因于他父亲在越南战争期间接触橙剂。 “爱荷华州人应该对这次行动对健康的影响有一个全面而清晰的了解，特别是建议儿童、孕妇和慢性病患者远离受影响地区。”
周二早些时候，军方发布了新地图，显示预计羽流路径将向爱荷华州米德尔敦陆军弹药厂西南方向移动，穿过该州东南部，然后延伸到密苏里州北部。
周二，军队向手机发送了紧急通知，确认了受控爆炸的时间，并警告说，工厂西南 5 英里范围内的一些人可能会被疏散。
“迫在眉睫的威胁警报”告诉20英里外的人们留在室内并关闭窗户，“以避免空气中的铅尘、噪音和振动”。
周二，即将离任的州长金·雷诺兹（Kim Reynolds）发布了得梅因县、李县和范布伦县进入灾难紧急状态的公告。此外，雷诺兹表示，她正在部署多达 100 名爱荷华州国民警卫队士兵来支持公共安全工作。
当天早些时候，州长在与包括美国国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯在内的军事领导人交谈后宣布支持计划中的爆炸。
她在一份声明中说：“我相信军队将竭尽全力保护可能受到影响的人们。”
军方表示，他们已经在掩体周围设置了额外的“防爆屏障”，叠氮化铅将在那里被引爆。该公司还表示，将使用弹道凝胶和泡沫来吸收铅尘，并用数千加仑的水浇灭爆炸材料。
在公众强烈关注后，日期已三度更改，联邦上诉法院为爆炸的发生扫清了道路，随后做出了继续进行的决定。环保人士起诉要求停止爆炸，认为计划中的爆炸没有正确获得许可。
环保主义者的一名律师强调，他们的法律挑战集中在环境保护局许可证的有效性上，而不是军队根据紧急条款推进爆炸的决定。

title_en: Fort Hood mass shooter makes legal move to stop Pentagon’s firing squad execution
title_zh: 胡德堡大规模枪击案凶手采取法律行动阻止五角大楼行刑队处决
summary: The former Army officer whose scheduled military execution by firing squad provoked outrage over an initial proposal to livestream his death is planning to file a constitutional challenge that could halt his December execution, his lawyers said Tuesday.
summary_zh: 一名前陆军军官计划由行刑队执行军事处决，最初提议直播他的死亡，这引起了愤怒，这是有计划的
body_en: Trump cancels Hegseth's plan to livestream Fort Hood shooter's execution
Nov. 24, 2026, 7:15 PM EST / Updated Nov. 24, 2026, 10:09 PM EST

The former Army officer whose scheduled military execution by firing squad provoked outrage over an initial proposal to livestream his death is planning to file a constitutional challenge that could halt his December execution, his lawyers said Tuesday.

Nidal Hasan, convicted in the 2009 mass shooting at Fort Hood, Texas, that claimed 13 lives, filed a motion for a stay of execution so he can submit what’s known as a habeas corpus petition, which requires the government to justify a person’s detainment.

“There is no question that the violence committed at Fort Hood caused unimaginable pain and loss,” Anna Arceneaux, deputy director of the ACLU’s Capital Punishment Project, said in a statement. “But the gravity of that loss does not change the government’s obligation to uphold the principles that define our justice system. Mr. Hasan, like every person facing an irreversible punishment, must have a chance to pursue federal review of his case.”
Hasan, 56, had officially exhausted his military justice appeals, opening the door to President Donald Trump in October approving his death sentence and the Army setting an execution date .

Hasan’s request was filed in civilian court, which is another process available to military prisoners. Military experts told NBC News the legal maneuver to file a habeas corpus petition would all but assure Hasan’s case will be tied up in a lengthy review process that could effectively stall his pending execution to well beyond the end of Trump’s term. At that point, they say, Trump’s successor may avoid setting another execution date.
The motion was filed on behalf of Hasan by the ACLU of Kansas. Pentagon and Army officials could not immediately be reached for comment.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth first raised the prospect of livestreaming Hasan’s execution, telling a conservative news outlet that he would ensure “people are able to watch it, that it’s public, because people need to understand that there’s serious consequences for these types of things.”
But John Baker, the federal public defender for the Western District of North Carolina whose capital habeas unit is assisting Hasan, said the case deserves further review by a federal court.

“The President, the Secretary of Defense, and others have turned Mr. Hasan’s case into a political spectacle,” Baker said in a statement. “Our government cannot be permitted to execute Mr. Hasan until his death sentence has received full and fair review, which the Constitution safeguards through our federal courts.”

Few details were made available about how a firing squad execution could unfold, although Army officials said it would occur at 1 p.m. Dec. 3 at Fort Hood — around the time the attack occurred at the military base. During the shooting, Hasan was injured by responding officers and paralyzed and now requires a wheelchair.

Within days of Hegseth’s announcement, Trump said he would ultimately decide whether Hasan’s death could potentially be watched by millions of people online. He subsequently said in a Truth Social post that while livestreaming the execution “might have been a strong deterrent,” there are other people who “would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device.”
“He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad,” the president said, “but this event will not be streamed.”

Hegseth’s announcement had set off immediate backlash from a bipartisan group of lawmakers, human rights organizations and religious leaders, many of whom said a livestreamed execution would be “medieval” and “barbaric,” echoing public killings conducted by the most brutal totalitarian regimes and terror states and harkening back to the nation’s dark period of public lynchings and racism.

In the U.S., the last large-scale gathering for a lawfully public execution occurred in 1936 in Kentucky , where a Black man convicted of raping a white woman was hanged in front of thousands, according to news reports.

Opponents of livestreaming Hasan’s execution also warned it could be used as propaganda by jihadist militants, while playing into the desires of Hasan, an American-born Muslim who had become radicalized.
“I’m paraplegic and could be in jail for the rest of my life,” Hasan told a mental health panel following the shooting spree. “However, if I died by lethal injection, I would still be a martyr.”
The U.S. military has not put a service member to death by firing squad since 1945 and last executed a service member in 1961, by hanging. Both were conducted privately.
Currently, four people, including Hasan, are on the military’s death row at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas.
body_zh: 特朗普取消了赫格斯直播胡德堡枪手处决的计划
美国东部时间 2026 年 11 月 24 日晚上 7:15 / 更新于美国东部时间 2026 年 11 月 24 日晚上 10:09
这名前陆军军官的律师周二表示，他计划由行刑队执行军事处决，最初提议直播他的死亡过程，这引起了人们的愤怒，他正计划提出一项宪法挑战，以阻止他 12 月的处决。
尼达尔·哈桑 (Nidal Hasan) 在 2009 年德克萨斯州胡德堡大规模枪击事件中被定罪，造成 13 人死亡，他提出了一项暂缓执行死刑的动议，以便他可以提交所谓的人身保护令请愿书，该请愿书要求政府证明拘留某人的合理性。
美国公民自由联盟死刑项目副主任安娜·阿尔塞诺在一份声明中表示：“毫无疑问，胡德堡发生的暴力事件造成了难以想象的痛苦和损失。” “但这种损失的严重性并不会改变政府维护司法系统原则的义务。哈桑先生，就像每个面临不可逆转惩罚的人一样，必须有机会寻求联邦对其案件进行审查。”
56 岁的哈桑已正式用尽军事司法上诉，为唐纳德·特朗普总统于 10 月批准他的死刑和陆军设定执行日期打开了大门。
哈桑的请求已向民事法庭提出，这是军事囚犯可以使用的另一个程序。军事专家告诉 NBC 新闻，提交人身保护令请愿书的法律手段几乎可以确保哈桑的案件将陷入漫长的审查过程，这可能会有效地将他即将被处决的时间推迟到特朗普任期结束后。他们说，到那时，特朗普的继任者可能会避免设定另一个执行日期。
该动议是由堪萨斯州美国公民自由联盟代表哈桑提出的。未能立即联系到五角大楼和陆军官员置评。
国防部长皮特·赫格斯首先提出了直播哈桑处决的前景，他告诉一家保守派新闻媒体，他将确保“人们能够观看它，它是公开的，因为人们需要明白，此类事情会产生严重后果。”
但北卡罗来纳州西区的联邦公设辩护律师约翰·贝克(John Baker)表示，该案值得联邦法院进一步审查，该州的首都人身保护单位正在协助哈桑。
“总统、国防部长和其他人已经将哈桑先生的案件变成了一场政治奇观，”贝克在一份声明中说。 “在哈桑先生的死刑得到充分和公正的审查之前，我们的政府不能被允许处决他，这是宪法通过我们的联邦法院保障的。”
尽管陆军官员表示将于下午 1 点执行行刑，但关于行刑队如何执行的细节很少。 12 月 3 日，胡德堡——军事基地袭击事件发生前后。在枪击事件中，哈桑被赶来的警察打伤并瘫痪，现在需要轮椅。
在赫格塞斯宣布这一消息的几天内，特朗普表示，他将最终决定哈桑的死亡是否可能被数百万人在网上观看。他随后在《Truth Social》的一篇帖子中表示，虽然现场直播执行死刑“可能具有强大的威慑作用”，但还有其他人“宁愿不通过直播或任何其他视觉设备观看他死亡”。
总统说：“他将如期被行刑队处决，但这一事件不会被直播。”
赫格斯的声明立即引起了由立法者、人权组织和宗教领袖组成的两党团体的强烈反对，其中许多人表示，现场直播的处决是“中世纪的”和“野蛮的”，呼应了最残暴的极权主义政权和恐怖国家进行的公开杀戮，让人回想起该国公开私刑和种族主义的黑暗时期。
据新闻报道，在美国，最后一次大规模的合法公开处决发生在 1936 年的肯塔基州，一名因强奸白人妇女而被定罪的黑人男子在数千人面前被绞死。
哈桑处决直播的反对者还警告说，这可能会被圣战武装分子用来进行宣传，同时满足哈桑这个美国出生的穆斯林、已变得激进的愿望。
“我截瘫了，可能会在监狱里度过余生，”哈桑在枪击事件发生后告诉心理健康小组。 “但是，如果我是注射死刑，我仍然是烈士。”
The U.S. military has not put a service member to death by firing squad since 1945 and last executed a service member in 1961, by hanging.两者都是私下进行的。
目前，包括哈桑在内的四人被关押在堪萨斯州莱文沃斯堡的军方死囚牢房中。

title_en: Fort Hood survivors denied bid to witness shooter’s firing-squad execution
title_zh: 胡德堡幸存者拒绝见证枪手行刑队的处决
summary: Army says trio injured in 2009 attack were not direct victims of Nidal Hasan’s and thus cannot attend event Three survivors of the shooting at Fort Hood will not be allowed to witness the execution by military firing squad of Nidal Hasan who shot 13 people dea
summary_zh: 陆军称 2009 年袭击中受伤的三人不是尼达尔·哈桑枪击事件的直接受害者，因此无法参加活动 胡堡枪击事件的三名幸存者
body_en: Army says trio injured in 2009 attack were not direct victims of Nidal Hasan’s and thus cannot attend event

Three survivors of the shooting at Fort Hood will not be allowed to witness the execution by military firing squad of Nidal Hasan who shot 13 people dead in the attack at the Texas army post in 2009, military officials said Tuesday.
Hasan was found guilty of multiple counts of murder and attempted murder related to those killed and the more than 30 who were wounded by gunfire in the attack.
I saw Iran execute a man in public. Is this what the US wants? | Robert Tait

On 10 November, the army said the three cannot attend the execution scheduled for the afternoon of 3 December because none of them was the direct victim of those charges, citing regulations governing military executions. An email sent Tuesday and shared with the Associated Press by recipients said military officials rejected their request for reconsideration, citing security and space issues.
Meanwhile, on Tuesday, Hasan sought a stay of execution, US court records showed.

Previously, the three survivors argued that the army should apply a broader definition of “victim” from the uniform code of military justice that says a victim can be someone who suffered “direct physical, emotional or pecuniary harm”. They argued that the military’s refusal to allow them to attend implied they had not been victims because they were not struck by bullets.
A previous plan to livestream the military execution, the first since 1961 and the first by firing squad since the second world war, was rescinded after bipartisan backlash.
The letter signed by the commandant of Fort Leavenworth, the military prison where Hasan is being held, said the three cannot appeal again.
“Please understand that this is not meant as a judgment on any emotional injury you or others suffered as a result of CP Hasan’s crimes,” it said.
Retired Colonel Kathy Platoni, who would have been Hasan’s supervisor during a planned deployment to Afghanistan, said the denial felt like a betrayal.
“I would desperately like to attend,” Platoni said from her home in Ohio. “To look Hasan in the eye and say: ‘You didn’t get me.’”
The army noted in a statement that regulations specify who can witness a military execution, and reiterated the size and space restrictions.
“Efforts have been made over the years, from the trial to notifications to memorials and now to the execution, to recognize the impacts and support the victims,” the Army statement said.
Platoni said the survivors from her unit deployed to Afghanistan 29 days after the attack, because, “we still served our country, and if we didn’t, [Hasan’] would have won”.
She said the building where Hasan initially opened fire had been crowded with returning soldiers and those preparing to deploy. She had been moved to another building when the attack began.
“The looks on the faces of my friends and colleagues as they carried in the dying and wounded that day … it will haunt me for the rest of my life,” she said.
She said they carried in the badly wounded captain who had rushed Hasan with a chair to try to stop the shooting.

“I was throwing computers to the ground trying to get the tablecloths because we needed blankets. We didn’t have medical supplies or even water,” she said. “I still have that blood-stained uniform, from kneeling down next to that young man, trying to get him to stay with us. That will be with me forever.”
body_zh: 陆军称 2009 年袭击中受伤的三人不是尼达尔·哈桑袭击的直接受害者，因此无法参加活动
军方官员周二表示，胡德堡枪击事件的三名幸存者将不会被允许目睹军事行刑队对尼达尔·哈桑的处决，尼达尔·哈桑在 2009 年得克萨斯州军事哨所的袭击中枪杀了 13 人。
哈桑被判犯有多项谋杀罪和谋杀未遂罪，罪名与袭击中遇难者和 30 多名枪伤者有关。
我看到伊朗当众处决一名男子。这就是美国想要的吗？ |罗伯特·泰特
11 月 10 日，军方援引有关军事处决的规定表示，这三人无法参加定于 12 月 3 日下午举行的处决，因为他们都不是这些指控的直接受害者。周二发送并由收件人分享给美联社的一封电子邮件称，军方官员以安全和太空问题为由，拒绝了他们重新考虑的请求。
与此同时，美国法庭记录显示，哈桑于周二寻求暂缓执行死刑。
此前，三名幸存者认为，军队应该应用统一军事司法准则中更广泛的“受害者”定义，即受害者可以是遭受“直接身体、情感或金钱伤害”的人。他们辩称，军方拒绝让他们参加意味着他们不是受害者，因为他们没有被子弹击中。
之前的一项直播军事行刑的计划是自 1961 年以来的第一次，也是二战以来行刑队的第一次，但在两党强烈反对后被取消。
关押哈桑的军事监狱莱文沃斯堡监狱长签署的信函称，三人不能再次上诉。
“请理解，这并不是对你或其他人因CP哈桑的罪行而遭受的任何情感伤害的判断，”它说。
退役上校凯西·普拉托尼（Kathy Platoni）在计划部署到阿富汗期间担任哈桑的上司，她表示，这一否认感觉像是一种背叛。
“我非常想参加，”普拉托尼在俄亥俄州的家中说道。 “看着哈桑的眼睛说：‘你没有明白我的意思。’”
军方在一份声明中指出，法规规定了谁可以见证军事处决，并重申了规模和空间限制。
陆军声明称：“多年来，从审判到通知、纪念，再到现在的处决，我们一直在努力认识到影响并支持受害者。”
普拉托尼说，袭击发生 29 天后，她所在部队的幸存者被部署到阿富汗，因为“我们仍然为我们的国家服务，如果我们不这样做，[哈桑]就会获胜”。
她说，哈桑最初开枪的大楼里挤满了回国的士兵和准备部署的士兵。袭击开始时，她已被转移到另一栋大楼。
“那天，我的朋友和同事们抬着死者和伤者时脸上的表情……这将在我的余生中困扰着我，”她说。
她说，他们抬走了受重伤的船长，他用椅子冲向哈桑，试图阻止枪击事件。
“我把电脑扔到地上，试图拿到桌布，因为我们需要毯子。我们没有医疗用品，甚至没有水，”她说。 “我仍然保留着那件沾满血迹的制服，那是我跪在那个年轻人旁边，试图让他留在我们身边。那将永远伴随着我。”

title_en: Moving to Florida may become a choice of some Republicans after midterms
title_zh: 中期选举后搬到佛罗里达可能成为一些共和党人的选择
summary: In Florida, Republicans kept power of state government after the midterms. It's now the largest state where the GOP is still in charge.
summary_zh: 在佛罗里达州，共和党人在中期选举后保留了州政府的权力。它现在是共和党仍在掌权的最大州。
body_en: Moving to Florida may become a choice of some Republicans after midterms In Florida, Republicans kept power of state government after the midterms. It's now the largest state where the GOP is still in charge.
In Florida, Republicans kept power of state government after the midterms. It's now the largest state where the GOP is still in charge.
Florida is the largest state in the country where Republicans kept control after the midterms. Some credit conservatives who moved there in recent years, like Republican Michael Fusella.
MICHAEL FUSELLA: So I think that they actually have a lot to thank us for, and they should be grateful that we're here.
DETROW: Meghan Bowman with member station WUSF in Tampa reports that the trend could continue post-midterms.

MEGHAN BOWMAN, BYLINE: Democratic candidates made gains in Florida in the midterms and won a few more seats in the state legislature, but Republicans still control all branches of Florida's government.
FUSELLA: It's been that, like, shining beacon on the hill for the country.
BOWMAN: Republican voter Michael Fusella says he's proud his party held strong here.

FUSELLA: This was a blue tsunami, but I also think it was a red wildfire. Wildfires, they burn everything down in sight. However, wildfires are actually good. They rejuvenate the soil, and that - it grows back even stronger, right?
BOWMAN: Fusella moved to Tampa from New Jersey about four years ago. He says Florida Republicans held the line election night because of people like him.
FUSELLA: So many conservatives, like myself, fled these Democrat states, especially from up north, and came down here and helped change Florida into the conservative stronghold that it is today.
BOWMAN: That was especially true during the COVID years. And now there are signs some Texans might consider the Sunshine State.

BOWMAN: People in Austin cheered when Democratic Senator-elect James Talarico won in the notoriously red state. But for conservative voters like Reigen Lox in suburban Dallas, the news wasn't as exciting.
REIGEN LOX: I had an inkling that something could change, but I didn't expect it on this large of a scale. And I think that is concerning for a lot of people in Texas.

BOWMAN: Now Lox is considering moving to Florida based on the midterm results. Marie Bailey is a conservative and a realtor in the Dallas-Fort Worth area. She started a Facebook group for people leaving California and moving to Texas. Now she's considering moving herself.

MARIE BAILEY: Everyone was shocked at the election, and there's a lot of people that are rethinking their move. And we all know that Florida's a destination for people moving, but I think even more so now that Texas turned blue.

BOWMAN: She says the beaches, amusement parks and cruise ports are a big draw. And with the midterm results, conservatives may be eyeing the state for its values. But Kirsten England, a political science professor at the University of South Florida, says it's unlikely a large influx of people are relocating solely because of the midterm results.
body_zh: 中期选举后移居佛罗里达可能成为部分共和党人的选择 在佛罗里达州，中期选举后共和党人保留了州政府的权力。它现在是共和党仍在掌权的最大州。
在佛罗里达州，共和党人在中期选举后保留了州政府的权力。它现在是共和党仍在掌权的最大州。
佛罗里达州是美国最大的州，中期选举后共和党继续控制该州。近年来搬到那里的一些信用保守派人士，例如共和党人迈克尔·富塞拉(Michael Fusella)。
迈克尔·富塞拉：所以我认为他们实际上有很多事情要感谢我们，他们应该感谢我们来到这里。
德特罗：坦帕 WUSF 会员站的梅根·鲍曼 (Meghan Bowman) 报告说，这种趋势可能会在中期选举后继续下去。
梅根·鲍曼连线：民主党候选人在佛罗里达州中期选举中取得了进展，并在州立法机构中赢得了更多席位，但共和党人仍然控制着佛罗里达州政府的所有部门。
富塞拉：就像山上为这个国家照亮的灯塔一样。
鲍曼：共和党选民迈克尔·富塞拉表示，他为自己的政党在这里保持强势而感到自豪。
弗塞拉：这是一场蓝色海啸，但我也认为这是一场红色野火。野火，烧毁了眼前的一切。然而，野火实际上是好事。他们使土壤恢复活力，然后它会变得更加强壮，对吧？
鲍曼：大约四年前，富塞拉从新泽西州搬到了坦帕。他说佛罗里达州共和党人因为像他这样的人而举行了选举之夜。
富塞拉：很多保守派人士，比如我自己，逃离了这些民主党州，尤其是来自北部的州，来到这里，帮助佛罗里达州变成了今天这样的保守派大本营。
鲍曼：在新冠疫情期间尤其如此。现在有迹象表明，一些德克萨斯人可能会考虑选择阳光之州。
鲍曼：当民主党当选参议员詹姆斯·塔拉里科在这个臭名昭著的红色州获胜时，奥斯汀的人们欢呼雀跃。但对于像达拉斯郊区的雷根·洛克斯这样的保守派选民来说，这个消息并不那么令人兴奋。
REIGEN LOX：我预感到有些事情可能会发生变化，但我没想到会发生如此大规模的变化。我认为这对德克萨斯州的很多人来说都是令人担忧的。
BOWMAN：现在 Lox 正在考虑根据中期结果搬到佛罗里达州。玛丽·贝利 (Marie Bailey) 是达拉斯-沃斯堡地区的一名保守派和房地产经纪人。她为离开加利福尼亚州搬到德克萨斯州的人们创建了一个 Facebook 群组。现在她正在考虑搬家。
玛丽·贝利：每个人都对选举感到震惊，很多人正在重新考虑他们的举动。我们都知道佛罗里达州是人们搬家的目的地，但我认为现在德克萨斯州变蓝后更是如此。
鲍曼：她说海滩、游乐园和游轮港口很有吸引力。从中期结果来看，保守派可能会关注该州的价值观。但南佛罗里达大学政治学教授克尔斯滕·英格兰表示，大量涌入的人不太可能仅仅因为中期结果而搬迁。

title_en: Meta and other social media firms are not liable for Buffalo mass shooting, court rules
title_zh: 法院规定，Meta 和其他社交媒体公司不对布法罗大规模枪击事件负责
summary: New York’s top court upholds lower court decision to dismiss claims against tech firms in lawsuit over 2022 shooting Facebook, YouTube and other social media companies aren’t liable for the racist mass shooting at a supermarket in Buffalo, New York, the state’
summary_zh: 纽约最高法院维持下级法院的裁决，驳回针对 2022 年 Facebook、YouTube 和其他社交媒体枪击事件对科技公司提起的诉讼
body_en: Meta and other social media firms are not liable for Buffalo mass shooting, court rules | Buffalo shooting
New York’s top court upholds lower court decision to dismiss claims against tech firms in lawsuit over 2022 shooting

Facebook, YouTube and other social media companies aren’t liable for the racist mass shooting at a supermarket in Buffalo, New York, the state’s highest court ruled this week in lawsuits over the 2022 attack.

In a 4-3 decision Monday, the court of appeals upheld a lower court’s decision to dismiss claims against the tech firms from survivors and victims’ relatives, more than four years after the shooting devastated the affected communities.
The lawsuits accused the companies of offering online platforms engineered to promote extreme content and encourage compulsive use and of helping to radicalize shooter Payton Gendron.

Gendron, who is white, absorbed racist conspiracy theories online before he killed 10 Black people and wounded three others at the Tops Friendly Market. The 23-year-old is serving a life sentence after pleading guilty to state-level murder charges.
He told a court in 2023 that he “believed what I read online and acted out of hate”.

The Albany-based court of appeals said the four lawsuits “fail to establish that the shooter’s actions were a natural and foreseeable consequence of these defendants’ decisions about how to design and operate their platforms”.

Three judges disagreed, saying the survivors and families had built enough of a case for it to go forward. Gendron described himself in his diary as an online “addict” whose “mental health has seriously degraded”, the dissenters noted in an opinion by judge Jenny Rivera.

The ruling affected Facebook and Instagram owner Meta; Google and YouTube parent Alphabet; and Reddit. Under different reasoning, the decision also upheld the dismissal of claims against other messaging and social media apps as well as Amazon, which owns Twitch, the service that Gendron used to livestream the rampage.
Matthew Bergman, who represents victim Heyward Patterson’s family and estate in one of the cases, said Tuesday they were assessing their legal options after the ruling.
“The families affected by the tragic May 2022 Buffalo grocery store attack deserve accountability when dangerous product design choices contribute to real-world harm,” Bergman said in a statement.
Messages seeking comment were sent to lawyers for the other plaintiffs and for the companies.
Jury selection is ongoing for Gendron’s additional trial on federal hate crimes, which carries the possibility of a death sentence if he is convicted. He has pleaded not guilty in that case.

The people he killed ranged in age from 32 to 86. In addition to Patterson, they were Celestine Chaney, Geraldine Talley, Katherine Massey, Pearl Young, Andre Mackneil, Ruth Whitfield, Roberta Drury, Margus Morrison and Aaron Salter.
body_zh: 法院规定，Meta 和其他社交媒体公司不对布法罗大规模枪击事件承担责任 |水牛射击
纽约最高法院维持下级法院驳回针对 2022 年枪击案诉讼中科技公司索赔的裁决
纽约州最高法院本周在针对 2022 年袭击事件的诉讼中裁定，Facebook、YouTube 和其他社交媒体公司不对纽约州布法罗一家超市发生的种族主义大规模枪击事件负责。
周一，上诉法院以 4 比 3 的裁决维持了下级法院的决定，驳回了幸存者和受害者亲属对科技公司提出的索赔，此时距枪击事件摧毁了受影响的社区已有四年多了。
这些诉讼指控这些公司提供旨在宣传极端内容和鼓励强迫性使用的在线平台，并帮助使射手佩顿·詹德伦变得激进。
白人詹德伦在网上吸收了种族主义阴谋论，然后在 Tops Friendship 市场杀死了 10 名黑人并打伤了另外 3 人。这名 23 岁的男子在承认州级谋杀指控后正在服无期徒刑。
2023 年，他在法庭上表示，他“相信我在网上读到的内容，并出于仇恨而采取行动”。
奥尔巴尼上诉法院表示，这四起诉讼“未能证明枪手的行为是这些被告关于如何设计和运营其平台的决定的自然且可预见的结果”。
三名法官不同意，称幸存者和家属已经建立了足够的证据来推动案件的进展。反对者在珍妮·里维拉法官的意见中指出，詹德伦在日记中将自己描述为一名网络“瘾君子”，其“心理健康状况严重恶化”。
该裁决影响了 Facebook 和 Instagram 所有者 Meta；谷歌和 YouTube 母公司 Alphabet；和Reddit。根据不同的推理，该决定还维持了对其他消息和社交媒体应用程序以及亚马逊的索赔，亚马逊拥有 Twitch，Gendron 用来直播这场暴行的服务。
其中一起案件中受害人海沃德·帕特森的家人和遗产的代表马修·伯格曼周二表示，他们正在评估裁决后的法律选择。
伯格曼在一份声明中表示：“当危险的产品设计选择造成现实世界的伤害时，受 2022 年 5 月布法罗杂货店悲剧性袭击影响的家庭应该承担责任。”
寻求评论的消息已发送给其他原告和公司的律师。
詹德伦联邦仇恨犯罪的额外审判正在进行陪审团遴选，如果罪名成立，他有可能被判处死刑。他在此案中不认罪。
他杀害的人年龄从32岁到86岁不等。除了帕特森之外，他们还包括塞莱斯廷·钱尼、杰拉尔丁·塔利、凯瑟琳·梅西、珀尔·杨、安德烈·麦克尼尔、露丝·惠特菲尔德、罗伯塔·德鲁里、马格斯·莫里森和亚伦·索尔特。

title_en: Climate scientists urge US lawmakers to vote no on sweeping permitting bill
title_zh: 气候科学家敦促美国立法者对全面的许可法案投反对票
summary: Open letter warns Baaja, intended to expedite energy and infrastructure projects, will cause irreversible climate harm A group of more than 120 climate scientists have urged US lawmakers to not pass contentious legislation to speed up the building of energy pr
summary_zh: 公开信警告巴哈旨在加快能源和基础设施项目，将造成不可逆转的气候危害 120多个气候组织
body_en: Open letter warns Baaja, intended to expedite energy and infrastructure projects, will cause irreversible climate harm

A group of more than 120 climate scientists have urged US lawmakers to not pass contentious legislation to speed up the building of energy projects, datacenters and other infrastructure, amid a growing backlash to the sweeping permitting bill.

In an open letter to members of the House of Representatives , the collection of Earth and social sciences researchers expressed “deep concern” that the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (or Baaja) weakens environmental laws, locks in new fossil fuel projects without recourse and delivers only minor cuts to planet-heating emissions.
A year of deadly floods and fires – and yet Cop31 still collapsed. When will our leaders grasp the scale of this crisis? | Bill McGuire
“We understand the need for trade-offs and compromise when passing bipartisan legislation,” they wrote. “But as scientists we feel strongly that the costs of this bill to the climate are too high.”

Last week, the US Senate rapidly passed Baaja , a bill co-written by two Democratic and two Republican senators but one that has bitterly divided Democrats and environmentalists . The House is set to vote on the bill next week, where it will be signed by Donald Trump into law if passed.

Michael Mann, a climate scientist who helped arrange the open letter, said that he did so because Baaja is a “deeply problematic bill” that is “backed by a veritable who’s who of bad fossil fuel and dark money actors”.

Mann said that Democrats, who take control of Congress in January, should “scrap Baaja, which in the end only takes us further down the dangerous fossil fuel pathway, and put a sensible, popular datacenter bill on Trump’s desk and force him to veto it. And force Republicans to defend sustaining that veto.”

Timmons Roberts, a Brown University academic and letter co-signatory, said the bill is “very worrisome, it has felt very rushed and there is grave potential for damage that can’t be undone any time soon”.

“We are in a broken system, and it’s hard to build anything, but there has to be a better way to do this,” Roberts added. “In some ways it feels like we are being held hostage. If you want more renewables you have to also see the lock-in of fossil fuels and the devastating gutting of core legislation that has allowed the US to improve its natural environment.”

Mann said that Sheldon Whitehouse, the Democratic senator and longtime champion of climate action who has co-sponsored Baaja, has “long been one of my heroes, and nothing pains me to find him not only in support of the bill but in fact one of its principal backers”.

Asked for his response to the letter, Whitehouse said: “I have great respect for these climate scientists, and I am sorry to disagree with them here. The important takeaways about this bill are the gigaton-scale emissions reductions, the freed-up clean power, the $10bn in annual consumer electricity savings, and the $35bn whack at datacenters.”

Supporters of Baaja, who include some Democrats, a minority of green groups and other climate scientists , point to the laborious, sometimes terminal wait for clean energy projects to be approved and come online, as well as the lack of integrated power lines to take solar or wind-generated electrons to where it is needed.

Baaja would slash the barriers to new transmission lines and shrink the role of statutes such as the Clean Water Act and Endangered Species Act in scrutinizing various projects, aiding their rapid approval and making them virtually immune from being overturned by any future administration or the courts.

This should unleash much of the clean energy waiting to be connected to the grid but will also sideline legal challenges to new oil pipelines, datacenters and other infrastructure, such as ICE detention centers. This has raised alarm over a potential surge in fossil fuel activity and datacenters sited on public lands, with little community or tribal input.
“Congress must reject Baaja in its entirety,” the National Congress of American Indians said in a statement. “Native sovereignty, sacred places, and cultural heritage are not negotiable.”

The varied coalition of opponents, including former vice-president Al Gore , also argue that Trump will not faithfully execute the law. The president, a major backer of the artificial intelligence industry, has said Baaja result in a “tremendous amounts of new building” for dat centers but has insisted that he will still not allow the permitting of new wind power, which he has called a “major loser”.
“Democrats, what is the matter with you? Don’t you know better than to trust Trump?” the actor Mark Ruffalo, an environmental advocate, said in a widely-viewed social media post .

Unusually for a major, 500-page piece of legislation , Baaja has been pushed through Congress without a hearing. The pace of its ascension increases its chance of getting needed Republican support, including Trump’s, to pass, with no guarantee of such backing should Democrats write their own, revised version from January.
body_zh: 公开信警告巴哈旨在加快能源和基础设施项目，将造成不可逆转的气候危害
由于对全面许可法案的强烈反对，由 120 多名气候科学家组成的团体敦促美国立法者不要通过有争议的立法来加快能源项目、数据中心和其他基础设施的建设。
在一封致众议院议员的公开信中，地球和社会科学研究人员的集合表达了“深切关注”，两党的美国负担能力和就业法案（或巴哈）削弱了环境法，锁定了新的化石燃料项目而没有追索权，并且仅小幅削减了地球供暖排放。
这一年发生了致命的洪水和火灾，但第 31 届缔约方大会仍然失败。我们的领导人什么时候才能掌握这场危机的严重程度？ |比尔·麦奎尔
他们写道：“我们理解在通过两党立法时需要进行权衡和妥协。” “但作为科学家，我们强烈认为这项法案对气候造成的成本太高了。”
上周，美国参议院迅速通过了《巴哈法案》(Baaja)，这项法案由两名民主党参议员和两名共和党参议员共同起草，但该法案引起了民主党和环保人士的严重分歧。众议院将于下周对该法案进行投票，如果获得通过，唐纳德·特朗普将签署该法案成为法律。
帮助安排这封公开信的气候科学家迈克尔·曼 (Michael Mann) 表示，他这样做是因为《巴哈法案》是一项“存在严重问题的法案”，该法案“得到了名副其实的不良化石燃料和黑钱演员的支持”。
曼恩表示，一月份控制国会的民主党人应该“废除巴哈法案，这最终只会让我们在危险的化石燃料道路上走得更远，并将一项明智的、受欢迎的数据中心法案放在特朗普的办公桌上，迫使他否决它。并迫使共和党人为维持否决权辩护。”
布朗大学学者、信件联署人蒂蒙斯·罗伯茨表示，该法案“非常令人担忧，感觉非常仓促，而且可能会造成严重的损害，而且短期内无法挽回”。
“我们处于一个破碎的系统中，很难构建任何东西，但必须有更好的方法来做到这一点，”罗伯茨补充道。 “在某些方面，我们感觉像是被扣为人质。如果你想要更多的可再生能源，你还必须看到化石燃料的锁定以及允许美国改善自然环境的核心立法的毁灭性破坏。”
曼恩表示，民主党参议员谢尔登·怀特豪斯（Sheldon Whitehouse）是巴哈的共同发起人，也是气候行动的长期倡导者，“长期以来一直是我的英雄之一，看到他不仅支持该法案，而且实际上是该法案的主要支持者之一，我感到很高兴”。
当被问及他对这封信的回应时，怀特豪斯说：“我非常尊重这些气候科学家，很抱歉在这里不同意他们的观点。这项法案的重要收获是十亿吨规模的减排、释放的清洁能源、每年节省 100 亿美元的消费者电力，以及对数据中心的 350 亿美元的打击。”
巴哈的支持者包括一些民主党人、少数绿色团体和其他气候科学家，他们指出，清洁能源项目获得批准和上线的过程非常漫长，有时甚至是最后一刻，而且缺乏综合电力线来将太阳能或风能发电带到需要的地方。
巴哈将削减新输电线路的障碍，并缩小《清洁水法》和《濒危物种法》等法规在审查各种项目方面的作用，帮助它们快速获得批准，并使它们几乎免受未来任何政府或法院推翻的影响。
这应该会释放大量等待并网的清洁能源，但也将回避对新石油管道、数据中心和其他基础设施（例如 ICE 拘留中心）的法律挑战。这引起了人们对化石燃料活动和位于公共土地上的数据中心可能激增的警惕，而社区或部落的投入很少。
美国印第安人全国代表大会在一份声明中表示，“国会必须完全拒绝巴哈”。 “土著主权、圣地和文化遗产是不容谈判的。”
包括前副总统戈尔在内的各种反对者联盟也认为特朗普不会忠实地执行法律。总统是人工智能行业的主要支持者，他表示巴哈为数据中心带来了“大量新建筑”，但坚称他仍然不会允许新的风力发电，他称之为“主要输家”。
“民主党人，你们怎么了？难道你们不知道最好不要相信特朗普吗？”环保倡导者演员马克·鲁法洛在一篇广受关注的社交媒体帖子中说道。
对于一项长达 500 页的重要立法来说，巴哈在没有举行听证会的情况下就被推向国会通过，这是不同寻常的。该法案提升的速度增加了获得包括特朗普在内的共和党支持通过的机会，但如果民主党从一月份开始编写自己的修订版本，则不能保证获得这种支持。

title_en: How tariffs, fuel and fertilizer costs are squeezing the U.S.'s biggest apple region
title_zh: 关税、燃料和化肥成本如何挤压美国最大的苹果产区
summary: Washington's $9 billion industry grows more than 70% of the nation's fresh apples. Farmers are being pressed by high costs, tariffs and a strong dollar that diminishes foreign purchasing power.
summary_zh: 华盛顿价值 90 亿美元的产业种植了全国 70% 以上的新鲜苹果。农民正面临高成本、关税和坚挺美元的压力
body_en: As Sean Gilbert stepped out of his white GMC pickup, he breathed in the scent of applewood and Columbia Basin dust. Here, just south of Wapato, Wash., one of his 50-acre Gala and Red Delicious apple orchards is ground into huge piles of mulch chips. The wood chipper is the size of a semi-truck and belts out a screeching racket.

He said this ground will lay fallow. It will cost this fifth-generation apple farmer less to leave it unplanted and weedy than to plant another orchard or crop. He scooped up a handful of applewood mulch. "It's a bit of a relief that we're not going to continue to be hemorrhaging dollars on orchards that the market doesn't want," he said. "It hasn't been making sense for a while."
Washington's $9 billion industry grows nearly 70% of the nation's fresh apples, according to Jon DeVaney, president of the Washington State Tree Fruit Association.

DeVaney said farmers are being pressed by the costs of labor, fuel, fertilizer, equipment, as well as weak exports from international tariffs and a strong dollar that diminishes foreign purchasing power.

He estimated thousands of acres of apple orchards across the Northwest are being rapidly torn out, or are not being actively cared for, because many farmers aren't making money growing the fruit. And after several years of similar economic conditions, many farms have gone deep into debt – with even some large, well-established operations filing for bankruptcy .
In this orchard, apples are often picked in the early hours of summer mornings to keep the fruit and workers cool. Andrea Starr hide caption

In the late summer and fall, unpicked apples have been left to rot in branches and on the ground. Over the past few years, an estimated thousands of acres have only been partially picked or not picked at all, according to Kate Tynan, senior vice president of the Northwest Horticultural Council , a trade association that advocates for the Northwest tree fruit industry on federal policy issues and international trade.
One U.S. visa program is growing rapidly. No one is happy with it
Farmers fear more damage from U.S.-Canada trade fight
Trump administration announces $12 billion in one-time payments to farmers

Recent federal regulatory changes would effectively lower wages for some immigrant workers and take housing costs out of their paychecks. Tynan said with updates to the way wages are calculated, farm owners are hoping they'll be able to break even – but the farm workers union has pushed back on these changes and an upcoming federal judicial decision could put operators on the hook for backpay for the 2026 season.

U.S. farmers have also been especially hard hit by tariffs and high input costs. The Trump administration announced $12 billion in payments to farmers at the end of 2025 that primarily targeted farmers who grow crops such as soybeans and corn. Tynan said much of that relief has not reached farmers that grow specialty crops like fruit and vegetables.

"The Pacific Northwest has lost an unprecedented number of tree fruit farms in recent years," Tynan said. "Economic conditions have worsened drastically since then, so we know that number is far higher today."

She points to a USDA census conducted every five years that recorded a 15% drop in Washington tree fruit farms between 2017 and 2022. In neighboring Oregon, more than a quarter of apple, pear and cherry farms were lost in that same time period. By the numbers, apple acreage in Washington increased slightly during this period. But small, family-run farms face another threat: large, well-funded corporations are buying out orchard owners, reducing competition when profits are already tight .
"Some of that was new investment from [private equity] coming in during that time. That acreage trend has since reversed," said Jon DeVaney, emphasizing that the industry is losing growers.

"From 2023, 2024 and 2025 have been the really hard years," said Sean Gilbert, who co-owns Gilbert Orchards, a family-run company founded in 1898 that manages 4,000 acres of fruit in Washington state.
While Gilbert Orchards has worked to navigate these broad economic shifts, visual journalists with Northwest Public Broadcasting chronicled a full year of the business of growing apples.

Maria Aguilar (center) and Maria de la Soccoro Ramirez (left) presort Granny Smith apples, removing leaves, debris and rotten fruit. Ramirez has worked at Gilbert Orchards in Washington's Yakima Valley for 15 years. She said she's comfortable here and enjoys that her job is close to her home. Annie Warren/NWPB hide caption

Fifth-generation apple farmer Sean Gilbert, co-owner of Gilbert Orchards, stands in his office in west Yakima Valley in front of portraits of his great-great-grandparents, who founded the family-run company in 1898. Annie Warren/NWPB hide caption
body_zh: 当肖恩·吉尔伯特走出他的白色 GMC 皮卡时，他吸入了苹果木和哥伦比亚盆地灰尘的气味。在这里，就在华盛顿州瓦帕托以南，他的一个 50 英亩的 Gala 和 Red Delicious 苹果园被磨成大堆的覆盖物碎片。这台木材削片机有半卡车大小，发出刺耳的噪音。
他说这块土地将休耕。对于这位第五代苹果种植者来说，如果不种植苹果并杂草丛生，其成本要比种植另一个果园或农作物要少。他舀起一把苹果木覆盖物。他说：“我们不会继续在市场不想要的果园上浪费金钱，这让我们松了一口气。” “已经有一段时间没有意义了。”
华盛顿州树果协会主席乔恩·德瓦尼 (Jon DeVaney) 表示，华盛顿州价值 90 亿美元的产业种植了全国近 70% 的新鲜苹果。
德瓦尼表示，农民面临着劳动力、燃料、化肥、设备成本以及国际关税导致的出口疲软和美元走强削弱外国购买力的压力。
他估计，西北地区数千英亩的苹果园正在迅速被拆除，或者没有得到积极的照料，因为许多农民种植苹果并没有赚钱。经过几年相似的经济状况，许多农场已经深陷债务之中，甚至一些规模较大、信誉良好的农场也申请破产。
在这个果园里，人们经常在夏季清晨采摘苹果，以保持水果和工人的凉爽。安德里亚·斯塔尔隐藏标题栏
在夏末和秋季，未采摘的苹果被留在树枝上和地上腐烂。西北园艺委员会高级副总裁凯特·泰南表示，在过去的几年里，估计有数千英亩土地只被部分采摘或根本没有采摘。西北园艺委员会是一个在联邦政策问题和国际贸易问题上倡导西北果树产业的贸易协会。
一项美国签证计划正在迅速发展。没有人对此感到满意
农民担心美加贸易战造成更多损失
特朗普政府宣布向农民一次性支付 120 亿美元
最近的联邦监管变化将有效降低一些移民工人的工资，并将住房成本从他们的工资中扣除。泰南表示，随着工资计算方式的更新，农场主希望他们能够实现收支平衡，但农场工人工会已经推迟了这些变化，即将到来的联邦司法裁决可能会让经营者承担 2026 年产季拖欠工资的责任。
美国农民也受到关税和高投入成本的严重打击。特朗普政府宣布于 2025 年底向农民支付 120 亿美元，主要针对种植大豆和玉米等农作物的农民。泰南表示，大部分救济并未惠及种植水果和蔬菜等特种作物的农民。
“近年来，太平洋西北地区失去了前所未有数量的果树农场，”泰南说。 “从那时起，经济状况急剧恶化，所以我们知道今天的数字要高得多。”
她指出，美国农业部每五年进行一次的人口普查显示，2017 年至 2022 年间，华盛顿州的果树农场减少了 15%。在邻近的俄勒冈州，同期有超过四分之一的苹果、梨和樱桃农场消失。从数字来看，华盛顿州的苹果种植面积在此期间略有增加。但小型家庭经营的农场面临着另一个威胁：资金充足的大型公司正在收购果园所有者，在利润已经紧张的情况下减少竞争。
乔恩·德瓦尼 (Jon DeVaney) 表示：“其中一些是当时来自[私募股权]的新投资。此后种植面积趋势发生了逆转。”他强调该行业正在失去种植者。
“从 2023 年、2024 年和 2025 年开始，是真正艰难的几年，”吉尔伯特果园 (Gilbert Orchards) 的共同所有人肖恩·吉尔伯特 (Sean Gilbert) 说，该公司是一家家族经营公司，成立于 1898 年，在华盛顿州管理着 4,000 英亩的水果。
虽然吉尔伯特果园致力于应对这些广泛的经济转变，但西北公共广播公司的视觉记者记录了全年的苹果种植业务。
玛丽亚·阿吉拉尔（中）和玛丽亚·德拉索科罗·拉米雷斯（左）对青苹果进行预处理，去除叶子、碎片和腐烂的水果。拉米雷斯已在华盛顿亚基马谷的吉尔伯特果园工作了 15 年。她说她在这里很舒服，并且喜欢她的工作地点离家很近。安妮·沃伦/NWPB 隐藏标题栏
第五代苹果种植者肖恩·吉尔伯特 (Sean Gilbert) 是吉尔伯特果园 (Gilbert Orchards) 的共同所有人，他站在西亚基马谷 (Yakima Valley) 的办公室里，面前是他的曾曾祖父母的肖像，他们于 1898 年创立了这家家族企业。Annie Warren/NWPB 隐藏标题栏

title_zh: 美国政府正在调查伊朗与多达 50 艘被黑客入侵的商船的关系
summary: The attacks, if officials who spoke to NPR are correct, may be the latest example of Iranian cyberattacks against global critical infrastructure during the war with the U.S.
summary_zh: 如果接受 NPR 采访的官员消息属实，这些攻击可能是伊朗在 2017 年针对全球关键基础设施进行网络攻击的最新例子。
body_en: In an aerial view, a container ship arrives at the Port of Oakland on Oct. 10, 2025 in Oakland, Calif. Justin Sullivan/Getty Images hide caption

The U.S. government has intelligence suggesting that up to 50 commercial shipping vessels were recently compromised by cyberattacks, activity federal officials are investigating as potentially linked to Iran.

That's according to a U.S. official familiar with the matter who was not authorized to speak on the record, a former military cyber operator and an industry executive briefed on the attacks. The series of breaches was first reported by the The Wall Street Journal .

The attacks against the maritime sector, if officials' suspicions are correct, may be the latest example of Iranian cyberattacks against global critical infrastructure during the ongoing war with the United States.
Iran denies it was behind cyber fridge attacks targeting France

NPR has reported that cybersecurity experts and U.S. officials believe Iranian hackers were responsible for a series of digital attacks against U.S. water treatment systems across the country in August as well as a pattern of attacks targeting refrigeration cooling systems that led to spoiled food at grocery stores on U.S. military bases and all across Europe as recently as early November.

The Coast Guard and the FBI first partnered in August to send a "highly specialized team" to board two different foreign commercial vessels "in the Gulf of America" heading to U.S. ports, according to a statement provided by the FBI and the Coast Guard. "The captain, crew, and shore-side corporate staff were critical partners in helping to ensure the threats were mitigated," according to the statement.
The FBI and Coast Guard press offices also told NPR that there are no current "reports of operational disruptions, vessel instability, physical danger to crews, or environmental impacts."
However, there are dozens more ships in international waters that the U.S. government believes have been compromised by hackers and many others who might be vulnerable to similar attacks.
A new cold war: hackers target fridges across the globe

According to the U.S. official familiar with the investigation, bad actors took advantage of known vulnerabilities in Fortinet FortiGate devices, which are frequently used in the maritime industry. The Coast Guard and FBI released a cyber bulletin in September warning the industry that bad actors were breaking into these devices, which help manage firewalls and virtual private networks. "Threat actors routinely scan for specific, unpatched vulnerabilities to gain a foothold," the bulletin read.

According to the U.S. official, in some cases, employees aboard the ships suspected something nefarious was going on when they noticed email disruptions or couldn't log in to their accounts, or, in at least one case, an extended communications blackout. The U.S. official declined to comment on how the U.S. government knows about the extent of breaches across the sector.

However, according to the U.S. official, hackers were able to break in using the Fortinet vulnerability and then pivot from the ships' IT systems over to their network of devices controlling physical processes on the ships, what's called operational technology.
Did Iran hack U.S. water systems? / Cyberwarfare abroad / Ukraine's air defense gap

The U.S. official said the bad actors "could have impacted the systems on board that control propulsion, steering, navigation, and cargo management," though they did not share any examples of that kind of activity occurring. In at least one case, one of the ships affected was an LNG tanker designed to transport liquified natural gas. It's important to keep systems at a certain temperature to prevent dangerous accidents if a ship's cargo includes explosive materials –from chemicals to fuel.

While commercial vessels are accustomed to physical security reviews entering the United States following the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks, digital threats are becoming all the more important to track as adversaries can break in and cause damage from afar. "It's a totally new paradigm that these tankers are networked in this way," the U.S. official said.

Even so, national security officials have feared something like this might happen for years. A former Navy official who requested anonymity to discuss internal operations tells NPR that "we had been tracking the possibility to exploit and take control of [operational technology] systems on Navy ships and Merchant [Marine] ships for a long time, and now this is coming to fruition."

While the U.S. government is wary of advertising Iranian hacking efforts during the war, officials also want to spread awareness of the vulnerability of internet connected devices, particularly those that are linked to the technology that controls critical processes. "These are not sophisticated attacks," the official said. "This is a known vulnerability that could be mitigated with some pretty basic cyber hygiene."
Are hacks of U.S. water facilities a new front in the Iran war?
body_zh: 从鸟瞰图中，一艘集装箱船于 2025 年 10 月 10 日抵达加利福尼亚州奥克兰的奥克兰港。Justin Sullivan/Getty Images 隐藏标题栏
美国政府的情报显示，多达 50 艘商船最近受到网络攻击，联邦官员正在调查这些活动是否可能与伊朗有关。
这是一位未获授权公开发言的知情美国官员、一名前军事网络运营商和一名听取了有关攻击情况简报的行业高管的说法。这一系列违规行为最先由《华尔街日报》报道。
如果官员们的怀疑正确的话，针对海事部门的攻击可能是伊朗在与美国持续战争期间针对全球关键基础设施进行网络攻击的最新例子。
伊朗否认是针对法国的网络冰箱攻击的幕后黑手
NPR 报道称，网络安全专家和美国官员认为，伊朗黑客对 8 月份在全国范围内针对美国水处理系统的一系列数字攻击以及针对制冷系统的一系列攻击负责，这些攻击导致美国军事基地和欧洲各地杂货店的食品变质。
根据联邦调查局和海岸警卫队提供的一份声明，海岸警卫队和联邦调查局于八月首次合作，派出一支“高度专业化的团队”登上“在美洲湾”前往美国港口的两艘不同的外国商船。声明称：“船长、船员和岸上公司员工是帮助确保减轻威胁的关键合作伙伴。”
联邦调查局和海岸警卫队新闻办公室还告诉 NPR，目前没有“有关运营中断、船只不稳定、船员人身危险或环境影响的报告”。
然而，美国政府认为国际水域还有数十艘船只受到黑客和其他许多可能容易受到类似攻击的船只的攻击。
新冷战：黑客瞄准全球冰箱
据了解调查情况的美国官员称，不法分子利用了 Fortinet FortiGate 设备中的已知漏洞，这些设备经常用于海事行业。海岸警卫队和联邦调查局 9 月份发布了一份网络公告，警告业界不良行为者正在侵入这些有助于管理防火墙和虚拟专用网络的设备。公告中写道：“威胁行为者会定期扫描特定的、未修补的漏洞以获得立足点。”
据美国官员称，在某些情况下，船上的员工在注意到电子邮件中断或无法登录帐户，或者至少在一种情况下，通讯中断时间延长时，就会怀疑发生了邪恶的事情。这位美国官员拒绝就美国政府如何了解整个行业的违规程度发表评论。
然而，据美国官员称，黑客能够利用 Fortinet 漏洞进行入侵，然后从船舶的 IT 系统转向控制船上物理过程的设备网络，即所谓的操作技术。
伊朗是否入侵了美国的供水系统？ / 国外网络战 / 乌克兰的防空差距
这位美国官员表示，不良行为者“可能会影响船上控制推进、转向、导航和货物管理的系统”，但他们没有分享任何发生此类活动的例子。至少在一个案例中，其中一艘受影响的船舶是一艘设计用于运输液化天然气的液化天然气油轮。如果船上的货物包含从化学品到燃料等爆炸性物质，则必须将系统保持在一定温度，以防止发生危险事故。
尽管商船在 9 月 11 日恐怖袭击后进入美国时已经习惯了物理安全审查，但数字威胁的追踪变得更加重要，因为对手可以从远处闯入并造成损害。这位美国官员表示：“这些油轮以这种方式联网，这是一个全新的范例。”
即便如此，国家安全官员多年来一直担心类似的事情可能发生。一位要求匿名讨论内部操作的前海军官员告诉美国公共广播电台，“我们长期以来一直在追踪利用和控制海军舰艇和商船[海军]舰艇[操作技术]系统的可能性，现在这一目标即将实现。”
尽管美国政府对宣传伊朗在战争期间的黑客活动持谨慎态度，但官员们也希望提高人们对互联网连接设备脆弱性的认识，特别是那些与控制关键流程的技术相关的设备。 “这些攻击并不复杂，”该官员表示。 “这是一个已知的漏洞，可以通过一些非常基本的网络卫生来缓解。”
对美国供水设施的黑客攻击是伊朗战争的新战线吗？

title_en: Schumer accuses Huang of violating US export control laws amid shipments of chips to China
title_zh: 舒默指责黄在向中国运送芯片的过程中违反了美国出口管制法
summary: Senate minority leader joins lawmakers from both parties outraged over Nvidia CEO’s reinstatement Chuck Schumer, the current Senate minority leader vying to lead the Democratic majority in the next Congress, accused Jensen Huang, the newly reinstated Nvidia CE
summary_zh: 参议院少数党领袖与两党议员一样对英伟达首席执行官查克·舒默(Chuck Schumer)复职感到愤怒，现任参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默(Chuck Schumer)
body_en: Senate minority leader joins lawmakers from both parties outraged over Nvidia CEO’s reinstatement

Chuck Schumer, the current Senate minority leader vying to lead the Democratic majority in the next Congress, accused Jensen Huang , the newly reinstated Nvidia CEO, of shipping “extremely advanced chips to China” and violating US export control laws.
On Tuesday, Schumer said the move “amounts to the equivalent of selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the space race”.
“This is an unfathomable failure of enforcement by the Trump administration ,” he said.

Nvidia’s board reinstated Huang on Monday after Donald Trump says he intervened on the executive’s behalf, assuring company leadership that he did not pose a national security risk despite questions surrounding his relationship with Alice Huang, a tech executive of no relation who has been accused of acting as a Chinese asset and routing advanced chips to Beijing via her datacenter company, Megaspeed.

Meanwhile, Huang’s reinstatement is “exhibit A” of the “political corruption and rot at the heart of the Trump administration’s big tech and AI policy”, Chris Van Hollen, the Maryland Democrat challenging Schumer to be the next Senate majority leader, told reporters Monday.

Van Hollen said he intends to focus on Huang’s “efforts to increase and accelerate the export of high-end chips to China, how he’s been accomplishing that, how he’s been getting his way with the administration” when the reinstalled executive appears before the Senate banking committee on 3 December.

It will be one of several appearances on Capitol Hill next week where skeptical lawmakers from both parties will grill Huang over his ties to a woman that some in the intelligence community have said was a spy for China. Huang will also sit for transcribed interviews with the House foreign affairs committee, as well as the select committee on the Chinese Communist party and the House intelligence committee.

“It’s completely hypocritical for the Trump administration, on the one hand, to say the reason we have to take all the brakes off AI development here at home is because China will leap ahead if we don’t,” Van Hollen said. “When in fact, it’s the Trump administration that’s helping China leap ahead.”

In an interview with CNBC on Monday, the US president defended his involvement in Huang’s reinstatement, arguing it would be a “bigger threat” for Nvidia to lose Huang’s “brain power” in the AI race. Trump also confirmed that he had provided the board with assurances regarding any national security concerns.
“I spoke to them, let me put it that way. And I convinced them,” Trump said.

Van Hollen pointed to a series of ties between Huang and Trumpworld as evidence of the executive’s influence over administration policy on advanced chips, including Nvidia’s $25m donation to Trump’s White House ballroom project, his personal holdings of Nvidia stock, Huang’s contribution to Trump’s inauguration fund and his attendance at a $1m-a-plate dinner at Mar-a-Lago.

The outrage spread on Capitol Hill on Monday. Gregory Meeks, a Democrat congressman from New York and the ranking member on the foreign affairs committee, called the decision “yet another example” of how “the wealthy and well connected are held to a different standard”.

John Curtis, a GOP senator from Utah, said that Huang was “right to step down” when news of his extramarital affair came to light. “Just 11 days after Nvidia announced his departure, the board brought him back while its own independent investigation was still under way. Last week, the board said it didn’t intend to reinstate him. I’d like to know what changed,” Curtis said.

For Matt Pearl, a director at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) who specializes in national security, geopolitics and technology, unanswered questions surrounding Huang’s conduct remain.
“We haven’t had an investigation,” Pearl said in an interview, noting that such a probe would normally take “at least a year”.
The Nvidia board, he argued, has instead relied on the “representations” of senior US government officials, including Trump himself, and is “essentially outsourcing the investigation”.

“I suspect that we’ll find out a lot more information in the coming weeks and months as Congress investigates, but it just seems that we have no idea what sort of the risks and threats were in this case,” Pearl said.
The episode, he added, could weaken how national security concerns are raised and acted upon inside government.
body_zh: 参议院少数党领袖与两党议员一起对英伟达首席执行官复职感到愤怒
现任参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默(Chuck Schumer)正在争夺下一届国会民主党多数党的席位，他指责新复任的英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋(Jensen Huang)“向中国运送极其先进的芯片”，并违反​​了美国出口管制法。
周二，舒默表示，此举“相当于在太空竞赛期间向苏联出售火箭发动机”。
他说：“这是特朗普政府执法方面的严重失败。”
周一，英伟达董事会恢复了黄的职位，此前唐纳德·特朗普表示，他代表这位高管进行了干预，并向公司领导层保证，尽管他与爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的关系存在疑问，但他不会构成国家安全风险。
与此同时，挑战舒默成为下一任参议院多数党领袖的马里兰州民主党人克里斯·范·霍伦(Chris Van Hollen)周一告诉记者，黄的复职是“特朗普政府大科技和人工智能政策核心的政治腐败和腐败”的“证据”。
范霍伦表示，当这位重新任命的高管于 12 月 3 日出现在参议院银行委员会面前时，他打算重点关注黄仁勋“增加和加速向中国出口高端芯片的努力，他是如何实现这一目标的，以及他如何与政府达成一致的”。
这将是下周在国会山举行的几次露面之一，两党持怀疑态度的议员将就黄与一名女性的关系进行盘问，情报界的一些人称这名女性是中国的间谍。黄还将参加众议院外交事务委员会、中国共产党特别委员会和众议院情报委员会的采访记录。
范霍伦说：“一方面，特朗普政府说我们必须在国内停止人工智能发展的原因是因为如果我们不这样做，中国就会取得飞跃，这完全是虚伪的。” “事实上，是特朗普政府正在帮助中国实现跨越式发展。”
在周一接受 CNBC 采访时，美国总统为自己参与黄仁勋的复职辩护，称在人工智能竞赛中失去黄仁勋的“脑力”对英伟达来说将是一个“更大的威胁”。特朗普还证实，他已就任何国家安全问题向董事会提供保证。
“我和他们谈过，让我这么说。我说服了他们，”特朗普说。
范·霍伦指出，黄仁勋和特朗普世界之间的一系列关系证明了这位高管对政府先进芯片政策的影响力，包括英伟达向特朗普的白宫宴会厅项目捐赠了 2500 万美元、他个人持有英伟达股票、黄仁勋对特朗普就职基金的捐款以及他出席海湖庄园每盘 100 万美元的晚宴。
周一，愤怒在国会山蔓延。纽约民主党国会议员、外交事务委员会高级成员格雷戈里·米克斯(Gregory Meeks)称，这一决定是“又一个例子”，说明“富人和人脉广泛的人如何受到不同的标准”。
犹他州共和党参议员约翰·柯蒂斯表示，当黄的婚外情消息曝光后，黄的下台是“正确的”。 “就在英伟达宣布他离职后 11 天，董事会就将他带回来，而其独立调查仍在进行中。上周，董事会表示不打算让他复职。我想知道发生了什么变化，”柯蒂斯说。
对于专门研究国家安全、地缘政治和技术的战略与国际研究中心 (CSIS) 主任马特·珀尔 (Matt Pearl) 来说，围绕黄的行为仍然存在未解之谜。
“我们还没有进行调查，”珀尔在接受采访时表示，并指出这样的调查通常需要“至少一年”。
他认为，英伟达董事会反而依赖包括特朗普本人在内的美国高级政府官员的“代表”，并且“基本上将调查外包”。
“我怀疑，随着国会的调查，我们会在未来几周和几个月内找到更多信息，但似乎我们不知道此案存在什么样的风险和威胁，”珀尔说。
他补充说，这一事件可能会削弱政府内部提出和采取行动的国家安全担忧的方式。

title_en: Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
title_zh: 特朗普命令联邦承包商在回应国会之前先与白宫核实
summary: President Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged
summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统指示联邦承包商和分包商就他们从国会收到的询问与他的政府进行磋商
body_en: President Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged

NEW YORK -- NEW YORK (AP) — President Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged, according to a new executive order .

The companies must also coordinate with the White House and U.S. agencies on “appropriate responses” to any such requests, the order issued late Friday says. If they fail to comply, the White House warns their contracts could be terminated and their future work with the federal government suspended.

The order is the Republican administration’s latest effort to resist what are expected to be wide-ranging and aggressive oversight efforts from Democrats when they take over Congress in January. Democrats have made government contracts one of their top investigative targets , noting that federal money has been flowing to companies linked with Trump’s family, particularly at the Pentagon.

White House officials have already begun taking steps to exert more control over how agencies and officials respond to congressional requests, anticipating there will be a flood of investigations initiated by Democrats.

Trump's counsel, Will Scharf, told federal agencies on Monday that they must seek approval from his office and the White House’s Office of Legislative Affairs before agreeing to appear before Congress. Scharf also suggested in a recent letter to Rep. Robert Garcia of California, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, that some congressional investigations may amount to “blatant criminality.”

Garcia sent letters this week directing members of Trump’s family and top administration officials to preserve documents. Scharf sought to dismiss the requests, noting in a letter to Democratic lawmakers that they are not yet in the majority and cannot compel compliance.

In a fact sheet , the White House framed the new requirements as “protecting executive privileges from congressional overreach,” arguing that some congressional leaders have tried to intrude on executive branch privileges by “harassing private companies that contract with the federal government.”

Presidents of both parties have long used executive privilege to resist congressional inquiries, but the claims can set up messy, protracted legal fights as parties dispute whether it applies. Executive privilege allows the president to keep information from the courts, Congress and the public to protect the confidentiality of White House deliberations, but the protection is far from absolute.
The latest executive order applies to all contractors and subcontractors, a universe of tens of thousands of businesses.

body_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统指示联邦承包商和分包商就他们从国会收到的询问与他的政府进行磋商，并保留白宫认为有特权的任何通信
纽约 - 纽约（美联社） - 根据一项新的行政命令，唐纳德·特朗普总统指示联邦承包商和分包商就国会提出的质询与他的政府进行磋商，并扣留任何白宫认为特权的通信。
该命令称，这些公司还必须与白宫和美国机构协调，对任何此类请求做出“适当回应”。如果他们不遵守规定，白宫警告他们的合同可能会被终止，并且他们未来与联邦政府的合作可能会暂停。
该命令是共和党政府为抵制民主党在一月份接管国会时预计将采取的广泛而积极的监督措施而采取的最新举措。民主党人已将政府合同作为其首要调查目标之一，并指出联邦资金一直流向与特朗普家族有联系的公司，尤其是五角大楼。
白宫官员已经开始采取措施，对各机构和官员如何回应国会要求施加更多控制，预计民主党将发起大量调查。
特朗普的律师威尔·沙夫周一告诉联邦机构，他们必须获得特朗普办公室和白宫立法事务办公室的批准，然后才能同意出席国会会议。沙夫还在最近给众议院监督委员会民主党领袖、加州众议员罗伯特·加西亚的一封信中表示，一些国会调查可能构成“公然犯罪”。
加西亚本周致函特朗普家族成员和高级政府官员保存文件。沙夫试图驳回这些要求，并在给民主党议员的一封信中指出，他们尚未占多数，无法强迫他们遵守。

title_en: Ex-White House AI adviser weighs in on national security as Huang is back as Nvidia CEO
title_zh: 黄仁勋重返英伟达首席执行官，前白宫人工智能顾问就国家安全问题发表看法
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back in leadership after resigning recently. Ben Buchanan, a Biden administration AI adviser, discusses what that means for U.S. national security and chip exports.
summary_zh: 英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在最近辞职后重新回到领导岗位。拜登政府人工智能顾问本·布坎南 (Ben Buchanan) 讨论了这对
body_en: Ex-White House AI adviser weighs in on national security as Huang is back as Nvidia CEO Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back in leadership after resigning recently. Ben Buchanan, a Biden administration AI adviser, discusses what that means for U.S. national security and chip exports.
Ex-White House AI advisor weighs in on national security as Huang is back as Nvidia CEO
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back in leadership after resigning recently. Ben Buchanan, a Biden administration AI adviser, discusses what that means for U.S. national security and chip exports.

We're going to stay on this topic. The Nvidia board said that it, quote, "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and is, quote, "confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk." President Trump has said that basically meant him, that he gave this input to the Nvidia board. We're going to talk this through with a former White House official. Ben Buchanan was special adviser for artificial intelligence during the Biden administration. Welcome to ALL THINGS CONSIDERED.
DETROW: What do you make of the White House's direct involvement here?

BUCHANAN: I'm surprised. Certainly, I was in the White House when Sam Altman had his firing and reinstatement, and I got a lot of questions then about, was the White House involved? And our posture was we did not want to live in a world in which the White House had roles in picking the executives of American companies. So it's certainly a departure from past norms in that regard.

DETROW: Yeah. I mean, there's a lot to ask about here. But I'm curious, from your past perspective as a White House official on this topic, is Nvidia as indispensable as it has been made out to be when it comes to the AI landscape, when it comes to the national security side of that?

BUCHANAN: Nvidia and their chips are absolutely incredibly important. To me, though, that reaffirms the importance of making sure those chips don't go to China more so than it reaffirms the importance of any one particular person. So my hope here is that because this technology matters so much, that Congress does a full investigation into the national security stakes of this, including were these chips being smuggled, was China accessing them remotely through data centers in Southeast Asia and the like? To me, that is really the crux of the national security matter in this instance.

DETROW: I want to go to the national security question at the heart of the Huang storyline. This is the reporting of this alleged relationship with an alleged Chinese espionage asset. What do you make of that particular part of the story?

BUCHANAN: It's hard to say from this vantage point of what's true and who knew what. Certainly, there's a lot of reporting that does seem to be credible that she was in the middle of chip smuggling and perhaps also had a relationship or ongoing conversations with the Ministry of State Security in China. To me, the chip smuggling part is enough reason for serious concern, and the intelligence links are secondary.

DETROW: What is the best way to frame how policy has changed from the Biden administration to the Trump administration when it comes to the accessibility of these chips in other countries, particularly China? Because that is an area where there's been a lot of reporting that Huang and Nvidia have had a lot of influence on President Trump.

BUCHANAN: We came into office in 2021 with the conviction that AI was going to get very powerful and that it would matter for national security and that it was chips, including Nvidia's chips, that were driving that increase in power. For that reason, in 2022, and then each subsequent year thereafter, we implemented and then tightened a series of export controls, denying China access to those chips and cutting off China smuggling routes and access to remote data centers in places like Singapore, containing those chips.

President Trump, when he came into office in 2025, walked back or declined to enforce a number of those policies - after initially talking and acting tough, walked those policies back in the late spring and summer of 2025 and then into the fall of 2025. To his credit, as this scandal broke, last week President Trump did put some rules back in place that, so far as we can tell, are still on the books that go back to something closer to the Biden administration policy.

DETROW: So when it comes to the policy of all of this, what do you think it may mean going forward if Jensen Huang is back in this perch with President Trump's full support, given the way that the two of them seem to have talked about these policies?

BUCHANAN: It really depends on what Congress does here. And because of President Trump's walk-back on this policy during his first two years, there has been a bipartisan move in Congress, including from some very MAGA senators - folks like Pete Ricketts and Jim Banks and Tom Cotton - to tighten the export controls once more, this time through legislation, depriving the administration of the opportunity to change these policies back and forth. Those bills - the MATCH Act, the OVERWATCH Act - are the two big ones - have bipartisan support, I think have a good chance of passing this Congress. And some of the leaders of those bills have come out today after this news and said they still have a lot of questions for Jensen, and they seem committed still to implementing this policy fully.
DETROW: That's Ben Buchanan, professor at Johns Hopkins University and a former AI adviser to the Biden White House. His new book about all of this is called "The Bitter Struggle." Thanks so much.

body_zh: 前白宫人工智能顾问黄仁勋回归国家安全，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在最近辞职后重新担任领导职务。拜登政府人工智能顾问本·布坎南讨论了这对美国国家安全和芯片出口意味着什么。
前白宫人工智能顾问黄仁勋重新担任英伟达首席执行官后，他对国家安全问题发表了看法
英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在最近辞职后重新回到领导岗位。拜登政府人工智能顾问本·布坎南讨论了这对美国国家安全和芯片出口意味着什么。
我们将继续讨论这个话题。英伟达董事会表示，它“收到了美国政府高层的意见”，并“相信黄先生的复职不会构成国家安全风险”。特朗普总统表示，这基本上是指他自己，他向英伟达董事会提供了这一意见。我们将与一位前白宫官员讨论这个问题。本·布坎南 (Ben Buchanan) 在拜登政府期间担任人工智能特别顾问。欢迎来到所有考虑的事情。
德特罗：您如何看待白宫的直接参与？
布坎南：我很惊讶。当然，当萨姆·奥尔特曼被解雇和复职时，我正在白宫，当时我有很多问题，白宫是否参与其中？我们的立场是，我们不想生活在一个白宫在挑选美国公司高管方面发挥作用的世界。因此，这肯定背离了这方面过去的规范。
德特罗：是的。我的意思是，这里有很多事情要问。但我很好奇，从您过去作为白宫官员的角度来看，在人工智能领域、在国家安全方面，英伟达是否像人们所认为的那样不可或缺？
BUCHANAN：Nvidia 及其芯片绝对非常重要。不过，对我来说，这再次证明了确保这些芯片不会流向中国的重要性，这比它再次证明了任何一个特定人的重要性还要重要。因此，我的希望是，由于这项技术非常重要，因此国会能够对其国家安全风险进行全面调查，包括这些芯片是否被走私，中国是否通过东南亚等地的数据中心远程访问它们？对我来说，这确实是本次事件中国家安全问题的症结所在。
德特罗：我想谈谈黄的故事情节的核心国家安全问题。这是对与所谓的中国间谍资产的所谓关系的报道。你对这个故事的特定部分有何看法？
布坎南：从这个角度很难说什么是真实的，谁知道什么。当然，有很多看起来确实可信的报道称，她正在进行芯片走私，并且可能与中国国家安全部有关系或正在进行对话。对我来说，芯片走私部分就足以引起严重关注，情报环节是次要的。
DETROW：当谈到这些芯片在其他国家（尤其是中国）的可及性时，最好的方式是什么来描述从拜登政府到特朗普政府的政策变化？因为在这个领域，有很多报道称黄仁勋和英伟达对特朗普总统产生了很大的影响。
布坎南：我们于 2021 年上任时坚信人工智能将变得非常强大，这对国家安全至关重要，而芯片，包括 Nvidia 的芯片，正在推动这种能力的增长。因此，在 2022 年以及此后的每一年，我们实施并加强了一系列出口管制，拒绝中国获得这些芯片，并切断中国的走私路线以及对新加坡等地包含这些芯片的远程数据中心的访问。
特朗普总统在 2025 年上任时，收回或拒绝执行其中一些政策 - 在最初言行强硬之后，在 2025 年春末和夏末，然后到 2025 年秋季，收回了这些政策。值得赞扬的是，随着这起丑闻的爆发，特朗普总统上周确实恢复了一些规则，据我们所知，这些规则仍然在记录中，这些规则与拜登政府的政策更接近。
德特罗：那么，当谈到所有这一切的政策时，考虑到他们两人似乎谈论这些政策的方式，如果黄仁勋在特朗普总统的全力支持下重新回到这个位置，你认为这可能意味着什么？

布坎南：这实际上取决于国会在这里做什么。由于特朗普总统在上任的头两年对这项政策做出了让步，国会中出现了两党共同采取的行动，其中包括一些非常崇尚 MAGA 的参议员——比如皮特·里基茨 (Pete Ricketts)、吉姆·班克斯 (Jim Banks) 和汤姆·科顿 (Tom Cotton)——再次收紧出口管制，这次是通过立法，从而剥夺了政府来回改变这些政策的机会。这些法案——《比赛法案》和《监督法案》——是两项重大法案——得到了两党的支持，我认为很有可能在本届国会获得通过。这些法案的一些领导人今天在得知这一消息后站出来表示，他们仍然对詹森有很多问题，而且他们似乎仍然致力于全面实施这项政策。
德特罗：这是本·布坎南 (Ben Buchanan)，约翰·霍普金斯大学教授、拜登白宫前人工智能顾问。他关于这一切的新书叫做《痛苦的斗争》。非常感谢。
