title_en: Army to detonate unstable explosives in Iowa Wednesday morning
title_zh: 上诉法院为陆军引爆爱荷华州炸药扫清道路
summary: A federal appeals court on Monday declined to block the Army from detonating explosives containing lead azide at a munitions plant in Iowa.
summary_zh: 周一，联邦上诉法院拒绝阻止陆军在爱荷华州一家军工厂引爆含有叠氮化铅的炸药。
body_en: The Army is set to detonate 5 tons of explosives containing lead azide at a munitions plant in Iowa on Wednesday morning after a back-and-forth that has played out between politicians and in court.

The detonation will take place at 9 a.m. Central time, acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle said Tuesday at a press conference. Telle said the unstable explosives become more dangerous as temperatures drop, and the weather forecast for Wednesday is "ideal to protect public health and safety across the region."

"Inaction is no longer an option," Army Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley, the commander of the operation, said Tuesday. "It would be irresponsible for us to not take the determined, consensus-based course of action moving forward."
The government has argued the detonation — which is expected to send a plume of toxic lead particles into the surrounding area — is necessary because the lead azide could spontaneously explode.

"There is consensus across the experts, across the country, that a controlled mitigated detonation of the lead azide here at Iowa Army Ammunition Plant is far preferable to an uncontrolled, spontaneous detonation of that substance," Telle said Tuesday.

In a social media post late Tuesday night , Telle said that federal authorities had constructed "earth berms, large sand-filled blocks" and what he described as a "water wall" filled with 100,000 gallons of water, all designed to "mitigate the effects of the blast."

"After the detonation, residents near the plant may see dark smoke," Telle wrote. "That smoke comes from explosives like C4 and diesel fuel, which are being used to direct the blast safely downward. Both are standard materials the Army burns every day."
Telle said that air quality would "be monitored throughout the operation and well into the day."

A federal appeals court on Monday declined to block the Army from detonating the explosives. The court's ruling came after environmental groups challenged the validity of the emergency permit granted by the Environmental Protection Agency and argued the EPA hadn't given enough notice to residents.
Following the ruling, the Army noted Monday night that current Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds "has given her support to go forward."

"It is the unanimous judgement of our people — the Army, Navy, EPA, ATF, FBI, DARPA, DoE, CDC, HHS, FEMA and every other agency involved — that the Army should proceed with an extensively mitigated, carefully controlled detonation, which will occur this Wednesday morning, as previously scheduled, based on forecast wind conditions," Telle said on X .

The 8th Circuit Court of Appeals temporarily blocked the detonation last week to give itself time to issue a longer-lasting ruling. On Monday, the court said the environmental groups that challenged the plan had failed to show they are likely to succeed.

"We are mindful of the very real risks presented by the Army's planned detonation of the stores of degraded lead azide," the ruling said. "However, we must acknowledge the realities of the situation: the degraded explosives present a risk of an uncontrolled and unplanned explosion, which would occur without the benefit of the safety measures that the Permit puts in place."

President Trump said earlier Monday the government would not carry out the detonation until the appeals court ruled and unless Democratic Iowa Gov.-elect Rob Sand signed off. Mr. Trump added that government experts felt detonating the material was the best option.

"If [Sand] or the Courts do not agree, we will have no choice but to not proceed with the controlled removal of these hazardous materials, and be forced to hold the incoming Governor responsible for any and all death or destruction caused by this very unfortunate, and longterm, situation," the president said on social media.

Sand, whose input was not required and who is not yet in office, said on social media the Trump administration "should make this decision based on the information they have from the people they brought in to do the job months ago and have been on the ground in Middletown for weeks."
"Everyday Iowans are entitled to know how Middletown came to this situation, and learn why the administration believes this is the best path forward," Sand said.

The government has argued that even if the appeals court had stayed its EPA permit, the Army has the legal right to move forward without a permit to "respond to the immediate threat of an uncontrolled explosion."

The Army has stored the lead azide in earthen-covered containers for decades at its ammunition plant in Middletown, a small town located near the Mississippi River in southeastern Iowa. The EPA has said the government discovered earlier this year that the material deteriorated over time, risking explosion if it is moved or disturbed.
The Pentagon asked the Massachusetts Institute of Technology's Lincoln Laboratory to study the detonation plan, officials told CBS News.
body_zh: 经过政客和法庭之间的争执后，陆军定于周三上午在爱荷华州的一家军工厂引爆含有叠氮化铅的 5 吨炸药。
代理陆军部长 Adam Telle 在周二的新闻发布会上表示，爆炸将于中部时间上午 9 点进行。泰勒表示，随着气温下降，不稳定的爆炸物变得更加危险，周三的天气预报“对于保护整个地区的公众健康和安全来说是理想的”。
该行动指挥官、陆军少将埃里克·雪利周二表示：“无所作为已不再是一种选择。” “如果我们不采取坚定的、基于共识的行动方针向前推进，那将是不负责任的行为。”
政府辩称，这次爆炸是必要的，因为叠氮化铅可能会自发爆炸，预计爆炸将向周围地区发射大量有毒铅颗粒。
特勒周二表示：“全国各地的专家一致认为，在爱荷华州陆军弹药厂对叠氮化铅进行受控缓和爆炸，远比该物质不受控制的自发爆炸要好得多。”
特勒在周二深夜的社交媒体帖子中表示，联邦当局建造了“土堤、大型填沙块”以及他所说的装有 10 万加仑水的“水墙”，所有这些都是为了“减轻爆炸的影响”。
“爆炸后，工厂附近的居民可能会看到黑烟，”特勒写道。 “烟雾来自 C4 和柴油等炸药，它们被用来安全向下引导爆炸。这两种都是陆军每天燃烧的标准材料。”
泰勒表示，空气质量将“在整个运营过程中一直受到监控，直至当天”。
联邦上诉法院周一拒绝阻止陆军引爆爆炸物。法院做出这一裁决之前，环保组织对环境保护局授予的紧急许可证的有效性提出质疑，并认为环保局没有向居民发出足够的通知。
裁决后，陆军周一晚间指出，现任爱荷华州州长金·雷诺兹“已支持继续前进”。
“我们的人民——陆军、海军、美国环保署、烟酒枪械管理局、联邦调查局、美国国防部高级研究计划局、美国能源部、疾病预防控制中心、美国卫生与公众服务部、联邦紧急事务管理署以及所有其他相关机构——的一致判断是，陆军应该根据预测的风况，按照先前的计划，在本周三早上进行广泛缓解、精心控制的爆炸，”陆军代理部长亚当·特尔说。
第八巡回上诉法院上周暂时阻止了爆炸，以便有时间做出更持久的裁决。周一，法院表示，质疑该计划的环保组织未能表明他们有可能成功。
裁决称：“我们注意到陆军计划引爆储存的降解叠氮化铅所带来的非常现实的风险。” “然而，我们必须承认现实情况：降解的爆炸物存在失控和计划外爆炸的风险，如果没有许可证所采取的安全措施，这种情况就会发生。”
特朗普总统周一早些时候表示，在上诉法院做出裁决之前，除非民主党爱荷华州当选州长罗布·桑德签字同意，否则政府不会实施爆炸。特朗普补充说，政府专家认为引爆这些材料是最好的选择。
总统在社交媒体上表示：“如果[桑德]或法院不同意，我们将别无选择，只能不继续有控制地清除这些有害物质，并被迫让即将上任的州长对这种非常不幸和长期的情况造成的任何和所有死亡或破坏负责。”
桑德并未被要求提供意见，而且尚未上任，他在社交媒体上表示，特朗普政府“应该根据他们从几个月前聘请的人员那里获得的信息做出这一决定，这些人已经在米德尔敦工作了数周。”
桑德说：“爱荷华州人民每天都有权了解米德尔敦是如何陷入这种情况的，并了解为什么政府认为这是最好的前进道路。”
政府辩称，即使上诉法院暂缓了美国环保局的许可，陆军也有合法权利在没有许可的情况下继续前进，以“应对失控爆炸的直接威胁”。陆军警告说，需要在寒冷的天气导致叠氮化铅晶体分解从而更有可能发生自爆之前采取行动。
几十年来，陆军一直将叠氮化铅储存在位于爱荷华州东南部密西西比河附近的小镇米德尔敦的弹药厂的土制容器中。美国环保署表示，政府今年早些时候发现，这种材料会随着时间的推移而变质，如果移动或受到干扰，就有爆炸的危险。
官员们告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，五角大楼要求麻省理工学院林肯实验室研究爆炸计划。

title_en: Kilmar Abrego Garcia leaves U.S. for Spain
title_zh: 基尔马·阿布雷戈·加西亚离开美国前往西班牙
summary: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, the El Salvador native who was mistakenly deported last year, left the U.S. for Spain on Tuesday, the Department of Homeland Security confirmed.
summary_zh: 美国国土安全部称，去年被错误驱逐出境的萨尔瓦多人基尔马·阿布雷戈·加西亚于周二离开美国前往西班牙
body_en: Kilmar Abrego Garcia leaves U.S., heads to Spain - CBS News

Kilmar Abrego Garcia, the El Salvador native who was mistakenly deported last year and sent to a notorious prison in his home country, left the U.S. for Spain on Tuesday, the Department of Homeland Security confirmed.
CBS News was first to report Abrego Garcia's plans earlier Tuesday.

Abrego Garcia, whose case became an early flashpoint in the debate over the Trump administration's deportation crackdown, was flying to Spain on a commercial flight, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter, who requested anonymity to talk about an arrangement that has not been disclosed publicly.

The exact nature of his arrangements and the conditions of his departure from the U.S. were not immediately clear. But the federal judge in Maryland overseeing his civil legal case issued an order Friday that remains sealed.

"We are delighted to announce that Kilmar Abrego Garcia has self-deported from the United States to Spain," Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said. He reiterated the Trump administration's allegation that Abrego Garcia belongs to a gang — which his legal team has denied — and said he now "cannot terrorize innocent Americans."

In a social media post late Tuesday night, the Department of Homeland Security wrote: "To be clear: Kilmar Abrego Garcia departed the United States pursuant to a removal order. He paid for his own flight and received no incentives. He will NEVER be allowed back inside the United States."
CBS News has reached out to an attorney and representatives for Abrego Garcia.

The move by Abrego Garcia comes after the Trump administration spent months trying to deport the man, who came to the U.S. illegally 15 years ago and had been living in Maryland with his wife and children when he was detained by immigration authorities in March 2025. He was then deported to El Salvador and held for months in the country's CECOT prison, despite a previous court order barring him from being sent back to his home country. He was brought back to the United States last year to face criminal charges.

Abrego Garcia has maintained for more than a year that if he had to leave the U.S. again, he would be willing to go to Costa Rica, and designated the Central American nation as his preferred country of removal.

But the Trump administration had resisted that suggestion and instead unsuccessfully sought to deport Abrego Garcia to numerous African countries, including Uganda, Eswatini and Ghana. In more recent months, DHS said it was ready to deport Abrego Garcia to Liberia — part of a broader practice of sending deportees to countries in Africa.

Abrego Garcia's departure from the U.S. came weeks after a hearing before U.S. District Judge Paula Xinis, who has been presiding over a civil case stemming from his deportation last year, was abruptly cancelled . The judge ordered Immigration and Customs Enforcement last year to release Abrego Garcia from immigration custody and has continued to bar immigration authorities from detaining him while litigation continued.

But the Trump administration had sought to lift Xinis' orders, which it said were the only impediments to Abrego Garcia's "prompt removal." The Justice Department said in March that the government was "ready, willing, and able" to deport Abrego Garcia to Liberia in West Africa.

Abrego Garcia's case gained national prominence last year after a top administration official acknowledged that his removal to El Salvador was an "error." Following his arrest by immigration authorities in March 2025, Abrego Garcia was among the more than 200 immigrants who were sent to El Salvador and detained at its notorious supermax prison, the Terrorism Confinement Center, or CECOT.

But Abrego Garcia had been granted a withholding of removal by an immigration judge in 2019, which prevented immigration authorities from deporting him to his home country of El Salvador because he was at risk of persecution by local gangs.

In April 2025, Xinis ordered the Department of Homeland Security to bring Abrego Garcia back to the U.S., and the Supreme Court said the government had to facilitate his release from Salvadoran custody.

The Trump administration ultimately brought Abrego Garcia back to the U.S. in June 2025, but only after he was indicted on federal charges of human smuggling stemming from a 2022 traffic stop in Tennessee. Abrego Garcia pleaded not guilty and in May, a federal judge in Tennessee dismissed the criminal charges on the grounds that his prosecution was vindictive.
The Justice Department has appealed that decision , and arguments before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 6th Circuit are scheduled for February.
This story published first on CBS News at 5:06 p.m. on Nov. 24, 2026.

美国国土安全部证实，萨尔瓦多人基尔马·阿布雷戈·加西亚(Kilmar Abrego Garcia)去年被错误驱逐出境，并被送往祖国一所臭名昭著的监狱，周二离开美国前往西班牙。
周二早些时候，哥伦比亚广播公司新闻首先报道了阿布雷戈·加西亚的计划。
据多位知情人士透露，阿布雷戈·加西亚（Abrego Garcia）的案件成为特朗普政府驱逐出境镇压争论的早期热点，他当时正乘坐商业航班飞往西班牙，他们要求匿名谈论一项尚未公开披露的安排。
他的安排的确切性质以及他离开美国的条件尚不清楚。但马里兰州负责监督他的民事法律案件的联邦法官周五发布了一项命令，该命令目前仍处于密封状态。
“我们很高兴地宣布基尔马·阿布雷戈·加西亚已从美国自行驱逐到西班牙，”国土安全部部长马克韦恩·穆林说。他重申了特朗普政府关于阿布雷戈·加西亚属于一个团伙的指控——他的法律团队否认了这一点——并表示他现在“不能恐吓无辜的美国人”。
美国国土安全部在周二深夜的社交媒体帖子中写道：“需要明确的是：基尔马·阿布雷戈·加西亚是根据驱逐令离开美国的。他支付了自己的机票费用，并且没有得到任何奖励。他永远不会被允许返回美国境内。”
哥伦比亚广播公司新闻已联系阿布雷戈·加西亚的律师和代表。
阿布雷戈·加西亚 (Abrego Garcia) 采取这一举措之前，特朗普政府花了数月时间试图驱逐这名男子。这名男子 15 年前非法来到美国，2025 年 3 月被移民当局拘留时，一直与妻子和孩子住在马里兰州。随后，他被驱逐到萨尔瓦多，并在该国的 CECOT 监狱关押了数月，尽管此前法院曾下令禁止他被遣返回国。去年他被带回美国接受刑事指控。
阿布雷戈·加西亚一年多来一直坚称，如果他必须再次离开美国，他愿意去哥斯达黎加，并指定这个中美洲国家为他首选的驱逐国。
但特朗普政府拒绝了这一建议，而是试图将阿布雷戈·加西亚驱逐到包括乌干达、斯威士兰和加纳在内的许多非洲国家，但没有成功。最近几个月，国土安全部表示准备将阿布雷戈·加西亚驱逐到利比里亚，这是将被驱逐者送往非洲国家的更广泛做法的一部分。
阿布雷戈·加西亚 (Abrego Garcia) 离开美国几周前，美国地区法官宝拉·西尼斯 (Paula Xinis) 主持的一场听证会突然取消，该法官一直在主持因阿布雷戈·加西亚 (Abrego Garcia) 去年被驱逐出境而引发的民事案件。法官去年下令移民和海关执法局将阿布雷戈·加西亚从移民拘留所释放，并继续禁止移民当局在诉讼继续期间拘留他。
但特朗普政府曾试图取消西尼斯的命令，并称这是“迅速撤职”阿布雷戈·加西亚的唯一障碍。司法部三月份表示，政府“准备好、愿意并且有能力”将阿布雷戈·加西亚驱逐到西非的利比里亚。
去年，在一名高级政府官员承认将阿布雷戈·加西亚驱逐到萨尔瓦多是一个“错误”后，阿布雷戈·加西亚的案件引起了全国关注。 2025 年 3 月，阿布雷戈·加西亚 (Abrego Garcia) 被移民当局逮捕，他是被送往萨尔瓦多并被拘留在臭名昭著的超级监狱、恐怖主义监禁中心 (CECOT) 的 200 多名移民之一。
但阿布雷戈·加西亚 (Abrego Garcia) 于 2019 年获得移民法官的暂缓递解令，这使得移民当局无法将他驱逐回祖国萨尔瓦多，因为他面临受到当地帮派迫害的风险。
2025 年 4 月，希尼斯命令国土安全部将阿布雷戈·加西亚带回美国，最高法院表示政府必须协助他从萨尔瓦多的拘留中获释。
特朗普政府最终于 2025 年 6 月将阿布雷戈·加西亚带回美国，但前提是他因 2022 年田纳西州一次交通堵塞而被联邦指控人口走私。阿布雷戈·加西亚（Abrego Garcia）不认罪，五月，田纳西州的一名联邦法官驳回了刑事指控，理由是对他的起诉是报复性的。
司法部已对该决定提出上诉，美国第六巡回上诉法院定于 2 月份进行辩论。

title_en: Maps show how far lead dust from Iowa detonation could travel
title_zh: 地图显示爱荷华州爆炸产生的铅尘可以传播多远
summary: Maps of the planned lead azide detonation in Middletown show the shaded area stretching from near Burlington toward Macon, Missouri, by noon Wednesday. The forecasts will change with the weather.
summary_zh: 计划在米德尔敦进行叠氮化铅爆炸的地图显示，截至周三中午，阴影区域从伯灵顿附近一直延伸到密苏里州梅肯
body_en: Maps show Iowa lead dust plume drifting southwest into Missouri Wednesday after detonation, Army shares - CBS News
New maps of the Army's planned lead azide detonation in southeast Iowa show a plume of toxic dust drifting southwest toward northeast Missouri between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. Wednesday.

The Army plans to detonate about 5 tons of degraded lead azide, in 68 barrels, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown at 9 a.m. Wednesday, the day before Thanksgiving, according to an emergency alert sent to cellphones Tuesday morning. The alert said some people within 5 miles southwest of the plant may be evacuated and told people up to 20 miles away to stay indoors with windows closed. Officials expect the wind to blow southwest, away from Burlington, a city of just under 25,000 people on the Mississippi River.
The last controlled detonation of lead azide happened in 1977.

The Army moved the detonation from Friday, citing more favorable wind and time to add safety measures, according to a government court filing. A federal appeals court cleared the way Monday for the detonation after it had been delayed several times amid lawsuits from environmental groups and concerns from elected officials in Illinois and Iowa.

The maps show the modeled lead dust from 9 a.m. until 5 p.m. Wednesday. At 9 a.m., a red circle is centered near the plant. By 9:45 a.m., the shaded area becomes a long oval running from near Burlington southwest toward the Missouri line.

By early afternoon, the shaded area stretches far into northeast Missouri, passing Knox City. By late afternoon, it narrows to a band running from the Burlington and Keokuk area toward Macon, Missouri, with Quincy, Illinois, just southeast of it.

Wind arrows on the maps point southwest. Illinois officials said Monday that NOAA's latest model showed no Illinois counties would be affected. The Illinois EPA had asked the Army for updated modeling but had not received it, officials said, and Gov. JB Pritzker has directed state agencies to remain on alert .
Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe said state agencies are setting up additional monitoring of air and water quality.

The maps are forecasts and will change with the weather. Under the EPA's permit, the Army must update its plume forecasts six hours before the detonation and hourly after that until it is finished. The Army's forecasts do not establish that harmful exposure will occur at every location inside a projected plume, and sampling will be needed to show where lead settles on farmland, playgrounds and other surfaces.
Officials recommend that people stay indoors during the detonation and rinse outdoor surfaces with water afterward.
The USDA estimates 250 farms could be impacted by the detonation.

"If we don't have a healthy herd, we don't have a healthy paycheck," said Steve Lucie, Iowa cattle farmer. "We're very concerned about what that's going to do to the health of our soil and our livestock."
Why the Army is detonating the lead azide, and the pushback
"Inaction is no longer an option," said Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley, who leads the operation.

The Army says the lead azide has been stored at the plant for more than 20 years in earthen-covered containers, in a bath of ethanol and water meant to keep it stable. A routine check this year found some of the water had evaporated, and the material has since recrystallized , making it increasingly sensitive to friction and shock. Army officials say moving the barrels now risks setting them off, and experts say the stockpile will become more volatile as temperatures cool, since less liquid in the barrels makes the solution more prone to freezing, which raises the risk of a chain reaction.

The Army has added blast barriers around the bunkers where the lead azide will be detonated, plans to apply ballistic gels and foams to absorb dust, and will douse the materials with thousands of gallons of water. Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle said the goal is to keep as much of the dust as possible on the plant's grounds. The Army considered "every viable solution," he said, and concluded a controlled detonation is safest. The EPA issued an emergency permit for the detonation Nov. 13.

The plan has drawn criticism from both parties. A bipartisan group of Illinois and Iowa elected officials asked the Army and EPA to delay it and look for safer alternatives, citing poor communication with the public. Sen. Tammy Duckworth, an Illinois Democrat, called the operation a "failure of leadership of epic proportions." Earthjustice sued on behalf of the Iowa Environmental Council and the Sierra Club's Iowa chapter, challenging the validity of the EPA's emergency permit. The 8th Circuit Court of Appeals temporarily blocked the detonation last week, then declined Monday to stop it, saying the groups had not shown they were likely to succeed and that the degraded explosives risk an uncontrolled blast without the permit's safety measures. The judges said the Army evaluated "a full range" of alternatives, including neutralizing the lead azide with other chemicals and thermal treatment.

President Trump said on social media that in addition to the court's go-ahead, he wanted Gov.-elect Rob Sand to approve the detonation. Sand, a Democrat who takes office in January, has said the decision is fully up to the administration. Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds said Tuesday she supports the plan after speaking with military leaders.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
body_zh: 地图显示爱荷华州铅尘羽在爆炸后周三向西南方向飘入密苏里州，陆军分享 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
陆军计划在爱荷华州东南部进行叠氮化铅爆炸的新地图显示，上午 9 点至下午 5 点之间，一股有毒尘埃向西南方向飘向密苏里州东北部。周三。
根据周二早上发送到手机的紧急警报，陆军计划于感恩节前一天周三上午 9 点在米德尔敦的爱荷华州陆军弹药厂引爆 68 桶约 5 吨降解叠氮化铅。警报称，工厂西南 5 英里范围内的一些人可能会被疏散，并告诉 20 英里以内的人们待在室内并关闭窗户。官员们预计风将吹向西南方向，远离密西西比河沿岸一座人口不到 25,000 人的城市伯灵顿。
最后一次叠氮化铅受控爆炸发生在 1977 年。
根据政府法庭文件，陆军以更有利的风向和增加安全措施的时间为由，从周五推迟了爆炸。由于环保组织的诉讼以及伊利诺伊州和爱荷华州民选官员的担忧，爆炸多次被推迟，周一，一家联邦上诉法院为爆炸扫清了道路。
地图显示了上午 9 点到下午 5 点的铅尘模型。周三。上午 9 点，工厂附近出现一个红色圆圈。到上午 9 点 45 分，阴影区域变成一个长椭圆形，从伯灵顿附近西南向密苏里线延伸。
到了下午早些时候，阴影区域一直延伸到密苏里州东北部，经过诺克斯城。到了下午晚些时候，它缩小为一条从伯灵顿和基奥卡克地区向密苏里州梅肯延伸的带，其东南部是伊利诺伊州昆西。
地图上的风向箭头指向西南方向。伊利诺伊州官员周一表示，美国国家海洋和大气管理局的最新模型显示，伊利诺伊州没有县会受到影响。官员们表示，伊利诺伊州环保局已要求陆军提供更新的模型，但尚未收到，州长 JB Pritzker 已指示各州机构保持警惕。
密苏里州州长迈克·基霍表示，州机构正在对空气和水质进行额外的监测。
这些地图是预测的，会随着天气而变化。根据美国环保局的许可，陆军必须在爆炸前六小时和爆炸后每小时更新其羽流预报，直到爆炸结束。陆军的预测并未确定预计羽流内的每个位置都会发生有害暴露，因此需要进行采样以显示铅沉积在农田、游乐场和其他表面的位置。
官员建议人们在爆炸期间呆在室内，然后用水冲洗室外表面。
美国农业部估计 250 个农场可能受到爆炸影响。
“如果我们没有健康的牛群，我们就没有健康的薪水，”爱荷华州的养牛户史蒂夫·卢西说。 “我们非常担心这会对我们的土壤和牲畜的健康造成什么影响。”
为什么陆军要引爆叠氮化铅，以及阻力
“无所作为已不再是一种选择，”领导该行动的埃里克·雪利少将说。
陆军表示，叠氮化铅已在工厂的土制容器中储存了 20 多年，并浸泡在乙醇和水中，以保持其稳定。今年的一次例行检查发现，一些水已经蒸发，并且材料已经重新结晶，使其对摩擦和冲击越来越敏感。陆军官员表示，现在移动这些桶可能会引爆它们，专家表示，随着气温下降，库存将变得更加不稳定，因为桶中液体较少，使得溶液更容易冻结，从而增加了连锁反应的风险。
陆军在将引爆叠氮化铅的掩体周围增加了防爆屏障，计划使用防弹凝胶和泡沫来吸收灰尘，并将用数千加仑的水浸泡这些材料。代理陆军部长亚当·泰勒表示，我们的目标是尽可能多地保留工厂场地上的灰尘。他说，陆军考虑了“每一个可行的解决方案”，并得出结论，受控爆炸是最安全的。美国环保署于 11 月 13 日颁发了爆炸紧急许可证。

该计划遭到了双方的批评。由伊利诺伊州和爱荷华州民选官员组成的两党团体要求陆军和环保局推迟这一计划，并寻找更安全的替代方案，理由是与公众沟通不畅。伊利诺伊州民主党参议员塔米·达克沃斯 (Tammy Duckworth) 称这次行动是“史无前例的领导失败”。地球正义代表爱荷华州环境委员会和塞拉俱乐部爱荷华州分会提起诉讼，质疑美国环保局紧急许可证的有效性。第八巡回上诉法院上周暂时阻止了爆炸，然后周一拒绝阻止爆炸，称这些组织没有表明他们有可能成功，并且如果没有许可证的安全措施，降解的炸药可能会发生失控的爆炸。法官们表示，陆军评估了“全方位”的替代方案，包括用其他化学品中和叠氮化铅以及热处理。
特朗普总统在社交媒体上表示，除了法院的批准外，他还希望当选州长罗布·桑德批准爆炸。一月份上任的民主党人桑德表示，这一决定完全取决于政府。爱荷华州州长金雷诺兹周二在与军方领导人交谈后表示支持该计划。
美联社对此报道作出了贡献。

title_en: Canadian astronaut's wife gives birth with husband aboard ISS
title_zh: 加拿大宇航员的妻子与丈夫在国际空间站上生下孩子
summary: The wife of Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk, who is currently aboard the International Space Station, gave birth to the couple's third child, Canadian officials announced.
summary_zh: 目前正在国际空间站上的加拿大宇航员约书亚·库特里克的妻子生下了这对夫妇的第三个孩子，Canadia
body_en: Wife of Canadian astronaut aboard International Space Station gives birth to couple's third child - CBS News
The wife of a Canadian astronaut who is currently aboard the International Space Station gave birth Tuesday to the couple's third child, Canadian officials announced.
Heather Kutryk, the wife of astronaut Joshua Kutryk, gave birth to a girl, the Canadian Space Agency said in a news release.
"Heather and baby are both doing well," the agency said, adding that Joshua Kutryk was able to share in the experience from the space station.

"Joshua is currently living out a childhood dream aboard the International Space Station," the couple said in a statement. "Even with the distance between us, we feel incredibly connected as we welcome our new little star into our lives."
The couple's two other children are ages 7 and 5.
Joshua Kutryk traveled to the space station on Oct. 1 from Florida aboard a SpaceX Crew Dragon capsule as part of Crew 13, accompanied by two NASA astronauts and a Russian cosmonaut.
In an interview just prior to his departure, he told CBS News that it would be tough to miss the birth, but that he would "try to take the positive things out of it."

"Physically, of course, I won't be here, but as hard as that will be, it also lends itself to what I hope will be a very unique and enriching life experience that we'll look on fondly," Joshua Kutryk said.

In the history of space travel, Joshua Kutryk is just the fourth astronaut to miss the birth of a child. A former military test pilot, this was Kutryk's first spaceflight. He is the 17th Canadian to fly in space.

"We have an enormous support network, and we feel just happy and joyful to be doing this," he said in that interview. "This is a hard job. There's a lot of good things about it, there's some bad things. One of those bad things is that it's very unpredictable, and you can't predict when things like launches are going to happen."
Crew 13 does not yet have a confirmed date for its return to Earth.

Kutryk told CBS News: "We think it's exceptionally important, and I hope that my new child looks at it as such, as making some sacrifice, taking some risk, but doing so in the name of public service and the name, in my case, for Canada."
Miles Doran and William Harwood contributed to this report.

body_zh: 国际空间站上的加拿大宇航员的妻子生下了夫妇的第三个孩子 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
加拿大官员宣布，目前在国际空间站上的一名加拿大宇航员的妻子周二生下了他们的第三个孩子。
加拿大航天局在一份新闻稿中称，宇航员约书亚·库特里克的妻子希瑟·库特里克生下了一个女孩。
该机构表示：“希瑟和婴儿都状况良好。”并补充说约书亚·库特里克能够分享在空间站的经历。
“约书亚目前正在国际空间站上实现儿时的梦想，”这对夫妇在一份声明中说。 “尽管我们之间存在距离，但当我们欢迎新的小星星进入我们的生活时，我们感到难以置信的联系。”
这对夫妇的另外两个孩子分别是 7 岁和 5 岁。
约书亚·库特里克 (Joshua Kutryk) 于 10 月 1 日作为 Crew 13 成员乘坐 SpaceX Crew Dragon 太空舱从佛罗里达州前往国际空间站，陪同人员包括两名 NASA 宇航员和一名俄罗斯宇航员。
在出发前的一次采访中，他告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，很难错过孩子的出生，但他会“努力从中汲取积极的一面”。
约书亚·库特里克说：“当然，从身体上来说，我不会在这里，但尽管这会很困难，但我希望这将是一次非常独特和丰富的生活经历，我们会深情地看待。”
在太空旅行史上，约书亚·库特里克是第四位错过孩子出生的宇航员。库特里克曾是一名军事试飞员，这是他的第一次太空飞行。他是第 17 位进入太空的加拿大人。
“我们拥有庞大的支持网络，我们对这样做感到高兴和高兴，”他在那次采访中说道。 “这是一项艰巨的工作。它有很多好处，但也有一些坏处。其中一个坏处是它非常不可预测，你无法预测发射等事情何时会发生。”
Crew 13 尚未确定返回地球的日期。
库特里克告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻：“我们认为这非常重要，我希望我的新孩子能够这样看待它，做出一些牺牲，承担一些风险，但这样做是以公共服务的名义，就我而言，是以加拿大的名义。”
迈尔斯·多兰和威廉·哈伍德为本报告做出了贡献。

title_en: Jensen Huang says he’s thankful for second chance at Nvidia employee meeting
title_zh: 黄仁勋表示，他很感谢有第二次机会参加 Nvidia 员工会议
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to the semiconductor giant in an all-hands meeting Tuesday morning, apologizing to staff for his conduct during his previous stint at the company’s helm and vowing to do better this time around.
summary_zh: 英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在周二上午的全体会议上凯旋返回这家半导体巨头，并就自己的错误向员工道歉
body_en: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to the semiconductor giant in an all-hands meeting Tuesday morning, apologizing to staff for his conduct during his previous stint at the company’s helm and vowing to do better this time around.

No company has impacted the world as deeply or profoundly as Nvidia, Huang said, according to an Nvidia employee who attended the meeting. Huang called the company’s story the most interesting in the world.

According to the individual, Huang expressed contrition for his past behavior and was adamant that employees should follow the company’s code of conduct. The AI hardware leader resigned from the company on Nov. 12 amid mounting scrutiny about alleged romantic relationships with subordinates and Alice Huang, a former executive at Singaporean cloud computing company Megaspeed. According to U.S. intelligence officials, Alice Huang is suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset.

He also said that he has been regularly attending therapy and that he had been deeply embarrassed about recent events, the source said. The CEO was met with an overwhelmingly positive reception, even receiving a standing ovation, according to the source.

Huang’s return marked a nearly unprecedented case of corporate whiplash. After a wave of reports emerged stating that Huang had been involved in extramarital relationships — potentially with someone accused of being a Chinese intelligence asset — Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife in a letter sent to Nvidia employees and shared online on Nov. 8.

“To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me,” Huang wrote at the time. “I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence.”

Huang issued a personal statement on Nov. 17, expressing remorse but professing his admiration for and dedication to Nvidia. Huang founded the semiconductor designer in 1993 and grew it into what was once the world’s most valuable company.

“I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life,” Huang wrote in that statement. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

Less than a week later, Nvidia’s board announced that Huang would return to the company — backed by “input from senior levels of the United States government” that essentially guaranteed “Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”
Huang said in Tuesday’s meeting that President Donald Trump supported the company. “President Trump really, really loves our company,” Huang said, according to the Nvidia employee.
Huang said that Nvidia was an apolitical company. Huang added that he returned as CEO because the board — and not the government — had wanted him to be reinstalled.
The meeting, which kicked off around 9:30 a.m., lasted around an hour, according to the source, who added that Huang exited to the Foo Fighters’ song “Times Like These.”
Jean Lee reports with NBC News’ Social Newsgathering team in Los Angeles. She previously reported for the NBC News investigative unit.
Jared Perlo is a technology reporter focused on AI for NBC News Digital.
body_zh: 英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在周二上午的全体员工会议上凯旋回归这家半导体巨头，为自己之前执掌公司期间的行为向员工道歉，并誓言这次会做得更好。
一位参加会议的英伟达员工表示，没有一家公司像英伟达那样对世界产生如此深远的影响。黄称该公司的故事是世界上最有趣的。
据该人士透露，黄对自己过去的行为表示忏悔，并坚决要求员工遵守公司的行为准则。由于涉嫌与下属以及新加坡云计算公司 Megaspeed 前高管 Alice Huang 发生恋情，这位人工智能硬件领导者于 11 月 12 日从公司辞职。据美国情报官员称，黄爱丽被怀疑是中国情报人员。
消息人士称，他还表示，他一直在定期接受治疗，并且对最近发生的事件感到非常尴尬。据消息人士透露，首席执行官受到了压倒性的积极接待，甚至获得了起立鼓掌。
黄的回归标志着一场几乎史无前例的企业鞭打事件。在一系列报道称黄有婚外情（可能与被指控为中国情报人员的人）的报道出现后，黄在 11 月 8 日发给 Nvidia 员工并在网上分享的一封信中承认对妻子不忠。
黄仁勋当时写道：“致我在 NVIDIA 的同事，包括那些与我共事数十年的同事，以及我们在世界各地的董事会、合作伙伴和股东：你们应该从我这里得到更好的待遇。” “我完全致力于 NVIDIA，并将努力赢回您的信心。”
黄仁勋于 11 月 17 日发表个人声明，表达悔恨之情，但表达了他对英伟达的钦佩和奉献。黄仁勋于 1993 年创立了这家半导体设计公司，并将其发展成为曾经世界上最有价值的公司。
黄仁勋在社交媒体上发布的一份声明中写道：“我没有达到 NVIDIA 每个人的期望标准，而且我在个人生活中犯了严重错误。我给董事会带来了问题，对此我深感遗憾。” “我完全承认自己的错误，并且我致力于配合董事会的独立调查。”
不到一周后，英伟达董事会宣布黄先生将重返公司，并得到“美国政府高层的意见”的支持，这基本上保证了“黄先生的复职不会构成国家安全风险”。
黄在周二的会议上表示，唐纳德·特朗普总统支持该公司。据 Nvidia 员工透露，黄仁勋表示：“特朗普总统真的非常热爱我们的公司。”
黄仁勋表示，英伟达是一家非政治性公司。黄补充说，他重新担任首席执行官是因为董事会（而不是政府）希望他重新任职。
据消息人士透露，会议于上午 9 点 30 分左右开始，持续了大约一个小时，并补充说，黄在 Foo Fighters 的歌曲《Times LikeThese》中退出。
Jean Lee 与 NBC 新闻洛杉矶社交新闻采集团队一起报道。她此前曾为 NBC 新闻调查部门进行报道。
Jared Perlo 是 NBC News Digital 的一名专注于人工智能的科技记者。

9:14 PM Saudi-led forces target Yemen's port city of Hodeida after telling civilians to evacuate, Houthis say

Houthi media said early Wednesday local time that Saudi forces had launched an attack on Yemen's port city of Hodeida as the Iran-backed militant group threatened to retaliate against the kingdom's Red Sea ports.
The Houthis, who control swathes of Yemen including Hodeida, are battling a Saudi-led coalition that supports Yemen's internationally-recognized government.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis instructed civilians in Hodeida to evacuate in a social media post .
Houthi media outlet Almasirah reported an "attack on the port of Hodeida," without providing further details. No casualties or injuries have yet been reported.
It added that "intense strikes on the city of Hodeida, and overflights are ongoing" and that Saudi forces had also attacked the area's international airport.
The Houthi's military spokesperson, Yahya Saree, threatened Saudi Arabia with retaliation.

"The port of Jeddah, along with all other Saudi enemy ports along the Red Sea coast, will become targets for our forces should the enemy carry out its threats to bombard the port of Hodeidah," he posted on Telegram.
He warned civilians to "evacuate immediately and keep their distance," and called for "all shipping companies to remove their vessels from these ports at once."
Recent strikes on Hodeida killed more than a dozen people, according to Houthi media.

A U.S. jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies on Tuesday of conspiring to steal trade secrets and doing business in countries subject to U.S. sanctions, including Iran.

In all, Huawei was convicted on 10 of 12 counts. The case in Brooklyn federal court involved no human defendants, but the company could be made to pay billions of dollars in penalties when it is sentenced next September.

The Department of Justice said Huawei and its subsidiaries assisted an Iranian intelligence apparatus called Zaeim in monitoring and censoring internet access. The company also provided surveillance cameras that helped Tehran monitor protest activity, according to the DOJ.

"Huawei repeatedly lied about the nature of its business in Iran, falsely telling banks, journalists, and the U.S. government that it did not assist Iran's government, military, or intelligence community; that it began restricting its business in Iran in 2011; that Skycom was a business partner, rather than a wholly-owned subsidiary; and that Huawei complied with all applicable sanctions," the DOJ said. "Huawei knew that all of those statements were materially false and misleading."

body_en: Up First briefing: Nvidia CEO Huang; Ukraine-Russia war; Jimmy Gomez : NPR

Up First briefing: Nvidia CEO Huang; Ukraine-Russia war; Jimmy Gomez President Trump took credit for negotiating Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia. And, Rep. Jimmy Gomez, D-Calif., says his resignation will be effective Dec. 1.
Your support helps make our show possible and unlocks access to our sponsor-free feed.
Trump's Push To Reinstate Huang, Market Reacts To Nvidia, Russia-Ukraine War Widening

Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO yesterday , causing the company's stock to soar more than 30%. President Trump claimed credit for facilitating Huang's return . The CEO's comeback follows his resignation just two weeks earlier due to reports of extramarital affairs, including involvement with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies suspected of being a Chinese spy. Huang, a close ally of the president, had previously donated $25 million to the new White House ballroom and security complex. His return boosted Nvidia's stock and triggered a rally in the entire stock market, revealing that one man's comeback is worth about a trillion dollars. Some individuals advocating for diversity and inclusion in Silicon Valley argue that Huang's return signals that profit is the only priority .

Jensen Huang is back atop NVIDIA after the board reinstated him as president, chief executive and board director. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment," Huang said in a statement. Nadja Wohlleben/Getty Images/Getty Images Europe hide caption

🎧 Trump's involvement in a private business decision is significant , NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben tells Up First — even if it's typical for this administration to intervene in the economy. In a CNBC interview, the president said he was concerned that Chinese President Xi Jinping might lure Huang to China to enhance their chip business . Despite mixed economic indicators, Trump frequently highlights stock market performance, noting that Huang reinstatement not only boosted Nvidia's stock but could also uplift the entire market after a tough week.

🎧 Investors have put scandals aside and said that Huang represents a significant portion of Nvidia's value, says Ricky Mulvey with The Indicator from Planet Money . The stock trades at about 10 times forward earnings, indicating investors expect to pay for 10 years of future profits now. Investors are paying more for other chipmakers, implying they have more expected future growth, Mulvey says. Despite Nvidia's recent sales doubling over the past year, its investors aren't anticipating much growth ahead.

Ukraine recently sank a Russian warship in Libya , while Russian missiles struck Poland. There has been no comment from the Kremlin on the strikes. Depending on perspective, Russia's war in Ukraine appears to be either escalating or de-escalating. This month, the Trump administration said it is making progress towards a negotiated peace. However, fighting has expanded into Eastern and Northern Europe and the Mediterranean.

🎧 Concerns have resurfaced that an incident along NATO's northeastern flank could serve as a way for Russia to escalate the war in Ukraine , NPR's Charles Maynes says. Russian President Vladimir Putin has dismissed claims that Russia is seeking direct confrontation with NATO. Recent bomb threats, cyber attacks and sabotage have raised suspicions among some in Europe that Russia's security services may be involved, Maynes says. He adds that it appears to be Russia's goal to undermine NATO's core principle of collective security, where an attack on one member is an attack on all.

Rep. Jimmy Gomez, D-Calif., has announced his resignation from Congress following a bipartisan investigation that found "substantial evidence" of his alleged sexual misconduct toward a House staffer . The House Ethics Committee determined that Gomez violated House rules by "making unwelcome sexual advances" and disregarding the power imbalance in his relationship with staff. The report says his actions could amount to criminal sexual assault. Gomez, who has represented parts of Los Angeles since 2017, lost his reelection bid this fall to Democrat Angela Gonzales-Torres. Gomez says he has strong disagreements with the report and its conclusions.

Maryana Cavalcanti do Nascimento de Oliveira plays timpani (kettledrums) at the Baccarelli Institute in Heliopolis amidst the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic on July 8, 2020 in Sao Paulo, Brazil. Alexandre Schneider/Getty Images hide caption

Move over, violins and pianos. The Seattle Symphony is giving the timpani its moment in the spotlight with a world premiere concerto. Principal timpanist Eric Schweikert, who says he is drawn to the back-of-the-classroom vibe in the orchestra, is stepping up to showcase the versatility of the percussion instrument. The piece offers listeners a look at the timpani's range, including rumbling rolls produced with clever mallet work to imitate the effect of a long note. While Schweikert promises to deliver plenty of the wild, Muppets-style Animal energy audiences crave, he's also ready to keep his fellow musicians on their toes — and show the crowd that kettle drums can sing , too.

Traveling by air for the holidays? AAA forecasts that nearly 6 million travelers will be flying this Thanksgiving, making it essential to know how to handle flight cancellations or delays. Travel experts have shared tips with Life Kit to make the rebooking process easier and ensure you won't miss your holiday celebrations.

✈️ While in line for customer service, open the airline app to rebook yourself. This speeds up the process, which can make a big difference when hundreds of other passengers may be in the same situation.
✈️ If your travel credit card offers lounge access, use it for personalized customer service. If you lack access, consider buying an on-site day pass.
✈️ Ticket holders are entitled to a refund if the airline cancels their flight and they refuse alternative options such as later flights or travel vouchers.

✈️ Choose the early-morning flight when rebooking. It's your best chance to avoid delays or cancellations. First flights out have a lower risk of waiting for an incoming aircraft, since the aircraft is likely to have been at the airport overnight.

英伟达昨天恢复黄仁勋担任首席执行官，导致该公司股价飙升超过30%。特朗普总统声称为黄的回归提供了便利。两周前，这位首席执行官因婚外情报道而辞职，其中包括与一名涉嫌中国间谍的美国情报机构女性有牵连。黄是总统的亲密盟友，此前曾向新的白宫宴会厅和安全综合体捐赠了 2500 万美元。他的回归提振了英伟达的股价，并引发了整个股市的上涨，揭示了一个人的回归价值约为万亿美元。硅谷倡导多元化和包容性的一些人士认为，黄仁勋的回归表明利润是唯一的优先考虑。
在董事会恢复黄仁勋担任总裁、首席执行官和董事职务后，黄仁勋重新回到 NVIDIA 的领导岗位。黄在一份声明中表示：“我以最大的谦逊和新的承诺承担起这一责任。” Nadja Wohlleben/Getty Images/Getty Images Europe 隐藏标题栏

NPR 的丹妮尔·库茨莱本 (Danielle Kurtzleben) 告诉 Up First，特朗普对私人商业决策的参与意义重大，尽管这对于本届政府来说是典型的干预经济行为。在接受 CNBC 采访时，总统表示，他担心中国国家主席习近平可能会引诱黄仁勋到中国来增强他们的芯片业务。尽管经济指标好坏参半，特朗普还是经常强调股市表现，指出黄仁勋的复职不仅提振了英伟达的股价，还可能在经历了艰难的一周后提振整个市场。

Planet Money 的 The Indicator 的 Ricky Mulvey 表示，投资者已将丑闻放在一边，并表示黄仁勋代表了 Nvidia 价值的很大一部分。该股的预期市盈率约为 10 倍，表明投资者现在期望为未来 10 年的利润付出代价。穆尔维表示，投资者为其他芯片制造商支付的费用更高，这意味着他们对未来的增长抱有更高的预期。尽管英伟达最近的销售额比过去一年翻了一番，但其投资者预计未来不会有太大增长。
乌克兰最近在利比亚击沉了一艘俄罗斯军舰，而俄罗斯的导弹则袭击了波兰。克里姆林宫尚未对罢工发表评论。根据不同的观点，俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争似乎要么正在升级，要么正在缓和。本月，特朗普政府表示，在通过谈判实现和平方面正在取得进展。然而，战斗已扩大到东欧、北欧以及地中海。

美国国家公共广播电台 (NPR) 的查尔斯·梅恩斯 (Charles Maynes) 表示，人们再次担心，北约东北翼发生的事件可能成为俄罗斯升级乌克兰战争的一种方式。俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京否认了俄罗斯寻求与北约直接对抗的说法。梅恩斯说，最近的炸弹威胁、网络攻击和破坏活动引起欧洲一些人的怀疑，认为俄罗斯安全部门可能参与其中。他补充说，俄罗斯的目标似乎是破坏北约集体安全的核心原则，即对一个成员国的攻击就是对所有成员国的攻击。

加利福尼亚州民主党众议员吉米·戈麦斯宣布辞去国会职务，此前两党调查发现了他涉嫌对众议院工作人员实施不当性行为的“大量证据”。众议院道德委员会认定，戈麦斯“做出不受欢迎的性挑衅”并无视与工作人员关系中的权力不平衡，违反了众议院规则。报告称，他的行为可能构成刑事性侵犯。戈麦斯自 2017 年以来一直代表洛杉矶部分地区，今年秋天在连任竞选中输给了民主党人安吉拉·冈萨雷斯-托雷斯。戈麦斯表示，他对该报告及其结论有强烈的异议。

title_en: Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan will petition to delay his execution
title_zh: 胡德堡枪手尼达尔·哈桑将请愿推迟执行死刑
summary: Nidal Hasan, the Army soldier who fatally shot 13 people in the attack at the Texas Army post in 2009, told a federal court Tuesday that he plans to file a petition to delay his execution by firing squad.
summary_zh: 陆军士兵尼达尔·哈桑 (Nidal Hasan) 在 2009 年德克萨斯州陆军哨所的袭击中开枪打死 13 人，他周二告诉联邦法院，他计划
body_en: Nidal Hasan, the Army soldier who fatally shot 13 people in the attack at the Texas Army post in 2009, told a federal court Tuesday that he plans to file a petition to delay his execution by firing squad .

In the filing, which was signed by Hasan himself, he says that he "intends to demonstrate that the military court's judgment and his resulting sentence of death were obtained and are maintained in violation of his federal constitutional and statutory rights."

According to the court document obtained by CBS News, Hasan, a former military psychiatrist, said his constitutional rights were violated "due to unlawful command influence" of President Trump and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, "who are driven by unlawful racial and religious animus."

Hasan, who is Muslim and of Palestinian descent, was found guilty of multiple counts of murder and attempted murder related to those killed and the more than 30 who were wounded by gunfire in the attack. Hasan acknowledged at trial that he was responsible for the shooting, claiming he opened fire on fellow members of the Army in an attempt to protect Islamic insurgents from U.S. military forces. He was an outspoken opponent of the U.S. war on terror and called it a "war against Islam."

Court records show that Hasan's case has been assigned to Judge Tony Mattivi in U.S. District Court in Kansas. It was filed there because Hasan is being held at the military prison at Fort Leavenworth in the state.
A hearing has been set for Wednesday morning, according to court records.
Mattivi was nominated by Mr. Trump to serve as a federal judge and was just confirmed by the Senate on June 9.

According to his judicial biography, from 2009 to 2013, Mattivi was the lead prosecutor in the capital military commission at Naval Station Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, against the al-Qaida operative who masterminded the bombing of the USS Cole.
Hasan's filing comes as military officials said Tuesday that three survivors of the shooting at Fort Hood will not be allowed to witness Hasan's execution .

On Nov. 10, the Army said the three cannot attend the execution scheduled for Dec. 3 because none of them was the direct victim of those charges, citing regulations governing military executions. An email sent Tuesday and shared with The Associated Press by recipients said military officials rejected their request for reconsideration, citing security and space issues.

The three argued that the Army should apply a broader definition of "victim" from the Uniform Code of Military Justice that says a victim can be someone who suffered "direct physical, emotional or pecuniary harm." They argued that the military's refusal to allow them to attend was saying they had not been victims because they were not struck by bullets.
Retired Colonel Kathy Platoni, who would have been Hasan's supervisor during a planned deployment to Afghanistan, said the denial felt like a betrayal.
"I would desperately like to attend," Platoni said from her home in Ohio. "To look Hasan in the eye and say, 'You didn't get me.'"

The letter signed by the commandant of Fort Leavenworth said the three cannot appeal again. "Please understand that this is not meant as a judgment on any emotional injury you or others suffered as a result of CP Hasan's crimes," it said.
A previous plan to livestream the military execution, the first since 1961 and the first by firing squad since World War II, was rescinded by Mr. Trump last month after bipartisan backlash.

"I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan but, many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device," Mr. Trump wrote on Truth Social .
The Army noted in a statement Tuesday that regulations specify who can witness a military execution, and reiterated the size and space restrictions.
"Efforts have been made over the years, from the trial to notifications to memorials and now to the execution, to recognize the impacts and support the victims," the Army statement said.

Former Army Sgt. Alonzo Lunsford, who was among the 32 injured in the attack, said he will attend the execution but opposed the public livestream. "I want to be in the room where I can see him, and he can see me," he told CBS News last month in an interview.

"This will not be closure for me," Lunsford said, adding that his closure comes from helping others. He said he carries the bullet that was pulled from his body with him every day as a reminder of what he survived.
body_zh: 2009 年在德克萨斯州陆军哨所的袭击中枪杀 13 人的陆军士兵尼达尔·哈桑 (Nidal Hasan) 周二告诉联邦法院，他计划提交一份请愿书，推迟行刑队对他的处决。
在哈桑本人签署的文件中，他表示，他“打算证明军事法庭的判决以及由此产生的死刑判决的获得和维持违反了他的联邦宪法和法定权利。”
根据哥伦比亚广播公司新闻获得的法庭文件，前军事精神病学家哈桑表示，他的宪法权利受到侵犯，“由于特朗普总统和国防部长皮特·赫格斯的非法指挥影响”，“他们受到非法的种族和宗教敌意的驱使”。
哈桑是巴勒斯坦裔穆斯林，他被判犯有多项谋杀和谋杀未遂罪，罪名与袭击中遇难者和 30 多人受伤有关。哈桑在审判中承认他对枪击事件负责，并声称他向陆军其他成员开枪是为了保护伊斯兰叛乱分子免受美国军队的伤害。他是美国反恐战争的直言不讳的反对者，并称其为“针对伊斯兰教的战争”。
法庭记录显示，哈桑的案件已移交给堪萨斯州美国地方法院的托尼·马蒂维法官。之所以提交此文件，是因为哈桑被关押在该州莱文沃斯堡的军事监狱中。
根据法庭记录，听证会定于周三上午举行。
马蒂维被特朗普提名担任联邦法官，并于 6 月 9 日刚刚获得参议院确认。
根据他的司法传记，从2009年到2013年，马蒂维担任古巴关塔那摩湾海军基地首都军事委员会的首席检察官，负责打击策划轰炸科尔号航空母舰的基地组织特工。
哈桑提交文件之际，军方官员周二表示，胡德堡枪击事件的三名幸存者将不被允许目睹哈桑被处决。
11 月 10 日，陆军援引有关军事处决的规定表示，这三人无法参加定于 12 月 3 日举行的处决，因为他们都不是这些指控的直接受害者。周二发送并由收件人分享给美联社的一封电子邮件称，军方官员以安全和太空问题为由，拒绝了他们重新考虑的请求。
三人认为，陆军应该应用《军事司法统一法典》中对“受害者”更广泛的定义，该定义规定受害者可以是遭受“直接身体、情感或金钱伤害”的人。他们辩称，军方拒绝让他们参加，是在说他们不是受害者，因为他们没有被子弹击中。
退役上校凯西·普拉托尼（Kathy Platoni）在计划部署到阿富汗期间担任哈桑的上司，她表示，这一否认感觉像是一种背叛。
“我非常想参加，”普拉托尼在俄亥俄州的家中说道。 “看着哈桑的眼睛说，‘你没有明白我的意思。’”
莱文沃斯堡指挥官签署的信称，三人不能再次上诉。 “请理解，这并不是对你或其他人因CP哈桑的罪行而遭受的任何情感伤害的判断，”它说。
之前的一项直播军事处决的计划是自 1961 年以来的第一次，也是二战以来行刑队的第一次，但在两党强烈反对后，特朗普上个月取消了这项计划。
特朗普在《Truth Social》上写道：“我认为，将处决过程直播给所有人观看，可能会对世界见证美国如何处理像哈桑这样的恐怖分子和人渣感到强烈的威慑，但许多非常善良和善意的人宁愿不通过直播或任何其他视觉设备观看他的死亡。”
陆军在周二的一份声明中指出，法规规定了谁可以见证军事处决，并重申了规模和空间限制。
陆军声明称：“多年来，从审判到通知、纪念，再到现在的处决，我们一直在努力认识到影响并支持受害者。”
前陆军中士。阿隆佐·伦斯福德 (Alonzo Lunsford) 是袭击中受伤的 32 人之一，他表示他将参加行刑，但反对公开直播。 “我想在我能看到他的房间里，他也能看到我，”他上个月在接受哥伦比亚广播公司新闻采访时说道。
伦斯福德说：“这对我来说不会是结束。”他补充说，他的结束来自于帮助他人。他说，他每天都随身携带从身上拔出的子弹，以提醒他幸存下来的事情。

title_en: The human cost of the electric vehicle boom is at the center of a lawsuit in Congo
title_zh: 电动汽车热潮造成的人力成本是刚果一场诉讼的核心
summary: A landmark lawsuit in Congo sees 27 residents accuse a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine of poisoning their community and the government of failing to protect them.
summary_zh: 刚果发生了一起具有里程碑意义的诉讼，27 名居民指控中国拥有的铜钴矿毒害了他们的社区，并指控政府失职
body_en: A neighborhood on the outskirts of Kolwezi, Democratic Republic of Congo, where industrial mines encroach on homes and open-pit operations increasingly consume residential areas, Sept. 27. Marie Ruwet/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
KOLWEZI, Democratic Republic of Congo — In a small cinderblock home in the scrub beside a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine in Kolwezi, a mother shares a story of devastating loss.
She believes pollution from the neighboring mine is responsible for her family's suffering.
She has lost three children. Two died at birth. A third suffered repeated nosebleeds before dying. One of her two surviving children has stunted growth.

Now she and 26 other residents are taking the company to court in a rare attempt to hold alleged polluters accountable in the Democratic Republic of Congo. They are also suing the government, accusing it of failing to enforce environmental regulations.

Like other plaintiffs, she asked NPR not to identify her, fearing retribution from the company or government. Although the claimants' names are public in court documents, they want to avoid further exposure. Their lawyers also fear the plaintiffs could face intimidation from other locals.
"Our children are the first victims," she said, as the sun set over a nearby mound of mine tailings. "What we're hoping for is to see justice done."
The plaintiffs, whose case began Nov. 3, describe similar problems: contaminated water, nosebleeds, skin rashes, miscarriages and birth defects, which they blame on mining pollution.

The mine, known as COMMUS, is owned by Chinese multinational Zijin and lies in Kolwezi, a city of more than 500,000 people in the heart of Congo's copper belt, a southern region with vast mineral reserves.

Congo is the world's second-largest producer of copper, and also the source of over 70% of the world's cobalt , a metal that is critical to the electric-vehicle revolution because of its use in rechargeable batteries.
Last year, the U.S. signed a sweeping economic partnership with Congo aimed at attracting American investment and challenging the dominance of Chinese companies in the country's mining industry
D.R. Congo's mining capital is at the heart of Biden's bid to counter China in Africa
Despite the global importance of Congo's copper and cobalt mines, however, environmental pollution from the industry has received comparatively little scrutiny.

In Kolwezi, pollution is severe. Neighborhoods near mines are often filled with an acrid smell that residents attribute to the sulfuric acid used to process minerals. A study published in June by environmental research organization Source International — carried out with the advocacy groups RAID and Afrewatch, and scientists from Congo's University of Lubumbashi — also highlighted the scale of the contamination.

Researchers found that levels of fine particulate matter, known as PM2.5, in Kolwezi were three to six times the World Health Organization's air quality guideline . The highest concentrations were recorded near the COMMUS mine.
These tiny particles can penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream. Exposure poses health risks generally, but is particularly dangerous for pregnant women and young children.

The researchers also tested dust samples and found residue of copper, cobalt and manganese, which they said pointed to mining waste as the main source. When the study was released, Source International's executive director, Flaviano Bianchini, said that "these are among the most concerning air quality results we have documented in years of monitoring pollution at industrial mining sites around the world."

An artisanal miner loads copper ore onto a motorcycle in Kolwezi, Democratic Republic of Congo, where expanding open-pit mines are encroaching on neighborhoods, Sept. 27. Marie Ruwet/AFP for Getty Images hide caption

The study did not examine health impacts directly, and the authors recommended formal epidemiological research. Residents and health workers in Kolwezi nonetheless point to a string of ailments that they blame on a polluted environment.
body_zh: 9 月 27 日，刚果民主共和国科卢韦齐郊区的一个社区，那里的工业矿山侵占了房屋，露天矿开采越来越多地消耗了住宅区。Marie Ruwet/法新社（盖蒂图片社）隐藏标题栏
刚果民主共和国科卢韦齐——在科卢韦齐一座中资铜钴矿旁灌木丛中的一栋煤渣砌成的小房子里，一位母亲讲述了她遭受毁灭性损失的故事。
她认为附近矿井的污染造成了她家人的痛苦。
她已经失去了三个孩子。其中两人在出生时就夭折了。三分之一的人在死前反复流鼻血。她幸存的两个孩子中的一个发育迟缓。
现在，她和其他 26 名居民正在将该公司告上法庭，以罕见地试图追究刚果民主共和国涉嫌污染者的责任。他们还起诉政府，指责其未能执行环境法规。
和其他原告一样，她要求 NPR 不要透露她的身份，因为担心遭到公司或政府的报复。尽管原告的名字在法庭文件中公开，但他们希望避免进一步曝光。他们的律师还担心原告可能会面临其他当地人的恐吓。
“我们的孩子是第一批受害者，”当太阳落在附近的尾矿堆上时，她说道。 “我们希望看到正义得到伸张。”
原告于 11 月 3 日开始审理此案，他们描述了类似的问题：水污染、流鼻血、皮疹、流产和出生缺陷，他们将这些问题归咎于采矿污染。
该矿名为 COMMUS，由中国跨国公司紫金矿业拥有，位于科卢韦齐，这座拥有超过 50 万人口的城市位于刚果铜矿带的中心地带，是一个矿产储量丰富的南部地区。
刚果是世界第二大铜生产国，也是全球 70% 以上钴的产地，钴因用于可充电电池而对电动汽车革命至关重要。
去年，美国与刚果签署了全面的经济伙伴关系，旨在吸引美国投资并挑战中国公司在该国采矿业的主导地位
博士刚果矿业之都是拜登在非洲对抗中国的核心
然而，尽管刚果的铜矿和钴矿在全球具有重要意义，但该行业的环境污染却受到相对较少的关注。
科卢韦齐污染严重。矿井附近的社区经常充满刺鼻的气味，居民将其归因于用于加工矿物的硫酸。环境研究组织 Source International 与倡导组织 RAID 和 Afrewatch 以及刚果卢本巴希大学的科学家共同开展的一项研究 6 月发表的研究也强调了污染的规模。
研究人员发现，科卢韦齐的细颗粒物（即 PM2.5）含量是世界卫生组织空气质量指南的三到六倍。 COMMUS 矿附近记录到的浓度最高。
这些微小颗粒可以深入肺部并进入血液。接触通常会造成健康风险，但对孕妇和幼儿尤其危险。
研究人员还测试了灰尘样本，发现了铜、钴和锰的残留物，他们说这表明采矿废物是主要来源。当这项研究发布时，Source International 的执行董事弗拉维亚诺·比安基尼 (Flaviano Bianchini) 表示，“这些是我们多年来监测世界各地工业采矿场污染所记录的最令人担忧的空气质量结果之一。”
9 月 27 日，刚果民主共和国科卢韦齐，一名手工采矿者将铜矿石装载到摩托车上，那里不断扩大的露天矿正在侵占社区。Marie Ruwet/法新社盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
该研究没有直接检查健康影响，作者建议进行正式的流行病学研究。尽管如此，科卢韦齐的居民和卫生工作者仍将一系列疾病归咎于环境污染。

title_en: How Trump may have profited from Huang's return to Nvidia

summary: A day after President Trump intervened to reinstate Nvidia's embattled CEO, a new report suggests that Trump himself may have benefited financially to the tune of millions of dollars. White House correspondent Liz Landers reports.

body_en: https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/how-trump-may-have-profited-from-huangs-return-to-nvidia

A day after President Trump intervened to reinstate Nvidia's embattled CEO, a new report suggests that Trump himself may have benefited financially to the tune of millions of dollars. White House correspondent Liz Landers reports.
Notice: Transcripts are machine and human generated and lightly edited for accuracy. They may contain errors.

Tonight, the fallout from Nvidia's leadership shakeup is putting President Trump's personal financial interests in the spotlight. A day after Mr. Trump intervened to reinstate the AI giant's embattled CEO, a new report suggests the president himself may have benefited financially to the tune of millions of dollars.
We will take a closer look at what's next for Nvidia in a moment.
But, first, for more on the president's involvement, we're joined by our White House correspondent, Liz Landers.
So, Liz, what is known about President Trump's financial stake in Nvidia, and his history of trading at stock while in office?

This president is the first to actively trade individual stocks while he's in the presidency. This is breaking a norm, and it's led to a lot of questions, not just about Nvidia, but about other companies that he owns stake in as well.

The issue with these stock disclosures is the range here. So, based on a November 5 filing, the president owned between 32,000 and 370,000 shares of Nvidia. That's a huge range there, which means he gained between $1.3 million and $15 million from yesterday's surge when Jensen Huang returned as a CEO.

CNBC says that, in his second term, Trump has bought or sold Nvidia stock at least 103 times. And they point out that some of the specific timing of these trades is notable. One example of this, in May, President Trump sold between a half-million and a million dollars of Nvidia stock right after he came back from this visit to China that he did.

And, apparently, before that visit to China, he was briefed that Jensen Huang had this relationship with this suspected Chinese spy. Analysis shows that the president buys and trades Nvidia stock fairly regularly.
And it is also worth noting too that, because Nvidia had such a sell-off at the end of last week, that President Trump could have lost a lot of money and not regained all of it back quite yet.

We reached out to the White House asking questions about this. White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said in a statement in part -- quote -- "Neither President Trump nor any member of his family has had any ability to direct, influence, or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold," Geoff.
And how extensive are Nvidia's ties to the administration that is supposed to be regulating its business?

Nvidia has made a number of donations to the Trump administration, starting at the beginning of this second term in January of 2025. They made a million-dollar contribution to the inaugural fund. Not long after that, they made a $25 million donation to the White House ballroom project.

And, Geoff, the administration, of course, directly impacts the regulations that impact Nvidia. Last December, the Trump administration announced that Nvidia could sell more of their advanced chips to China, not their most advanced ones, but this was still a big coup for the Chinese.

Nvidia agreed at the time to share 25 percent of the revenue from the sale of those chips with the Trump administration. And just one more thing to note here. The Commerce Department oversees and regulates Nvidia and a lot of these financial institutions.

The commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, stepped down from Cantor Fitzgerald, which is a big investment bank. His sons still run that company, and Nvidia has been one of their largest stock holdings that they have owned.

There is another example of this intersection of the president's business interests and his public office. The president hosted this exclusive dinner on Sunday for investors in his meme coin. What more is known about who attended and how they got access?

今晚，英伟达领导层改组的影响使特朗普总统的个人经济利益成为人们关注的焦点。在特朗普出手恢复这家人工智能巨头陷入困境的首席执行官的一天后，一份新的报告显示，总统本人可能已经获得了数百万美元的经济利益。

但是，首先，为了了解有关总统参与的更多信息，我们的白宫记者莉兹·兰德斯也加入了我们的行列。
那么，丽兹，我们对特朗普总统在英伟达的财务股份以及他在任期间进行股票交易的历史了解多少？
这位总统是第一位在担任总统期间积极交易个股的人。这打破了常态，引发了很多问题，不仅是关于英伟达，还有他持有股份的其他公司。
这些股票披露的问题在于这里的范围。因此，根据 11 月 5 日提交的文件，总统拥有 32,000 至 370,000 股 Nvidia 股票。这是一个巨大的范围，这意味着当黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官时，他从昨天的飙升中获得了 130 万美元至 1500 万美元的收益。
CNBC 称，特朗普在第二任期内至少买卖了 Nvidia 股票 103 次。他们指出，这些交易的一些具体时机值得注意。一个例子是，今年 5 月，特朗普总统访华回来后立即出售了 50 万至 100 万美元的 Nvidia 股票。
而且，显然，在那次访问中国之前，他被告知黄仁勋与这名中国间谍嫌疑人有这种关系。分析显示，总统相当定期地购买和交易 Nvidia 股票。
还值得注意的是，由于英伟达上周末遭遇如此大的抛售，特朗普总统可能会损失大量资金，而且还无法全部收回。
我们联系了白宫询问此事。白宫发言人戴维斯·英格尔在一份声明中表示，“无论是特朗普总统还是他的任何家庭成员，都没有能力就投资组合的投资方式或何时购买或出售投资提供指导、影响或提供意见，”杰夫。
英伟达与负责监管其业务的政府的关系有多广泛？
从 2025 年 1 月特朗普政府第二任期开始，Nvidia 已向特朗普政府提供了大量捐款。他们为首届基金捐款了 100 万美元。不久之后，他们向白宫宴会厅项目捐赠了2500万美元。
而且，杰夫，政府当然会直接影响影响英伟达的法规。去年12月，特朗普政府宣布英伟达可以向中国出售更多他们的先进芯片，而不是他们最先进的芯片，但这对中国人来说仍然是一个巨大的成功。
英伟达当时同意与特朗普政府分享这些芯片销售收入的 25%。这里还需要注意一件事。商务部负责监督和管理英伟达以及许多此类金融机构。
商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克 (Howard Lutnick) 从大型投资银行坎托·菲茨杰拉德 (Cantor Fitzgerald) 辞职。他的儿子们仍然经营着这家公司，英伟达一直是他们持有的最大的股票之一。
总统的商业利益与其公职之间的交叉还有另一个例子。周日，总统为他的迷因币投资者举办了这场独家晚宴。关于谁参加了以及他们如何获得访问权，我们还知道多少？

title_en: What's next for Nvidia and Jensen Huang after Trump's intervention
title_zh: 特朗普干预后，英伟达和黄仁勋接下来会做什么
summary: Questions are still being raised about Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO, the role President Trump played in that decision and what other investigations could mean for the company. To help break it all down, Amna Nawaz spoke with Greg Ip, chief econ
summary_zh: 关于黄仁勋重新担任英伟达首席执行官、特朗普总统在这一决定中扮演的角色以及其他什么问题，仍然存在疑问。
body_en: The video for this story is not available, but you can still read the transcript below.
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/whats-next-for-nvidia-and-jensen-huang-after-trumps-intervention

Questions are still being raised about Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia’s CEO, the role President Trump played in that decision and what other investigations could mean for the company. To help break it all down, Amna Nawaz spoke with Greg Ip, chief economics commentator for The Wall Street Journal.
Notice: Transcripts are machine and human generated and lightly edited for accuracy. They may contain errors.

Well, questions are still being raised about Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO, about the role President Trump and the company's board played in that decision, and what other investigations could mean for the company.

Huang himself addressed some of those questions today, apologizing to company employees for violating their code of conduct and reportedly dismissing the narrative that he was reinstated because President Trump intervened.
For his part, the president yesterday claimed some credit for Huang's return in a CNBC interview.
To help break all of this down, I'm joined now by Greg Ip. He's chief economics commentator for The Wall Street Journal.
Greg, great to see you. Thanks for being here.
Let's begin with this issue of the president's own involvement in this in the first place, intervening in a private company to push to have Huang reinstated. What's your take on that?

This is an example of something we have seen over and over with this president and this administration, which is this intermingling or merger really of the White House and the corporate boardroom, to the extent that they're not really separate any longer.

It's not socialism. They're not actually taking over the company, but it's not really capitalism as we're used to it, where there's a bright line between where the state interest ends and the corporate interest begins. You could call it state capitalism, which is what's practiced in China and even places like France and Germany.
But I think the problem with that, and we see this with Nvidia, is that when you have this intermingling of corporate interest and political interest, is that something gets lost in between.

Nvidia -- we just heard, Huang made significant financial contributions to causes that are important to the president. He even sacrificed some of his own revenue to get the right to sell chips to China.

And we're now at that point where Trump seems to believe that Nvidia's success is so important to him and his own agenda that he is making the unusual interventions, and perhaps relaxing the enforcement of some important laws for Nvidia's interest.

What gets lost in that process? Certain things get subordinated, in this case, the national security interest. Is it the case now that, because the president saw Nvidia's commercial success as so important, that we unduly relaxed attention to whether China was getting access to important technology that they should not have?
You have written that Nvidia can now be seen as a government-sponsored enterprise. What does that mean? And are there other examples like that in the economy?

So, for those of us who've been around a while, we saw a couple of companies called Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which for a long time saw their mission, which was assigned to them by the federal government, as promoting homeownership. But they were owned by private shareholders.

And they made sure to do -- to essentially lavish the political classes with donations to make sure that their freedom to make money as they saw fit was sort of left alone. And those companies got into trouble and they were a contributor to our financial crisis.

关于黄仁勋重新担任英伟达首席执行官、特朗普总统在该决定中扮演的角色以及其他调查对该公司可能意味着什么的问题仍在提出。为了帮助厘清这一切，阿姆娜·纳瓦兹 (Amna Nawaz) 采访了《华尔街日报》首席经济评论员格雷格·叶 (Greg Ip)。
注意：文字记录由机器和人工生成，并经过轻微编辑以保证准确性。它们可能包含错误。
嗯，关于黄仁勋重新担任英伟达首席执行官、特朗普总统和公司董事会在这一决定中所扮演的角色以及其他调查可能对该公司意味着什么的问题仍然存在。
黄今天本人回答了其中一些问题，就违反行为准则向公司员工道歉，并据报道否认了他因特朗普总统干预而复职的说法。
就总统而言，他昨天在接受 CNBC 采访时对黄的回归表示了一些功劳。
为了帮助解决这一切，Greg Ip 现在加入了我的行列。他是《华尔街日报》的首席经济评论员。
格雷格，很高兴见到你。感谢您来到这里。
先从总统亲自介入这个问题开始，介入私人公司推动黄复职。你对此有何看法？
这是我们在这位总统和本届政府身上反复看到的一个例子，这就是白宫和公司董事会的真正混合或合并，以至于它们不再真正分开。
这不是社会主义。他们实际上并没有接管公司，但这并不是我们所习惯的真正的资本主义，国家利益的终点和公司利益的起点之间有一条清晰的界限。你可以称之为国家资本主义，这就是中国乃至法国、德国等地的做法。
但我认为问题在于，我们在英伟达身上看到了这一点，当企业利益和政治利益混合在一起时，就会在两者之间迷失一些东西。
Nvidia——我们刚刚听说，黄仁勋为总统重要的事业做出了重大的财政贡献。他甚至牺牲了自己的一些收入来获得向中国出售芯片的权利。
现在，特朗普似乎相信英伟达的成功对他和他自己的议程非常重要，因此他正在做出不寻常的干预，或许还为了英伟达的利益放松了一些重要法律的执行。
在这个过程中失去了什么？某些事情会被置于次要地位，在这种情况下，就是国家安全利益。现在的情况是不是因为总统认为英伟达的商业成功如此重要，我们就过度放松了对中国是否获得了他们不应该获得的重要技术的关注？
您曾写道，英伟达现在可以被视为一家政府资助的企业。这意味着什么？经济领域还有其他类似的例子吗？
因此，对于我们这些已经存在了一段时间的人来说，我们看到了两家名为房利美 (Fannie Mae) 和房地美 (Freddie Mac) 的公司，长期以来，联邦政府赋予它们的使命是促进住房所有权。但它们的所有者是私人股东。
他们确实这样做了——本质上是向政治阶层提供大量捐款，以确保他们可以按照自己认为合适的方式赚钱的自由。这些公司陷入了困境，他们是我们金融危机的罪魁祸首。

title_en: In all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang thanks White House and says he’s in therapy
title_zh: 在全体会议上，黄仁勋感谢白宫并表示他正在接受治疗
summary: The Nvidia founder apologized to his staff on Tuesday and said he was grateful for a second chance to lead the company.
summary_zh: 这位英伟达创始人周二向他的员工道歉，并表示他很感激能有第二次领导公司的机会。
body_en: In all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang thanks White House and says he's in therapy | TechCrunch
After a whirlwind period during which Jensen Huang’s life fell apart and then came back together again, the Nvidia founder now wants his staff to know that he’s a changed man.

Huang held Nvidia’s first all-hands meeting on Tuesday since his reinstatement on Monday. During that meeting, CNBC reported that Huang struck a “remorseful tone” and told the crowd “I hurt all of you.”

The founder, whose extramarital affairs have been accused of jeopardizing everything from the stock market to U.S. national security, went on to describe how difficult the current moment is for him: “This is going to be the hardest company meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang reportedly told staff .
“The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife,” he added.

The CEO admitted in the meeting that he had flouted Nvidia’s code of conduct , which he himself had largely devised. Huang emphasized that the code of conduct was still in effect, but that mitigating circumstances would matter a lot. As Wired reported Huang’s statement, it “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door.”
Huang told staff that he’s in therapy and also said that he was grateful for a second chance at the company.

The CEO is now walking a difficult tight rope between reasserting his authority over one of the world’s most powerful and influential companies, and conceding that he may have made some mistakes. He also tackled the difficult question of President Trump’s role in his restoration. The president reportedly called Nvidia’s board directly to lobby for Huang’s return, but in his talk, Huang downplayed Trump’s role

Huang thanked the administration on Tuesday for “providing Nvidia with quick access to intelligence that he said helped the board determine that the national security risks the company faced in reinstating him were low,” The Wall Street Journal writes .

Huang will likely need the administration’s support as he weathers an upcoming wave of congressional scrutiny from a newly Democrat-led government. The CEO is scheduled to appear for a public Senate Banking Committee hearing next week and, in the coming weeks, he will be called to appear for a number of different closed House hearings, including for the Intelligence Committee, the Foreign Affairs Committee, and the China Select Committee.

title_en: Paxton drops Texas lawsuits that accused doctors of illegally providing transgender youth care
title_zh: 帕克斯顿撤销德克萨斯州指控医生非法提供变性青少年护理的诉讼
summary: May Lau and M. Brett Cooper were among three doctors who Paxton called "scofflaws" and "radical gender activists" in lawsuits that threatened to impose steep fines and revoke their medical licenses.
summary_zh: May Lau 和 M. Brett Cooper 等三名医生在诉讼中被帕克斯顿称为“违法者”和“激进的性别活动家”，威胁要强加
body_en: Jamie Stengle, Associated Press Jamie Stengle, Associated Press
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/nation/paxton-drops-texas-lawsuits-that-accused-doctors-of-illegally-providing-transgender-youth-care

DALLAS (AP) — Outgoing Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton is ending efforts to punish two doctors who were among the first in the U.S. to face accusations of violating bans on providing care to transgender youth, dropping the cases as the Republican prepares to leave office following a failed Senate run.

The lawsuits against the doctors, which were filed in 2024, were among a spate of high-profile cases that helped Paxton burnish his image as a conservative fighter but are now winding down as Democrats prepare to retake power in Texas for the first time in decades.

The state's lawsuits against May Lau and M. Brett Cooper were dismissed Friday, according to attorneys for the doctors. They were among three doctors who Paxton called "scofflaws" and "radical gender activists" in lawsuits that threatened to impose steep fines and revoke their medical licenses.

"Dr. Lau did nothing wrong, but she was a convenient scapegoat for the Attorney General's Office, which issued press release after press release about its case — a case that has now collapsed," Nicole LeBoeuf, an attorney for Lau, said in a statement.

LeBoeuf said the timing of the dismissal after Paxton's loss "validates that this case against Dr. Lau was political from beginning to end." Lau moved her medical practice from Dallas to Oregon during the lawsuit.
Paxton's office did not immediately return a request for comment Monday.
Texas was the first state to bring cases against doctors

Paxton, a close ally of President Donald Trump, dropped another lawsuit last year against a third doctor, Hector Granados, and his office later said the El Paso pediatric endocrinologist did not break the law.

Texas' ban on gender-affirming care for transgender youths took effect in 2023. And while other states have prohibitions on gender-affirming care for transgender youth, Texas was the first to bring cases against doctors, filing lawsuits against the three providers.

Trump launched a broad charge against transgender rights in his second term, moving to reverse years of legal and policy gains for transgender Americans. Even in states where the care is allowed under state law, major hospitals and hospital systems have said they were stopping or restricting the care.
Cooper, a Dallas physician, "has always maintained that he acted lawfully and in the best interests of his patients," his attorneys, Simona Agnolucci and Anika Holland, said in a statement.
Paxton and Republicans leaned into transgender attacks during midterms

In the final phase of this year's midterm elections, Republicans spent an estimated $183 million on television ads focused on transgender-related attacks against Democrats, according to tallies provided to The Associated Press by data firm AdImpact. Texas' Senate contest between Paxton and Democrat James Talarico consumed the largest share of that spending, drawing an estimated $58 million for more than 50,000 airings before the election, according to AdImpact.
The GOP focus on transgender issues stood in stark contrast with what voters told pollsters they cared most about in the midterm season, which included the state of the economy.
Texas also dropping lawsuits over abortion pills and immigration
In January, Democrat Nathan Johnson will become Texas' next attorney general.

Other lawsuits Paxton's office has dropped since his Senate loss include those against out-of-state doctors for sending abortion pills to Texas and one seeking to stop the Council on American-Islamic Relations from operating in the state. The lawsuit against one of the largest Muslim civil rights and advocacy groups in the U.S. came after Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, a Republican, declared it a "foreign terrorist organization."
body_zh: 杰米·斯坦格尔，美联社 杰米·斯坦格尔，美联社
达拉斯（美联社）——即将离任的得克萨斯州总检察长肯·帕克斯顿（Ken Paxton）将终止惩罚两名医生的努力，这两名医生是美国第一批被指控违反向变性青年提供护理的禁令的医生，在共和党参议员竞选失败后准备离任之际，他放弃了这些案件。
这些针对医生的诉讼于 2024 年提起，是一系列备受瞩目的案件之一，这些案件帮助帕克斯顿提升了他作为保守派斗士的形象，但随着民主党准备几十年来首次在德克萨斯州重新掌权，这些诉讼现在正在逐渐结束。
据医生的律师称，该州对 May Lau 和 M. Brett Cooper 的诉讼于周五被驳回。他们是帕克斯顿在诉讼中称为“违法者”和“激进性别活动家”的三名医生之一，这些医生威胁要处以巨额罚款并吊销他们的医疗执照。
刘博士的律师妮可·勒博夫 (Nicole LeBoeuf) 在一份声明中表示，“刘博士没有做错任何事，但她很容易成为总检察长办公室的替罪羊，司法部长办公室就其案件发布了一篇又一篇新闻稿——该案现已失败。”
勒伯夫表示，帕克斯顿败诉后解雇的时机“证实了针对刘博士的案件从头到尾都是政治性的。”在诉讼期间，刘将她的医疗诊所从达拉斯搬到了俄勒冈州。
帕克斯顿办公室周一没有立即回复置评请求。
德克萨斯州是第一个对医生提起诉讼的州
唐纳德·特朗普总统的亲密盟友帕克斯顿去年撤销了对第三位医生赫克托·格拉纳多斯的另一起诉讼，他的办公室后来表示，埃尔帕索儿科内分泌学家没有违法。
德克萨斯州禁止为跨性别青少年提供性别肯定护理的禁令于 2023 年生效。虽然其他州也禁止为跨性别青少年提供性别肯定护理，但德克萨斯州是第一个对医生提起诉讼的州，对这三个提供者提起诉讼。
特朗普在第二任期内对跨性别者权利发起了广泛的指控，扭转了美国跨性别者多年来取得的法律和政策成果。即使在州法律允许提供护理的州，主要医院和医院系统也表示他们正在停止或限制护理。
库珀是达拉斯的一名医生，他的律师西蒙娜·阿格诺鲁奇和阿尼卡·霍兰德在一份声明中表示，他“一直坚称自己的行为合法，并且符合患者的最大利益”。
帕克斯顿和共和党人在中期选举期间倾向于攻击跨性别者
根据数据公司 AdImpact 向美联社提供的统计数据，在今年中期选举的最后阶段，共和党人在电视广告上花费了大约 1.83 亿美元，重点关注针对民主党人的跨性别相关攻击。据 AdImpact 称，帕克斯顿和民主党人詹姆斯·塔拉里科之间的得克萨斯州参议院竞选消耗了该支出的最大份额，在选举前播放了 50,000 多场节目，预计耗资 5,800 万美元。
共和党对跨性别问题的关注与选民告诉民意调查者他们在中期选举中最关心的问题形成鲜明对比，其中包括经济状况。
德克萨斯州也放弃了有关堕胎药和移民的诉讼
一月份，民主党人内森·约翰逊将成为德克萨斯州的下一任总检察长。
自帕克斯顿在参议院失利以来，帕克斯顿办公室撤销的其他诉讼包括针对州外医生向德克萨斯州运送堕胎药的诉讼，以及一项试图阻止美国伊斯兰关系委员会在该州运作的诉讼。针对美国最大的穆斯林民权和倡导团体之一的诉讼是在得克萨斯州州长、共和党人格雷格·阿博特宣布其为“外国恐怖组织”之后发生的。

title_en: Trump targets Newsom and Democrats in Justice Department speech focused on violent crime
title_zh: 特朗普在司法部针对暴力犯罪的演讲中针对纽瑟姆和民主党人
summary: President Donald Trump has condemned California Governor Gavin Newsom's decision to commute hundreds of death sentences
summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统谴责加州州长加文·纽瑟姆为数百名死刑减刑的决定
body_en: President Donald Trump has condemned California Governor Gavin Newsom's decision to commute hundreds of death sentences

WASHINGTON -- President Donald Trump condemned California Gov. Gavin Newsom’s decision to commute hundreds of death sentences in the state, using a Justice Department visit to sharply chastise an outspoken Democratic critic who is considering his own bid for the White House.

The speech offered the president a platform to showcase what he said was his administration's success in combating violent crime, a favored Trump topic he has repeatedly invoked to rally his Republican base. But the address, Trump's second at the department in less than two years , veered openly into partisan politics as the president lambasted both a governor with whom he has openly feuded and a Democratic Party he depicted as soft-on-crime and part of a “radical left.”

“For years now, we have watched the radical left commit one betrayal of justice and safety after another,” Trump said in a speech that was also interspersed with first-person accounts from relatives of victims of crimes affected by Newsom's clemency who criticized the commutations.

Newsom has said the announcement this month to commute the sentences of more than 500 inmates to punishments of life in prison without parole was among the most difficult choices of his career because it will surface painful memories for crime victims’ families. The state’s Supreme Court would be required to approve the majority of those commutations.

“I won’t take lectures on accountability from a president who has used the pardon power to help wealthy friends and business associates avoid accountability while victims are left fighting to recover what was stolen from them. Justice should be about the people we serve, not the political interests of the people in power,” Newsom said in a statement about Trump's speech.

Asked at an event Monday why he didn't take the death penalty reveal to the ballot, Newsom said he had the “constitutional right” to do what he did. He added: “I may be the first to have received the kind of response from the sitting president of the United States at the Department of Justice with the FBI director — talk about weaponization.”
The speech marked the latest tussle between Trump and Newsom.

In June, Newsom accused the Justice Department of launching a politically motivated investigation into him and his wife, which his office said was focused on “increasingly personal matters involving the governor’s family and professional network.” He has denied any wrongdoing. The president has repeatedly gone after the heavily Democratic California during his second term and the state has pushed back by suing the federal government dozens of times.

The president's address unfolded against the backdrop of sweeping Republican losses in this month’s midterm elections , which gave Democrats control of the House and Senate. The development tees up possible congressional inquiries into everything from the mass firings of federal agents and prosecutors by the Trump administration Justice Department to a series of politically charged investigations into Trump adversaries that have been rejected by grand juries and judges alike.

Trump was introduced by Attorney General Todd Blanche , his former personal defense lawyer who has been unapologetic in his view that the Justice Department as an executive branch agency is an extension of the White House and that the president is free to exert his will over the institution. He said Monday that the Justice Department in the Trump administration was seeking the death penalty whenever appropriate.

“I want to take just a moment and tell every law enforcement member watching or here in this room that we have your back, that President Trump has your back, and he will always have your back,” Blanche said.

Trump has long sought to position himself as a tough-on-crime president who staunchly backs law enforcement. He has taken credit for dropping violent crime rates that experts say have been declining since 2022.

"Our opponents seek an America that empowers the most violent and dangerous elements and celebrates deviancy and enables dysfunction and demands empathy for serial killers and criminals, while hardworking citizens are treated with hatred and scorn and contempt,” Trump said Monday. “In the Trump administration, we believe in the exact opposite.”

As with last year’s speech, Monday’s remarks were delivered inside the ceremonial Great Hall of the Justice Department headquarters, a building whose exterior in the last year was decorated with a massive banner of Trump’s face in a physical demonstration of the president’s sway over the agency.

Trump's March 2025 address was meant to rally support for his administration’s policies on violent crime, drugs and illegal immigration but became a forum for a litany of complaints about the criminal cases Trump faced during Democratic President Joe Biden’s administration — when prosecutors charged him with hoarding classified documents at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Palm Beach, Florida, and with conspiring to overturn his 2020 election loss to Biden — and to vow retribution for what he described as the “lies and abuses that have occurred within these walls.”
body_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统谴责加州州长加文·纽瑟姆为数百名死刑减刑的决定
华盛顿——唐纳德·特朗普总统谴责加州州长加文·纽瑟姆对该州数百名死刑犯减刑的决定，并利用司法部的访问严厉惩罚了一位正在考虑入主白宫的直言不讳的民主党批评者。
这次演讲为总统提供了一个平台，展示他所说的政府在打击暴力犯罪方面所取得的成功，这是特朗普最喜欢的话题，他曾多次援引这一话题来团结他的共和党基础。但特朗普在不到两年的时间里在该部门发表的第二次讲话，公开地转向了党派政治，总统痛斥了一位与他公开不和的州长，以及他将民主党描绘成对犯罪温和、属于“激进左翼”的民主党。
特朗普在一次演讲中表示，“多年来，我们看到激进左派一次又一次背叛正义和安全。”演讲中还穿插了受纽瑟姆宽大处理影响的犯罪受害者亲属的第一人称叙述，他们对减刑提出了批评。
纽瑟姆表示，本月宣布将 500 多名囚犯的刑期减为终身监禁且不得假释，这是他职业生涯中最困难的选择之一，因为这将给犯罪受害者家属带来痛苦的记忆。其中大部分减刑必须得到该州最高法院的批准。
纽瑟姆在一份有关特朗普演讲的声明中表示：“我不会听一位总统关于问责制的讲座，他利用赦免权帮助富有的朋友和商业伙伴逃避责任，而受害者却在为追回被盗的东西而奋斗。正义应该是关于我们所服务的人民​​，而不是当权者的政治利益。”
纽瑟姆在周一的一次活动中被问及为何不将死刑公布纳入投票时表示，他有“宪法权利”去做他所做的事情。他补充道：“我可能是第一个收到美国司法部现任总统与联邦调查局局长的此类回应的人——谈论武器化。”
这次演讲标志着特朗普和纽瑟姆之间的最新争执。
今年六月，纽瑟姆指责司法部对他和他的妻子发起了出于政治动机的调查，他的办公室表示，调查的重点是“越来越多涉及州长家庭和专业网络的个人事务”。他否认有任何不当行为。总统在第二个任期内多次针对民主党占主导地位的加州，而该州则多次起诉联邦政府进行反击。
总统的讲话是在共和党在本月中期选举中惨败的背景下发表的，这次中期选举让民主党控制了参众两院。这一事态发展为国会可能对一切问题进行调查，从特朗普政府司法部大规模解雇联邦特工和检察官，到对特朗普对手进行的一系列政治调查，但这些调查均被大陪审团和法官拒绝。
特朗普是由他的前私人辩护律师、司法部长托德·布兰奇(Todd Blanche)介绍的。布兰奇一直毫无歉意地认为，司法部作为行政部门是白宫的延伸，总统可以自由地对该机构行使自己的意愿。他周一表示，特朗普政府司法部正在寻求在适当的时候判处死刑。
布兰奇说：“我想花一点时间告诉每一位正在观看或在座的执法人员，我们支持你，特朗普总统支持你，他将永远支持你。”
2020 年去世的宾夕法尼亚州青少年可能成为第一位 Z 世代圣人
华盛顿州官员谴责 ICE 两名乘客在西雅图机场登机时被捕
